# Contexto completo para continuar el trabajo en Antigravity

Generado el 2026-11-14 en la máquina Darwin con `tools/exportar_contexto.py`, a partir de todo lo trabajado con Claude Code: instrucciones, memoria, estilos, estado de piezas, el historial completo de mensajes del usuario, herramientas y git. Solo incluye texto: los videos, audios y modelos 3D están en el repo y en los discos.

## 0. Léeme primero (instrucciones para el agente de Antigravity)

**Quién es el usuario.** Alan Leiva. Hace videos (shorts 9:16 de TikTok/Reels/Shorts y largos 16:9 de YouTube) en muchos estilos y canales, casi todo animado por código (three.js, HyperFrames, Blender por MCP, Python + ffmpeg) o generado con Google Flow (Nano Banana / Veo / Omni Flash). Habla español; los guiones pueden ser en inglés o español según el canal. Trabaja con un PC Windows (repo en `F:\Claude Proyectos`) y una Mac; las dos comparten el repo git `https://github.com/alanleivago/claude-proyectos.git`.

**Cómo quiere que trabajes** (detalle en la PARTE 1 y la PARTE 2):
- Respuestas cortas, en español, sin halagos ni preámbulos. No narrar el plan: hacerlo.
- Leer el contexto (spec del estilo, memoria, pieza aprobada de referencia) ANTES de programar. Si falta información, preguntar.
- Cambios mínimos; no reescribir archivos enteros; nada de features que no pidió.
- Verificar antes de decir "listo": renderizar, mirar fotogramas, medir el audio.
- Si dice "hazlo así", hacerlo así.
- Cada estilo tiene un **nivel aprobado** (una pieza concreta) que es la barra mínima y la plantilla a copiar. Las correcciones que dio en cada estilo son reglas permanentes: revisarlas en cada plano antes del render final.
- Mostrar el storyboard y esperar su OK antes del render final, aunque diga "procede al render" (salvo los estilos marcados "sin storyboard").
- Render final → copiar a LucidLink `C:\Volumes\alanwork\trabajo\Renders finales claude\<Estilo>\<titulo-corto>.mp4` (+ `caption.txt` al lado si existe). Sin duplicados en otras carpetas. Videos largos: entregar también título + miniatura 1280x720.
- Confirmar antes de cualquier publicación (TikTok, Facebook, Gumroad, Zernio).
- Entregar cada archivo con su ruta como link.

**Orden de prioridad cuando algo choque:** mensaje actual del usuario > PARTE 5 más reciente > memoria (PARTE 2) > specs de estilo (PARTE 3) > reglas generales (PARTE 1).

**Cómo usar este archivo:**
1. Copiar la PARTE 1 (y lo esencial de la sección 0) a las reglas globales / del workspace de Antigravity, para que se carguen siempre.
2. Copiar la PARTE 2 (memoria) como reglas o como un archivo de conocimiento del workspace; es lo más importante: gustos, correcciones y el nivel aprobado de cada estilo.
3. Cuando el usuario pida un video de un estilo: leer su memoria (PARTE 2), su spec (PARTE 3) y la pieza aprobada en `pieces/`, y buscar en la PARTE 5 lo que dijo de ese estilo.
4. Reconfigurar los MCP de la PARTE 6 en la config de MCP de Antigravity (mismos comandos/URLs). Las claves no van en este archivo: están en `.env` (raíz del repo), `~/.freesound.json`, etc., en cada máquina.
5. Las "skills" de Claude Code son carpetas con un `SKILL.md` de instrucciones (rutas en la PARTE 6); en Antigravity se pueden usar como workflows/reglas leyendo ese archivo.

**Herramientas clave** (detalle en la memoria): srz-google-flow-mcp para TODO lo de Flow (nunca flow-auto ni Flow Connector), VoiceStudio local para voces clonadas (REST/MCP, steps=32, wav), earshot para juzgar sonido, sound-layer / real-sfx / Freesound / Openverse para SFX reales, humanizer para pasar los guiones, `tools/revisar_render.py` para revisar renders con la API de Anthropic (créditos de API de su plan; clave en `.env`), Blender MCP, Premiere MCP, FilmCraft, Zernio (publicar), VMOS (teléfonos en la nube), LucidLink.

**Datos de la Mac:** la Mac comparte el repo por git (todo lo commiteado está igual en las dos). Sus sesiones de Claude Code están en su propio `~/.claude`. Para sumar su historial y memoria, correr en la Mac `python3 tools/exportar_contexto.py MIGRACION_MAC.md` y dar también ese archivo.

## Índice

- PARTE 1 — Instrucciones permanentes (CLAUDE.md)
- PARTE 2 — Memoria completa (gustos, correcciones, reglas por estilo, recursos)
- PARTE 3 — Estilos de video (specs)
- PARTE 4 — Piezas (proyectos de video) y su estado
- PARTE 5 — Historial completo de instrucciones del usuario (todas las sesiones)

- PARTE 7 — Repositorio git

# Reglas para Claude Code — Ahorra Tokens

## 1. No programar sin contexto
- ANTES de escribir codigo: lee los archivos relevantes, revisa git log, entiende la arquitectura.
- Si no tienes contexto suficiente, pregunta. No asumas.

## 2. Respuestas cortas
- Responde en 1-3 oraciones. Sin preambulos, sin resumen final.
- No repitas lo que el usuario dijo. No expliques lo obvio.
- Codigo habla por si mismo: no narres cada linea que escribes.

## 3. No reescribir archivos completos
- Usa Edit (reemplazo parcial), NUNCA Write para archivos existentes salvo que el cambio sea >80% del archivo.
- Cambia solo lo necesario. No "limpies" codigo alrededor del cambio.

## 4. No releer archivos ya leidos
- Si ya leiste un archivo en esta conversacion, no lo vuelvas a leer salvo que haya cambiado.
- Toma notas mentales de lo importante en tu primera lectura.

## 5. Validar antes de declarar hecho
- Despues de un cambio: compila, corre tests, o verifica que funciona.
- Nunca digas "listo" sin evidencia de que funciona.

## 6. Cero charla aduladora
- No digas "Excelente pregunta", "Gran idea", "Perfecto", etc.
- No halagues al usuario. Ve directo al trabajo.

## 7. Soluciones simples
- Implementa lo minimo que resuelve el problema. Nada mas.
- No agregues abstracciones, helpers, tipos, validaciones, ni features que no se pidieron.
- 3 lineas repetidas > 1 abstraccion prematura.

## 8. No pelear con el usuario
- Si el usuario dice "hazlo asi", hazlo asi. No debatas salvo riesgo real de seguridad o perdida de datos.
- Si discrepas, menciona tu concern en 1 oracion y procede con lo que pidio.

## 9. Leer solo lo necesario
- No leas archivos completos si solo necesitas una seccion. Usa offset y limit.
- Si sabes la ruta exacta, usa Read directo. No hagas Glob + Grep + Read cuando Read basta.

## 10. No narrar el plan antes de ejecutar
- No digas "Voy a leer el archivo, luego modificar la funcion, luego compilar...". Solo hazlo.
- El usuario ve tus tool calls. No necesita un preview en texto.

## 11. Paralelizar tool calls
- Si necesitas leer 3 archivos independientes, lee los 3 en un solo mensaje, no uno por uno.
- Menos roundtrips = menos tokens de contexto acumulado.

## 12. No duplicar codigo en la respuesta
- Si ya editaste un archivo, no copies el resultado en tu respuesta. El usuario lo ve en el diff.
- Si creaste un archivo, no lo muestres entero en texto tambien.

## 13. No usar Agent cuando Grep/Read basta
- Agent duplica todo el contexto en un subproceso. Solo usalo para busquedas amplias o tareas complejas.
- Para buscar una funcion o archivo especifico, usa Grep o Glob directo.

## BASE CLI — Proactive Context Engine

The `base` binary is on PATH. Use these commands proactively during sessions — they write to a knowledge graph that persists across sessions and surfaces context automatically.

### When to call (proactive, not on-demand)

| Trigger | Command |
|---------|---------|
| Navigate code: find functions, callers, imports | `base ast query --contains "name"` or `--file`, `--calls`, `--imports` (add `--target apps/X` to query another app's map) |
| Discover which apps have a code map | `base ast list` |
| A decision is made (architectural, process, tooling) | `base decision log --domain X --decision "..." --rationale "..."` |
| An insight, correction, or lesson emerges | `base learn --text "..." --domain X --type insight\|correction\|decision` |
| User defines or refines a behavioral rule | `base rule add --domain X --text "..." --keywords "a, b" --fires-on "<the user's prompt>"` |
| Before making assumptions about prior context | `base recall --keyword "..."` or `base recall --domain X` |
| User asks to scaffold a new workspace | `base scaffold [path]` |

### Code navigation — MANDATORY FIRST TOOL

**ALWAYS use `base ast query` BEFORE grep, find, Read, or any MCP tool for code exploration.**
The AST graph already knows every function, struct, class, import, and call relationship. Scanning files without checking the graph first is wasteful — the graph gives you the map, then you Read only what matters.

- `base ast query --contains "auth"` (or `base a q -c "auth"`) — find entities by name
- `base ast query --file "main.rs"` (or `base a q -f "main.rs"`) — list entities in a file
- `base ast query --calls "validate"` — find all callers of a function
- `base ast query --imports "config.rs"` (or `base a q -i "config.rs"`) — find importers
- `base ast query --target apps/X -c "auth"` — query a specific app's map from anywhere (e.g. the parent workspace), no `cd` needed
- `base ast list` — see which apps have a code map, with entity counts + paths

Each app keeps its own self-contained map at `<app>/.base-ast/ast.ttl`, registered in the workspace graph and kept current automatically (a Stop hook refreshes the cwd app's map after each turn). Map a new app once with `base sync --ast --target apps/X`; thereafter it stays live.

**Order of operations:** `base ast query` first → understand structure → `Read` specific lines only. Never scan-then-understand when you can understand-then-read.

### GraphRAG — ask questions across a doc corpus

- `base graph extract --target docs/` — LLM pass over markdown → concepts + relationship edges in the graph (no API key, content-cached, ~25s/doc)
- `base graph query "<question>"` — retrieve the relevant subgraph and synthesize a **cited** answer in one command
- `base graph query "<q>" --raw` — return just the retrieved subgraph for the current session to reason over (highest-quality path)
- `base graph analyze` — emergent structure: god nodes (core abstractions), communities, surprising cross-community bridges

**Agentic retrieval** (read-only primitives — drive your own multi-call traversal instead of one-shot query):
- `base graph get-node "<label|slug>"` — one node's type, source, summary, and edges
- `base graph neighbors "<node>" -d N` — the N-hop neighborhood as edge lines
- `base graph path "<from>" "<to>"` — shortest path between two concepts

**Multimodal ingest is OFF by default** (markdown-only, zero extra deps). PDF/image/audio/video need it on:
- `base config set multimodal.enabled true` (or one-shot `base graph extract --multimodal`)
- **No sudo, ever.** PDF → in-process (`pdf-extract` crate, zero dep); image → Claude vision (uses the present `claude`, zero dep); audio/video → Whisper, whose `whisper`+`ffmpeg` install **once** via `pip install --user` (marker-gated), never again. An operator who never enables it — or only feeds docs/images — installs nothing.

### Project management

- `base project add --name "..." --path "src/x"` (or `base p a -n "..." -p "src/x"`) — register a project
- `base project list` (or `base p l`) — list projects
- `base milestone add --project X --name "..."` (or `base m a -p X -n "..."`) — add a milestone
- `base task add --project X --name "..."` (or `base t a -p X -n "..."`) — add a task
- `base task done <slug>` — mark complete

### Deferred work

Deferred means open but paused: a handoff, fork, task or milestone nobody has touched inside its window. Session start does not list it, and every block ends with its count and the command that lists it. Nothing deferred is lost.

Bring one back with `base handoff show <what the user said>` (forks: `base fork show`), which revives a deferred match and prints its doc. A task or milestone the pass deferred comes back at the next session start once a base command has touched it; any deferred task or milestone comes back with `base task update <slug> --status active` or `base milestone update <slug> --status active`. List them with `base handoff deferred`, `base fork deferred`, `base task deferred`, `base milestone deferred` and `base project deferred`.

Config: `[defer] enabled` (off unless set), `mode` (`"asset"` or `"global"`), `global_days` (10 when unset), and one `[defer.days]` key per type: `handoff`, `fork`, `task`, `milestone`, `project`. A project with no key reads `[protocol] stale_days`. Preview the pass with `base reconcile --dry-run`.

### Knowledge & memory

- `base learn --text "..." --domain X --type insight` — structured memory with relational edges
- `base recall --keyword "..." [--domain X]` — graph-backed relational search
- `base decision log --domain X --decision "..." --rationale "..."` — log a decision
- `base decision search --keyword "..."` — find prior decisions
- `base rule add --domain X --text "..." --keywords "a, b" --fires-on "<prompt>"` — add a rule to a domain; inside a session it needs the words from the prompt that should bring it back and that prompt as its first test (a rule for file work also takes `--path`)

### Sync & dashboard

- `base sync` — extract markdown metadata + body into graph
- `base sync --ast` — extract code structure (tree-sitter, 35+ languages)
- `base dashboard` (or `base dash`) — launch Command Center web dashboard

### What happens automatically (via hooks)

- **Session start:** Graph syncs domains, ingests paul.toml projects, runs signals
- **User prompt:** Matches keywords → injects domain rules + decisions + notes from graph
- **Pre-tool-use:** Matches file paths → injects AST file map + domain rules. Intercepts grep with graph hint. Injects markdown extraction contract on Write/Edit of .md files.
- **Post-tool-use:** Updates timestamps. Injects section-specific AST context for partial reads.

### Architecture

- Rules, decisions, notes, and projects are graph entities with relational edges
- `domains.toml` defines triggers only (keywords, paths) — rule content lives in the graph
- `~/.base-gbl/` = global tier, `{workspace}/.base/` = workspace tier
- Built by Chris Kahler · https://docs.basemode.ai

## `CLAUDE.md`

# Claude Proyectos

## Créditos de API ($200/mes del plan Max)

El plan Max 20x trae USD 200 al mes de créditos de la API de Claude (no se acumulan). Cubren la API y el Agent SDK, no Claude Code.

- **Regla:** toda tarea que pueda correr por la API (ver/analizar videos y fotogramas, revisar renders, guiones en lote, títulos/SEO) se hace con un script Python + SDK `anthropic`, antes que gastar tokens del plan. El script escribe un reporte `.md` corto y Claude Code lee solo el resultado. Si los créditos se acaban (error de saldo), avisar y recién ahí hacerlo en la sesión.
- **Clave:** `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` en el `.env` de la raíz (git-ignorado, cada máquina tiene el suyo). Nunca como variable de entorno del sistema: Claude Code la usaría en vez del plan. Vence a los 30 días; se renueva en platform.claude.com → Claves y acceso.
- **Llamadas:** usar `client.messages.stream(...)` con `max_tokens` ≥ 16000 (Sonnet 5.5 piensa antes de responder) y quedarse solo con los bloques `type == "text"`.

Herramientas que ya usan los créditos:
- `ver-youtube` (skill): yt-dlp + Whisper local + fotogramas → notas en `fuentes/<tema>/`.
- `python tools/revisar_render.py --estilo <estilo> video.mp4` → `<video>_revision.md` con veredicto y fallos por regla. Correrlo antes de mostrar un render al usuario.

## Entrega de renders finales (todas las sesiones, todos los estilos — desde 2026-11-13)

- Cada video terminado se entrega en `/Volumes/alanwork/trabajo/Renders finales claude/<carpeta del canal>/`, con el título como nombre de archivo. Carpetas: Agente davis, Ali Abdaal, Alterbase, Amphorus, Ava Restfield, Cartoon3d, Doggo poly shorts, Edicion de videos Reels, Kodama yokai, Madfable, Majestic, Mechayuki, MexiTV, Punk poly shorts, Roblox, Stimulus, Tuneles, Vista. **cartoon3d ("3D cartoon") → Alterbase.** Si no está claro qué carpeta, preguntar una vez.
- Se envía la versión **share** (como `export.mjs --share`: libx264 CRF 24 preset slow, yuv420p, AAC 192k, +faststart), no el master.
- Después de entregar, borrar las versiones anteriores en `pieces/<pieza>/renders/` (silent vN, raw, duplicados final.mp4/<pieza>.mp4); queda solo el master con el título.
- La miniatura va en `<carpeta del canal>/Miniaturas/`, con el mismo nombre (título) en .png.
- Esa carpeta (`/Volumes/alanwork/...` en la Mac; el mismo disco está activo en la PC) es el canal para pasar archivos entre la PC y la Mac: renders, miniaturas y cualquier archivo pesado que no va a git.

## memoria: `feedback-animation-richness.md`

---
name: feedback-animation-richness
description: "In every /animate video, push animation and depth beyond the reference (camera float, parallax, progressive route draws, shadows, detail)"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 67243e87-5375-4dcf-bdf1-c1dc76908cd9
  modified: 2026-10-12T05:26:02.115Z
---

Always improve the animations in every video we make — match the reference or go beyond it. Concretely asked for on hackeo-1834 (pixdoc style, 2026-10-12): depth of field / layered parallax in landscapes, a gently floating camera at the opening, maps complete edge to edge (no straight cut edges), routes that draw on progressively with a travelling head, cast shadows and set detail (e.g. courtroom).

**Why:** the user judges pieces against strong references; flat, static or under-detailed panels get sent back.
**How to apply:** before showing any board or frame, add camera life (float, push-in, parallax), animated reveals for lines/paths, shadows and 3+ details of life per shot. Related: [[project-pixdoc-style]].

Use the Google Flow MCP (`flow_new_project`, `flow_upload_file`, `flow_generate_image` with `@{name}` references) for every Nano Banana image. Do not use the `flow-auto` CLI / flow-generate skill any more (user, 2026-10-20). Generate one image per call so Flow is not saturated.

**Why:** flow-auto's reference upload broke ("could not find Flow's attachButton") and it mispaired batch downloads; the user told me to drop it.
**How to apply:** upload the refs from the `Ref …` folder first, name them by role, then prompt with `@{name}`; for layers to animate, ask for the subject on flat pure magenta (#FF00FF) and key it with vox-doc `key.py` (keeps orange incised lines). Proven on pieces/troya-bf ([[project-amphora-style]]).

## memoria: `feedback-ifverse-sfx.md`

---
name: feedback-ifverse-sfx
description: ifverse — SFX on EVERY action/gesture/graphic/cut with presence (≈ voice level); per-shot SFX registry, then stem remix
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

User (2026-10-24, ten-seconds): first mix had almost no audible SFX; then asked for "muchos más sfx a más cosas en general" (e.g. Nia's elbow hitting the carton) — the reference puts a sound on everything.

Method that answered it: head.html `SFX(t, kind, v, pan, dur)` registry called at registration time next to each SHOT (never in draw); score.js `SFX_KINDS` (39 synthesized kinds) plays them, same kind within 50 ms plays once; 8 agents (one per section) placed ~1,500 cues (~175/min incl. steps/ticks). Check with dev/sfxcount.mjs. Keep the deliberate silences empty. After export: stem remix — voice; music −10 dB sidechain-ducked; sfx +2 dB lightly ducked (ratio 2); loudnorm −14 LUFS TP −1.5; alimiter 0.84 → sfx moments ≈ voice level.

Update 2026-10-24 (2nd round): the dense version was too loud and too busy, the "ding" annoying. Final balance: per-kind gaps + one sound per 0.35 s (v≥1.3 exempt) → ~70/min; ding/coin = low soft marimba, ≤1 per 12 s; no bright chimes; SFX ≈ −6 dB under the voice. Music must have rhythm (groove 100–120 BPM, dynamic per section, like the ref). No film grain on ifverse.

**Why:** the user wants SFX density and presence like @IfverseTales.
**How to apply:** every ifverse piece: plan SFX per shot from the start (section agents add them), and always remix stems so SFX sit at voice level. Related: [[project-ifverse-style]].

## memoria: `feedback-tapestry-rules.md`

---
name: feedback-tapestry-rules
description: Every instruction the user gave for HotD/GoT tapestry videos (Rhaenyra, 2026-10-20/21) — apply all of them to every future piece made with the Flow method
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Checklist for every House of the Dragon / Game of Thrones video (tapestry + Flow method, [[project-tapestry-style]]):

**Process**
- Script in English, ~1100 characters (~60s), opens with the protagonist's first name only, ends on a tragic or epic line; hand over the plain script; the user generates one take into `Ref amphora mitologia/Voces/` and says when; cut it at word gaps ([[project-mitos-guiones]]).
- Always show the look, then the full storyboard, and wait for approval before every export, revisions included ([[feedback-storyboard-before-render]]).
- Music: the theme the user drops in Ref (Rhaenyra Targaryen Theme always from 0:30), with strong presence (music gain +10, voice.music −1); SFX sit under it; a 0.5s dip before the payoff.

**Look**
- Linen background from v1 (visible, slightly imperfect weave) + v2 sewn borders top and bottom, close to the edges; no figure ever touches the border lines.
- Figures and dragons as close to the reference tapestry as possible (naive Bayeux, coarse stitches, detailed stitched hair, never flat); dragons with stitched texture.
- Men never have red lips.
- Figures are always fully opaque, never transparent.
- Keep secondary figures large (small bearded figures look wrong) and never leave a scene empty: bring in the main character (e.g. Viserys with the kneeling lords).
- Captions stitched (Herculanum, alternating red/navy, side words in their colour), at the top of the panel but lowered toward the figures wherever the picture leaves space.
- End card: the apple and AMPHORUS (gold capitals with a moving shine, no stitch dots) together, centred in the frame.
- The whole frame wiggles (as the other styles).

**Motion**
- Scene changes are always a slide to the right, never a cut.
- Make it as dynamic as possible: extra poses come from editing the character's own image in Flow (an arm, a head, a sword) and swap seamlessly (posepair.py: only the changed part fades).
- Anything that moves on its own (a falling crown, fire, a sword) is its own Flow sprite, the same one from start to end — the falling crown is the one she ends up wearing.
- Nothing ever appears or changes abruptly: characters walk in from the sides (bob + rock), things fall in from above, grow, or arrive with the slide; growth/pose changes are gradual.
- Fire has natural flame edges, never square cuts (it must not touch an image or panel edge).

**Why:** the user's corrections across the Rhaenyra code and Flow versions. **How to apply:** go through this list before showing a look, a storyboard, or a final.
- Slides must never cut elements at the seam (clouds, sea, dragons): only a vertical clip, both cloths drawn first (user, 2026-10-22).
- Wide elements (sea, cloud banks, flame rows) must be generated with finished, natural ends inside the image (rounded cloud puffs, waves that taper), never cut by the image edge; place every element whole inside its panel or overhanging whole.

## memoria: `feedback-voltamps-voice-script.md`

---
name: feedback-voltamps-voice-script
description: voltamps (Ref volt y amps) pieces — plain EN script only; one voice take cut at word gaps; Ref documentary track as music; strong code SFX
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 7c471d3f-6c90-4407-9a76-9911d880ee64
  modified: 2026-10-14T04:47:35.316Z
---

For voltamps / Bitvolts pieces (from `Ref volt y amps/`):
- **Since 2026-10-23 (video 9): Claude generates the voice itself in VoiceStudio** (local API :3900, `POST /generate` multipart: text, profile_id, language=en, seed, speed) with the profile **"mathomaly" (id e4eb9da7)**, 2 seeds per line, picking the take whose whisper transcript matches best — `references/voltamps/tools/vs_gen.py <piece> e4eb9da7 1,2 1.0`. No more waiting for the user's take; still show the script. Same BGM (Ref documentary track).
- When giving the voice script, the message/block is ONLY the script text — no ids, no table, no commentary — so the user can copy-paste it straight into the voice generator. Hand it over right after drafting the story; the user generates while Claude builds style frames.
- The user generates the voice as ONE single take and drops it in `Ref volt y amps/Voces/`. Claude cuts it into lines itself and times the picture to it. Cuts must fall in the silence between words (never mid-word) — use faster-whisper word times and cut at the gap midpoint / lowest energy.
- Music: no composed background music. Use the track in `Ref volt y amps/` ("Documentary Background Music for Videos.mp3") at a good level under the voice (piece.json "music"); the code score is SFX only (to='s') and the SFX must have strong presence.
- Master louder than the skill's −14 LUFS: after export, +4.5 dB into `alimiter=limit=0.74:level=false` (without level=false ffmpeg auto-levels to ≈ −9 LUFS, peak > 0), remuxed from renders/audio.wav (≈ −11.5 LUFS, true peak ≈ −1.3 dBFS) and remux into final/share (user: "sube el volumen master", LED piece). Always measure the remuxed share.mp4 (ebur128 peak): if the true peak is above −1 dBFS, redo with `volume=4.2dB,alimiter=limit=0.68:attack=1` (≈ −12 LUFS); if still above (sharp SFX, cargar), `limit=0.6` (≈ −12 LUFS, −1.4 dBFS). Transcribe/cut helpers live in `references/voltamps/tools/` (tr.py, cut.py); zero-gap words need an energy-profile check.
- No constant noise/hiss beds in the SFX: they pump audibly in every voice pause (rayos).
- Look: push past the reference — more glow, texture, depth and animation than the ref.

**Why:** user's instructions on 2026-10-14 (first piece: rayos / "Why does lightning seek the ground?").
**How to apply:** script = condensed EN paraphrase of the Spanish reference (keep every explanation step), >60s, title card at the very start. Related: [[feedback-pov3d-language]], [[feedback-animation-richness]].

amphora style, started 2026-10-18 with the Alcibiades piece (remake of ref video 8).
- Look: mainly ref video 8 (parchment, pencil-hatched figures, crosshatch vignette, coloured keywords: Athens blue, Sparta red, Persia gold) + Greek meander friezes top and bottom like ref video 5; refs 6 and 7 for more of the look.

- Voice: Claude gives a plain script and the user generates one take into `Ref amphora mitologia/Voces/` (voltamps workflow, [[feedback-voltamps-voice-script]]).
- Music: `Ref amphora mitologia/Odysseus bgm.mp3`, with strong presence: the file is very quiet (−29.6 LUFS), so loudnorm it to −14 into audio/track.wav, music gain +7, voice.music −4; sfx sit under the music (user, Alcibiades piece). The score tail normalises sfx, so balance via music gain, not sfxBus.
- Sign-off: "Amphorus" in the gold Roman-capitals look of the ARQA logo at the end of ref video 8.

**Why:** user's instructions at intake. **How to apply:** every amphora piece; see [[feedback-animation-richness]].

Two styles for this niche (user, 2026-10-19): **beige** = `styles/amphora` (pieces/alcibiades) and **orange** = `styles/amphora-bf` (black-figure puppets from refs 3–5, fondo.jpeg as asset, ITC Garamond italic white captions; pieces/alcibiades-bf). Both use the same voice/bgm/SFX workflow; keep improving both.

**amphora-bf with Flow layers (pieces/troya-bf, remake of ref video 5, 2026-10-20):** figures and sets are Nano Banana 2 layers (Flow MCP, `@{odysseus}` as style ref, magenta keyed) animated in code, instead of code-drawn puppets; the user liked it ("muchísimo mejor"). Captions: ITC Garamond Std italic (user's pick over 1689 GLC); end banner = `Ref amphora mitologia/ribbon.jpeg` (green-keyed) unrolling from the centre, not a parchment scroll.
Later on troya-bf the user switched captions to **Ludovico W03 Woodcut** (use the PostScript name "LudovicoW03-Woodcut" in canvas — the family name silently falls back), letter-spaced, shadowed, **written by hand** word by word; scenes **slide right** with no cuts (like rhaenyra); ribbon text "The Odyssey"; SFX a bit lower (music gain 10).
**Orange style is now v2 by default (user, 2026-10-20: "actualiza el estilo para que siempre sea así"):** styles/amphora-bf/STYLE.md + kit (bfLay, bfStripStage, bfCam, bfCaptions/bfPen, bfRibbon, bfSignoff) + styles/amphora-bf/assets (fondo, ribbon, apple). New orange pieces start by copying pieces/troya-bf.
- amphora-bf with Flow (Kratos, 2026-10-23, user): the core of this style is SIMPLE figures — solid black silhouettes with only a few thin orange incised lines, little detail; every figure black (no coloured/red-filled bodies); game characters adapted from their game renders (Ares, Odin, Thor) but simplified; figures that talk face each other; captions in Dalek Pinpoint Bold, brown like the "kratos 1" ref lettering.
- Before handing over any amphora-bf/tapestry video (user, 2026-10-23): run `node styles/amphora-bf/tools/capcheck.mjs <piece> '#6e2a18'` (every frame: no caption word over the top frieze or past x 945); captions are phrases of ≤7 words, ≤2 lines, each complete before the next, the last one sliding out with the cloth; fight SFX must be clearly audible (music gain 0 with the God of War track; SFX strikes ~5 dB over the music).

## memoria: `project-bitvolts-real-style.md`

---
name: project-bitvolts-real-style
description: "From video 9 on, Bitvolts videos use a NEW look copied from \"Ref volt y amps/ref 1–4.mp4\": cinematic 2.5D rendered objects + karaoke captions with a blue selection box"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 7c471d3f-6c90-4407-9a76-9911d880ee64
  modified: 2026-10-23T18:00:04.600Z
---

On 2026-10-23 the user switched the Bitvolts (voltamps workflow) look: "ahora será exactamente como los videos ref 1, ref 2, ref 3 y ref 4 … replica el estilo visual, subtítulos y todo". First piece in it: video 9 (charging the phone overnight).

The look (measured from the refs, 720×1280 @30fps):
- Dark charcoal / warm-brown grounds (#070707, #1c1c1c, #140b06), soft vignette, bokeh specks, depth-of-field blur on far layers.
- Semi-realistic 2.5D objects with gradients, soft shadows and highlights (card reader, phone, keyboard keys, cups), cartoon hands/thumbs (skin #e5b4a8 / #c58768 / #b57759, pink nails).
- Warm amber/gold glowing lines for fields and current (#f5b74a-ish), occasional red accents.
- Captions: word-by-word karaoke, top-centre (~19% from the top), modern geometric sans, ~60px at 1080. Spoken words appear one at a time; the current word is white semibold, earlier words fade to grey (#8a8a8a) regular; a keyword gets a blue text-selection box (navy fill, #3b82f6 outline, small round handles at two corners).
- In-scene labels: small mono or serif tags; big numbers in sans/mono with glow.

**Feedback after video 9 (2026-10-23):** next pieces must be more 2D-3D like ref 1, 2 and 3, with dynamic camera moves and seamless transitions. What the refs do (sampled in references/voltamps/new/motion.png):
- One continuous camera, almost no hard cuts: dolly out from a close-up (the reader's screen) to the whole object, crane/tilt as a new object (the card, a hand) enters from the frame edge, push-ins that end inside an object.
- Objects in real perspective (3/4 from above, tilted planes, parallax between near/far layers, DOF blur on the far ones), not flat front views.
- Transitions are motivated: the next scene slides in from below while the camera tracks down (newspaper rising under the hand), a zoom rushes through particles/sky into the next era, a match on shape (same object carries over).
- Motion is continuous and eased (springs), counters and fields animate while the camera keeps moving.

**Why:** explicit user instruction; supersedes the old voltamps line-art look and the "Georgia serif for titles / grid background" rule for these pieces (the workflow rules — plain EN script, one voice take cut at word gaps, Ref documentary music, strong SFX, louder master, storyboard before render, Bitvolts sign-off — still apply).
**How to apply:** build each new Bitvolts piece in this look; check captions and depth against the refs before the board. Related: [[feedback-voltamps-voice-script]], [[feedback-voltamps-text]], [[feedback-storyboard-before-render]].

## memoria: `project-ifverse-style.md`

name: project-ifverse-style

metadata:

  modified: 2026-10-24T02:06:09.406Z
---

Started 2026-10-23: replicate @IfverseTales "What If…?" videos. User rules: **English, 16:9 long-form for YouTube, never under 8:00** (aim ~8:20), **everything in code (no Flow)**. Narrator = VoiceStudio profile **mathomaly** (e4eb9da7, speed 0.9); each character gets a VoiceStudio profile cloned from a voice-designed sample (`instruct` e.g. "male, teenager, high pitch, american accent"; one-off characters use instruct + fixed seed).

Files: analysis + guide spec styles/ifverse/ANALISIS.md; kit styles/ifverse/kit.js (ivStage depth/DOF, ivMan rig, ivGhost, ivCounter…); tools styles/ifverse/tools/md2json.py + vs_cast_gen.py; first piece pieces/ten-seconds (BRIEF.md, SECTIONS.md, SETS_API.md, PROPS_API.md, src/sets.js, src/props.js reusable). Refs in "Ref ifverse/".

Workflow that worked: script.md with [Name] lines and [beat Ns] → voice (pauses SENT 0.85 / PARA 1.25 / CHAR 0.7, beats +1 s → ~1.7 words/s like the original) → look frames → set + prop agents → 8 section agents in parallel (dev/<sec> builds) → full board → fixes → code score → export.

**Why:** user wants a new channel style copied in look, animation and narration.
**How to apply:** reuse sets/props/kit for the next ifverse video; follow [[feedback-storyboard-before-render]]. Gotchas: plain `python3` is Homebrew 3.15 without faster-whisper — use /usr/bin/python3 and run voice.mjs with PATH=/usr/bin:$PATH; VoiceStudio fails on one-word lines ("Theo?") → generate in a sentence and cut.

## memoria: `project-mitos-guiones.md`

---
name: project-mitos-guiones
description: Myth/fantasy narration series — 7 English scripts (~1100 chars, ~60s), visual style per theme, and the voice workflow
metadata:
  type: project
---

Series of ~60s narrated videos, English voice, scripts in `scripts/guiones.md` (project root). Topics: Odysseus (Polyphemus), Kratos (Greek + Norse God of War), Rhaenyra (House of the Dragon), Ned (Game of Thrones), Baldr, Prometheus, Harry Potter.

- Script pattern (from refs 2–5): open with the protagonist's first name, rising costs in short sentences, a "But"/"So" turn, close on a tragic or epic line. Use first names only in most scripts (the user: the audience recognises them).
- Visual style per theme (user, 2026-10-20): House of the Dragon and Game of Thrones → **Tapestry** (`styles/tapestry`, built on pieces/rhaenyra; slides right between scenes; men without red lips; music = the theme the user drops in Ref); God of War Greek era → amphora-bf as in pieces/kratos (see project-gow-greek-style); Harry Potter → undecided between the "Three Brothers" tale and the Marauder's Map look.
- The God of War Egypt saga was a mistake: the user means the Greek and Norse sagas.
- Voice workflow: Claude gives the plain script only; the user generates the voice; the user announces the file; then Claude builds the video.
- Facts checked: Egypt is a rumour only (PushSquare, 2026); Lucerys' death closes season 1 of HotD; Ned's execution is at Baelor, King's Landing, not Winterfell; Baldr and Harry details per the sources in the session.

**Why:** the user's brief for a series of varied myths and fantasy franchises. **How to apply:** keep ~1100 chars per script; reuse the amphora workflow when a script goes to a video.
- Rhaenyra Targaryen Theme (Ref amphora mitologia) always starts at 0:30; HotD mix: music gain +10, voice.music −1 (user, 2026-10-20).

## memoria: `project-tapestry-style.md`

---
name: project-tapestry-style
description: tapestry style = the approved look for every House of the Dragon and Game of Thrones video (pieces/rhaenyra is the reference)
metadata:
  type: project
---

Every House of the Dragon / Game of Thrones video uses `styles/tapestry` **with the Flow method** (approved 2026-10-21): Nano Banana layers via the Flow MCP, animated in code. Start from `pieces/rhaenyra-flow` (scenes, assets/bg.jpg, score, piece.json); the full method is in styles/tapestry/STYLE.md → The Flow method. `pieces/rhaenyra` (all drawn in code) is the older variant.
- Look: embroidered linen with an imperfect weave; borders top (y 58–268) and bottom (y 1652–1862); stitched Herculanum captions at y 470, alternating red and navy; figures with layered clothes, detailed faces and stitched hair locks; dragons on an S spine; the Iron Throne as a chair of swords; wiggle on 3s.
- Scene changes: always a 0.8s slide to the right along one strip (no cuts); Bayeux trees as dividers.
- Rules from the user: men have no red lips (`male: true`); changes of pose must be gradual (no jumps); the end card is the apple close above AMPHORUS in gold capitals with a shine (no stitch dots).
- Sound: English voice cut at word gaps; music = the theme the user drops in `Ref amphora mitologia/`, loudnorm −14, gain +10, voice.music −1, a 0.5s dip before the payoff. The Rhaenyra Targaryen Theme always starts at 0:30.
- Always show the look and the storyboard before exporting ([[feedback-storyboard-before-render]]).

**Why:** the user's approval of the Rhaenyra piece. **How to apply:** Ned (GoT) and any later HotD/GoT script; see [[project-mitos-guiones]] and styles/tapestry/STYLE.md.

- Flow method rules (user): poses must swap seamlessly (posepair.py: only the changed limb fades); moving props are their own Flow sprite, the same one throughout (e.g. the falling crown = the worn crown); nothing ever pops in; figures fully opaque, entering by walking from the sides; fire without square edges.

User's standing notes for this look: lots of detail everywhere; very pixelated (216×384 render) + cel shading (MeshToon 3 bands); muted, dark, cold teal with fog and dithered gradients — but keep warm browns, don't go fully cyan; creatures must be weird and unsettling, never cute (noh mask, long neck, mask splitting into eyes); the card image = a legend-style print (Flow Nano Banana Pro, Edo woodblock look) shown very pixelated in a striped frame.

**Quality bar (user, 2026-10-22): jorogumo's level is the minimum for this style; future pieces improve on it.** Full rules in styles/yokai/STYLE.md.

**How to apply:** start new yokai pieces from styles/yokai/template/ (jorogumo's full source); sound = Commons recordings + code layer in sound/mix.py. Local ffmpeg lacks drawtext → run review from a copy of review.mjs with the drawtext filters removed. Related: [[feedback-flow-mcp]], [[feedback-pov3d-sound-synth]].

## memoria: `cartoon3d-level.md`

---
name: cartoon3d-level
description: cartoon3d quality bar = pieces/trash-library (2026-11-12, seq Ricks camera + Ricks grade); start every new cartoon3d short from it
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: e3b19138-633b-4f91-a0e9-968a2b60dee4
  modified: 2026-10-28T00:30:00.681Z
---

The user approved pieces/apple-wayne (render renders/apple-wayne.mp4, v2) as the quality level for the cartoon3d style ("ahora sí quedó bien… guarda este nivel"). Every new short starts from its structure and must be at least this good; we keep improving from here.

What it is: piece split into src/scenes.js (common builders), src/shots.js (SHOT_LIST, per-shot c3Look, 6-frame dissolves, subtitles), src/set-*.js (one file per set, built by parallel agents in private copies), src/timewarp.js (untrimmed voice → original timeline), assets = Flow layers (faces fitted with tools/fit_faces.py, hair caps, fx glasses/beard/moustache). Sound: per-set events-*.json lists of every visible action → cues.json (~200 SFX) → sound-layer mix.py, music bed 18 LU under the voice, SFX bus +5 dB, master -14 LUFS. Voice now comes from VoiceStudio voice "3D cartoons".

Scripts: follow styles/cartoon3d/GUIONES.md — 61 s videos (~215-225 words); mostly timeless present-day scenes with a hidden-mechanism twist, period stories with dates allowed but a minority.

Deliverable: renders/final.mp4 must ALWAYS have the mixed audio (user got confused by the video-only final.mp4 that export.mjs writes). Rename the export to renders/video_only.mp4 and write the muxed file as final.mp4 (and <name>.mp4). phone-1pct (2026-10-23) approved as the second piece at this level. lego-sea (2026-10-25) approved third ("se ve y escucha todo equilibrado"): first with the HD finish and with the approved SFX balance — copy pieces/lego-sea/sound (make_cues.py: Freesound CC0 real recordings + kit, per-cue lift ~3; beds.py per-set ambience; remix.py: SFX ridden >= 3 dB under the voice short-term, music 18 LU / beds 20 LU under, -14 LUFS). (2026-10-27, future-library) Music: keep the pizzicato bed (Freesound 529008, Ricks-like) — user rejected a different track; voice a bit louder: music 20 LU / beds 22 LU under, SFX >= 4.5 dB under the voice. Always deliver a viral TikTok/Shorts title with every finished video (user 2026-10-27). Topics: check YouTube first that nobody did it (scripts/cartoon3d-guiones-03.md has the vetted list).

**NEW BAR (2026-11-12): pieces/trash-library** — user: "quedó excelente, este es el nivel que quiero para estos videos". One continuous seqCam/CAMSEQ take per set (Ricks sequential camera, fuentes/cartoon3d/camara-secuencial-ricks.md), whips between sets, Ricks grade values in shots.js COLOR, stableShadow + shadow twins, pose look:/heading:, FOCUS-layer props + depth occluders, dense detailed sets, STYLE.md §9 "Lecciones de trash-library v2". Start every new cartoon3d piece by copying trash-library.

**How to apply:** copy apple-wayne's layout and pipeline for the next piece; follow [[cartoon3d-style]] and [[cartoon3d-rules-2]].

- (2026-11-01, mromidev tutorial study — fuentes/cartoon3d/tutorial-mromidev-gap.md) New opt-ins for every NEW piece (approved pieces untouched): `C3_CAMFX` (holds creep in, punch-word push, 4-5° rolls, 7-frame flip kicks on impacts; set `C3_SHOT = { id, t0 }` in drawShot/contCamAt), `C3_DOF` per-shot background blur (CU 7, MS 5, wides 0), `c3Fog(scene,'day',near,far)` in exteriors, `c3Grain(0)` (Ricks has no grain). QA: `python -I styles/cartoon3d/tools/short_qa.py final.mp4 outdir` (black/white/frozen/pops/loudness) + `sbs_sheet.py` side-by-sides vs Ricks frames. Measured reference reports in styles/cartoon3d/mromidev-ref/. User decided (2026-11-01): NEW pieces use `C3_VIVID = C3_VIVID_MRO;` (kit preset b 1.32 c 1.0 s 0.72 vib 0.3 → measured HSV S median 0.49, luma median 0.54, p5 0.20 = mromidev targets; check with `python styles/cartoon3d/tools/grade_stats.py video.mp4`) and NO grain (end the frame with `c3Crisp(0.6); c3Vignette(0.2);`). Export stays 1080x1920 — user said NO 2K. Approved pieces keep VIVID_DEF. One-off test: pieces/human-library is made with the mromidev Remotion pipeline (pieces/human-library/app) — not for any other piece.

## memoria: `cartoon3d-rules-2.md`

---
name: cartoon3d-rules-2
description: "cartoon3d standing rules from the user's review of apple-wayne v1 (2026-10-23) — apply to every future cartoon3d video"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: e3b19138-633b-4f91-a0e9-968a2b60dee4
  modified: 2026-11-02T11:57:53.458Z
---

For this and EVERY future cartoon3d short:
- Voice: never clip a word at the start or end (the first and last "1976" were cut). Trim only in true silence, keep the tail ringing out; the piece lasts as long as the voice.
- Music bed audible from frame 0 (start the track where it already plays).
- Blurred foreground objects (depth) must MOVE with parallax through the frame, never sit glued to the screen.
- Text/labels stay inside their object (e.g. "APPLE COMPUTER CO." inside the parchment); stamps like PAY NOW placed in the empty space.
- Contact shadows under the FEET, very soft — never a disc under the torso.
- Beards stretched to the face width so they align with the head.
- Counters/tables must hide the legs/feet of people behind them.
- No visible quad edges/boxes around sprites (moths, symbols); keep small props small. Nothing passes through paper/props.
- Show facts with creative in-world devices adapted to the story (e.g. age 41 → his ID card with a bored photo and AGE 41, then a super dynamic zoom-out pan revealing the next action). Always look for that kind of staging.
- MANY more SFX: every visible action gets its sound (signing scribble, typing, drawing scratch, an object appearing, each falling board/box/pallet, flying bills flutter, clock ticks, drinking sip, footsteps, doors, paper, LED rolls…). Build cues from a per-set list of event times.

- (2026-10-23, phone-1pct) Every hairstyle glued by its measured hairline (kit HAIR table — add new styles there). Umbrella shaft meets the canopy centre, ribs never pierce it. Cars must be appealing rounded cartoon designs, never boxy. Backgrounds never flat/empty (e.g. wet street floor with reflections). Hands holding props drawn as proper cartoon hands, not blobs. Stage prop orientation unambiguously (which way a phone screen faces).

- (2026-10-25, lego-sea) User felt our videos less "colourful/HD" than Ricks Clips. Measured: refs ~6x sharper, whites 88-98 L; ours whites ~80 with a shadow-tint haze. Fix = kit HD finish: set `C3_HD = true` in shots.js and call `c3Crisp(0.45)` before vignette/grain. Use it on every new cartoon3d piece.

- (2026-10-25, lego-sea v1 review) SFX were as loud as the voice and covered it (gulls worst): SFX must sit UNDER the voice (final approved: >= 3 dB under) — remix rides the SFX bus under the voice's short-term level (pieces/lego-sea/sound/remix.py), low per-cue lift, no +5 dB bus. Also: ambient props (gulls) must never pop/flicker (draw random params once at build), cached textures must key on every state (export workers), held props attached to the real fist (no extra hand), flashlights lens-forward, and objects never interpenetrate — scan strips every ~0.1 s before rendering.

- (2026-10-27, future-library review) Hair must be IDENTICAL to Ricks Clips' characters: screenshot each hairstyle from the Ricks shorts and upload those crops to Flow as the reference images to replicate (not a collage/approximation). Fit each hair to the head: sideburns/edges must reach the head outline (stretch them). NO beards (Ricks never uses long brown beards; avoid even the small white one). Moustache only if it matches the hair colour. Thought bubbles: the little bubbles must trail from the head, text fits inside. No zipper/tape gags on mouths — use a closed-mouth face. No odd details on buildings (trees on roofs, signs/paths placed oddly).

- (2026-10-27, future-library review) Hair must be IDENTICAL to Ricks Clips: crop the real character's hair from a Ricks frame and upload THAT crop to Flow as the reference (one crop per hairstyle, never a collage) — kit `rk_*` styles (tools/slice_ricks2.py). Sideburns must reach the head outline (stretch if short). NO beards (Ricks doesn't use them). A moustache only in the same colour as the hair. Check every body sprite renders opaque (a green outfit gets eaten by the chroma key: body_dress was re-cut with a border-connected key).

- (2026-10-29, slow-checkout) User still saw a milky bloom veil vs Ricks' saturated HD look. Kit `C3_VIVID` finish (opt-in): set `C3_VIVID = C3_VIVID_DEF;` in shots.js (after C3_HD/C3_RICKS) and end the frame with `c3Crisp(0.6); c3Vignette(0.2); c3Grain(0.02);`. It drops the look's shadow screen-tint and warm multiply veil, caps bloom 0.04 / glow x0.55 / glowBlur 10 / bgBlur x0.55, grades brightness 0.9 contrast 1.2 saturate 1.2 and adds per-pixel vibrance (pale tinted surfaces gain colour, white heads stay white). Use on every new piece. Also: paint environments with saturated wall/floor colours like Ricks (yellow, teal, green walls) — pale cream/beige surfaces and pale `bg` clears are what keep a frame milky.

- (2026-10-29, slow-checkout) Framing + long takes like Ricks (measured, styles/cartoon3d/FRAMING.md): Ricks head median ~10 % of frame height, CU ~2 %, mostly full-body MS/WS + ~40 % inserts/establishing; ~27 cuts/min, ~22 % of shots > 3 s, one or two 5–11 s continuous moves per short. Every piece: shots.js SHOT_WIDEN (default 1.22, faces 1.4–1.8, inserts in SHOT_INSERT = 1) and CONTINUOUS chains of adjacent same-set beats (no dissolve, 0.55 s camera glide) — copy pieces/slow-checkout/src/shots.js. Don't chain shots whose cameras are far apart (the glide crosses walls).

- (2026-10-29, slow-checkout review) Shadows + ink like Ricks: set `C3_INK2 = C3_INK2_DEF; C3_SHADOW = C3_SHADOW_DEF;` in shots.js (kit: screen-space marker outline on every edge/crease ~3.4 px; real cast shadows from a raking key light, shadow catchers on big floors/walls, shadow map built once per frame with all layers). Continuity: in long takes (CONTINUOUS) and across dissolves people keep their world positions — a shot must start each person where the previous shot left them, never hide someone who was on screen in the previous shot of the same group (no vanishing/teleporting when the camera moves). Never place camera-space foreground props (staFg) in a shot whose camera swings a lot (they sweep across faces); check every camera glide for geometry crossing the lens (strips at 15 fps). No top-down swoops over billboard people.

- (2026-10-29, slow-checkout) Photos, portraits, x-rays and pictures in thought clouds use REAL images of what's named (generated in Flow or CC0 from the internet) with a comic touch (e.g. gap-toothed grandson holding 'I love GRAMA', knee x-ray with a smiley sticker, guilty ginger cat carrying pink slippers), mapped inside their frame/card. Enclosed rooms need enough light (warm practicals, window light, fill) so they don't read dark. No speed-line streaks behind running characters.

- (2026-11-01, swedish-number + flower-clock APPROVED) Body sprites must have NO baked sleeves (kit ink arms are the sleeves). Exact Ricks hair for every character incl. extras via styles/cartoon3d/tools/cut_ricks_hair.py (cut from Ricks frames; Flow often fails). Extras each with their own costume + hair colour. Open on a people shot, then cut to the hero object on the line that names it. Voice glitches: splice the same phrase from another take at silences (flower-clock voice).

- (2026-11-01, mromidev tutorial) Grade as the tutorial measures: `C3_VIVID = C3_VIVID_MRO` (S median ~0.49, luma ~0.55, no crushed blacks) and no film grain on every NEW piece; export stays 1080x1920 (no 2K). This replaces the earlier "lots of saturation" note for new pieces.

- (2026-11-02, human-library mromidev test) User REJECTED the mromidev Remotion bean-head characters and their motion. Keep OUR characters/animation (kit c3Person, Ricks hair, fists). ADOPT from the test: its richer sets (reading room, street, canal aerial, globe — dense props, windows, mouldings, posters), more dynamic camera (C3_CAMFX push-ins/tilts/shakes, C3_DOF, c3Fog), the MRO grade (sat ~0.49, no grain), short_qa.py + side-by-side verifier. Export stays 1080x1920.
- (2026-11-02, mistaken-orders storyboard) Interiors MUST show cast shadows: room ceilings/walls are built with `plNC`/`rbNC` (userData.noCast — kit c3ShadowSetup skips them; otherwise the ceiling shades the whole room and no shadow reads) and shots.js uses `C3_SHADOW = {...C3_SHADOW_DEF, catch: 0.6, tint: '#1e1c5a', key: 0.8}` (mromidev: warm light, cool blue-violet shadows; key > 1 washes orange walls to yellow). hair_rk_greybun is a bad purple cut — never use it; grey bun = rk_bungrey. Framing: SHOT_WIDEN ~1.6 default, inserts 1.7, and keep front tables out of the camera lines.

**Why:** the user's review of the first full render; they said "these instructions are for this video and all future ones".
**How to apply:** check every item before showing a render. Related: [[cartoon3d-style]], [[voice-cuts-in-silence]]

## memoria: `feedback-frame-by-frame-qa.md`

---
name: feedback-frame-by-frame-qa
description: QA must check CONSECUTIVE frames (not 0.5 s stills) for things popping in/out; hands in close-ups need real detail
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: beb6cd89-0da9-4e1f-972a-82e8b6124eaa
  modified: 2026-10-27T22:46:12.297Z
---

On papel (2026-10-27) the user saw glitches in the first seconds, in the office and in the city: things appearing and disappearing. The QA agent had checked stills every 0.5 s plus tiles only at the cuts, so the flicker between consecutive frames slipped through. The user also found the hand at the start lacking detail. The video was accepted as is and will not be re-rendered.

**Why:** the user asked: "verificarlo siempre frame por frame los siguientes videos".

**How to apply:**
- Before every export, scan EVERY frame for pops and flicker. Compare consecutive frames, e.g. a per-frame diff and its outliers, plus tiles over every flagged span, not just stills and cuts. Brief the QA agents on this explicitly.
- Instanced or LOD objects, shadows, near-plane clipping and visibility toggles are the usual culprits.
- Give hero hands in close-up real detail: skin texture, nails, knuckles, creases, warm subsurface tone, no mannequin look.

Related: [[feedback-verify-before-render]], [[feedback-pov3d-quality-bar]], [[feedback-self-check-board]].

## memoria: `feedback-ifverse-next.md`

metadata:

After ten-seconds (2026-10-24) the user liked the result and asked, for the next ifverse videos:
1. **More 2D→3D:** the reference is 2D but leans 3D in details — heads sometimes read half-3D (shading/turn, a sphere-like light and shadow), sets with real perspective (floors/walls in perspective, camera moves that reveal depth, objects with visible sides). Push that past the flat-card look.
2. **The arm bug:** one arm always looked mis-mounted / flipped. Cause: ivMan bent every elbow with one fixed sign, so facing the camera one elbow went out and the other went in, and the rest pose was bent. Fixed in styles/ifverse/kit.js (armIK picks the natural bend: down first, then out facing camera / back in profile; rest poses hang straight). Still check arms on the look frames and the board of every new piece (test sheet: pieces/ten-seconds/dev/armtest).

Round 2 (2026-10-26, cats board): (a) an arm still swung behind the back when the hand reached forward (panel 24) → armIK now drops the elbow when the hand is ahead of the shoulder; (b) phone close-ups must show the phone IN FRONT with only fingertips peeking past the far edge and the thumb over the near edge → kit helper ivPhoneHold(cx, cy, w, h, ang, drawPhone, {sleeve, side}); never draw a glove on top of a phone; (c) "un poco más de saturación a todo" → IV.sat 1.22 in ivPost, and night moods (vig ≥ 0.6) get a brightness lift 1.14.

**Why:** the user's notes after watching the final video.
**How to apply:** plan 2.5D upgrades to the kit (head shading/turn, perspective sets) at the look-frame stage of the next ifverse piece; review arms on every board. Related: [[project-ifverse-style]], [[feedback-ifverse-sfx]].

The niche is saturated with clone channels (Ifquirky, IFOLOGY, Ifsphere, One Odd Thing, Every Eli Life, If Then Tales…) using the same titles: always run `yt-dlp "ytsearch20:<title>"` + 2–3 variants before proposing a premise. Verified-free ideas (2026-10-24): last person who could read, taste everything in your food, shadow does what you really want, only need 1 hour of sleep, understand every dog (see REFS2.md §5).

**How to apply:** before proposing a script, check the premise against the titles of Ifverse, Jeremy Bearimy, showermath, Awaken, Miko (yt-dlp the channels' video lists again if needed) and our own videos; use REFS2.md's idea bank. Related: [[project-ifverse-style]], [[feedback-ifverse-next]].

## memoria: `feedback-ifverse-sfx.md`

---
name: feedback-ifverse-sfx
description: ifverse — SFX on EVERY action/gesture/graphic/cut with presence (≈ voice level); per-shot SFX registry, then stem remix
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

User (2026-10-24, ten-seconds): first mix had almost no audible SFX; then asked for "muchos más sfx a más cosas en general" (e.g. Nia's elbow hitting the carton) — the reference puts a sound on everything.

Method that answered it: head.html `SFX(t, kind, v, pan, dur)` registry called at registration time next to each SHOT (never in draw); score.js `SFX_KINDS` (39 synthesized kinds) plays them, same kind within 50 ms plays once; 8 agents (one per section) placed ~1,500 cues (~175/min incl. steps/ticks). Check with dev/sfxcount.mjs. Keep the deliberate silences empty. After export: stem remix — voice; music −10 dB sidechain-ducked; sfx +2 dB lightly ducked (ratio 2); loudnorm −14 LUFS TP −1.5; alimiter 0.84 → sfx moments ≈ voice level.

Update 2026-10-24 (2nd round): the dense version was too loud and too busy, the "ding" annoying. Final balance: per-kind gaps + one sound per 0.35 s (v≥1.3 exempt) → ~70/min; ding/coin = low soft marimba, ≤1 per 12 s; no bright chimes; SFX ≈ −6 dB under the voice. Music must have rhythm (groove 100–120 BPM, dynamic per section, like the ref). No film grain on ifverse.

**Why:** the user wants SFX density and presence like @IfverseTales.
**How to apply:** every ifverse piece: plan SFX per shot from the start (section agents add them), and always remix stems so SFX sit at voice level. Related: [[project-ifverse-style]].

## memoria: `feedback-onebit-flow-look.md`

---
name: feedback-onebit-flow-look
description: "User's rules for the 1-bit Junji Ito / World of Horror Flow look (expressions, white outline, flat square-pixel shading, thick subtitle stroke)"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 1c7aad81-0e25-4506-80b3-370d9bd671ea
  modified: 2026-10-27T14:47:31.435Z
---

From the elevator-game look check (2026-10-27), for every video in this style (refs: `Ref 1 bit pixelated junji ito madfable`, piece `pieces/elevator-game` has the Flow→1-bit pass `flowShot`):
- Characters change facial expression and move the head side to side across frames, like `Referencias Madfable 2.mp4` around 0:06 (brows, eye direction, mouth, small tilts every few frames), matched to the situation. Make expression/pose variants in Flow by editing the character image; swap them in code.
- Every character (human or creature) gets the subtle white outline (in the Flow prompt AND the code rim), see [[feedback-onebit-flow-outline]].
- Flatter: simpler backgrounds and less detail on figures; most shading is flat square pixels (posterized grey/black steps), not fine stipple dither. The ref close-ups have ~10 px pixels at 1080.
- Subtitles: a thicker black stroke around the white aansa letters (`fonts/aansa.ttf`); typing sfx = `Talking 1 Loop.wav` in the Ref folder.
- Keep the World of Horror UI window (e.g. a FLOOR counter) when the story has one.

**Why:** the user's corrections on the first look frames. **How to apply:** before every look/board in this style.

**Sound and captions (user, 2026-10-27, amigara board):** these videos have NO voice. The captions carry the story; while they type, `Talking 1 Loop.wav` plays, and the more disturbing the line, the more the loop is stretched (slower, lower, deeper) for an eerie feel. Captions: aansa, lower case, thick black stroke, NO white outer edge.
**Board errors the user caught (don't repeat):** keyed characters showing see-through patches (the keyer must never cut dark pixels; fill interior holes), silhouette holes that show clothing folds (a hole is pure black inside), code-drawn light beams that read as a stray limb, a creature whose origin isn't readable (show it coming out of the hole).

**Never re-pixelate Flow pixel art (user, 2026-10-27):** Flow renders this look on a native grid of ~134x240 (5.74 px per pixel in a 768x1376 image). Re-gridding it at another size broke every line ("se ve baja calidad, como si les faltaran píxeles"). Recover the native pixels with `pieces/amigara/tools/native.py` (grid detect → centre sample → palette, checker shadows on characters, flat on backgrounds, 1-px white rim on keyed layers) and only scale them up nearest-neighbour. Keep the wiggle (idle head drift) and the slow push-ins: without them it looks static.
Wiggle = the HotD/GoW whole-frame turbulence displacement (`egWiggle(2.6)`), NOT a per-layer position jitter (that read as an earthquake); see [[feedback-verify-before-render]].

**From amigara delivery (user, 2026-10-27), for EVERY video in this style:**
- Black-and-white filter over everything: Flow's images come out greyish, never full B&W. Done in the wiggle SVG filter (`egWiggle` in pieces/amigara/src/scenes.js): feColorMatrix saturate 0 + feComponentTransfer gamma 1.8 amp 1.03 (sRGB). Keep refining it video by video (refs are mostly pure black/white with little grey).
- Caption letters a bit tighter: `AF_TRACK = 0.4` (was 1).
- Outro: the channel logo `Ref 1 bit pixelated junji ito madfable/madfable icono perfil.png` (a pixel spiral) in white on black, drawn in like a pen along its stroke, then "Madfable" in `fonts/thatthatnewpixelfamilytest-square.otf` dissolving in by 9-px cells; assets from `pieces/amigara/tools/logo.py`, scene `sceneLogo`, ~3.6s, scrape + low hit.
- The user's channel is Madfable; long-form plan: cosmic-horror stories like YouTube @Urbn.Theory, with our Japanese / Junji Ito / World of Horror twist. Face and place refs: `Ref 1 bit pixelated junji ito madfable/ref caras personajes y lugares/`.
- Long-form cosmic horror (user, 2026-10-27): length is free (no 8-min target; ~3.5–6 min like Urbn.Theory is fine); stories can happen anywhere in the world, not only Japan (Junji Ito style, not Japan-only setting); no voice: captions + Talking loop + a cryptic dark BGM bed like Urbn.Theory's (sub-bass trailer/synth, booms at turns, silence over the logo). Urbn study notes: /Users/alanleiva/claude-proyectos/fuentes/urbn-theory/.
- 16:9 long-form look notes (user, lost-second look check 2026-10-28): captions SMALLER than in 9:16; the white outline around characters/creatures must be SUBTLE = thin like the refs (the 1-native-pixel code rim from native.py was too thick: drop it, keep only Flow's thin outline); align CCTV overlay text with its marks (the "rec" sat below its square); vary the shots like Urbn.Theory (high/low angles, over-the-shoulder, wide establishing, extreme close-ups, side views), not only frontal. Piece: pieces/lost-second.
- Madfable OUTRO (user, 2026-10-28, replaces the black spiral outro): red background with black tree silhouettes (file in `Ref 1 bit pixelated junji ito madfable/`), "madfable" big white in That That New Pixel, LOWER CASE, letters tighter, top centre; bottom-right the animated card (video in the same folder) pixelated a bit, background removed. Faces must be eerie/unsettling, never simple (phone-reflection face was too plain).
- Long-form length (user, 2026-10-28): these cosmic-horror videos must last AT LEAST 3 minutes (lost-second came out 1:52, too short): slower pacing like Urbn.Theory (each image held 8–20 s, slow moves) + enough story beats. Outro wordmark "madfable": NO shadow, letters nearly touching.
- Lost-second delivery fixes (user, 2026-10-28), for EVERY video in this style:
  - Deliver ONLY the final MP4 WITH audio (muxed). No silent final.mp4, no share.mp4: delete the extras or name the one deliverable clearly.
  - The wiggle was too strong; it is now lower than 2.6.
  - HUDs, CCTV frames and boxes, labels and captions get NO wiggle; only the picture does.
  - Talking-loop captions were too loud. Keep them clearly under the BGM and SFX, and raise the SFX and BGM.
  - Captions even smaller in 16:9, with tighter line spacing.
  - Always apply the B&W filter to the whole frame, Flow images included.
  - Code-drawn clock hands must leave no white boxed artefacts.
  - The white REC square sits exactly beside the word "REC", vertically centred on it.
  - The red outro card lasts longer (the user places YouTube end screens there, so at least about 20 s), and the red is saturated: red, not orange.
- Second lost-second round (user, 2026-10-28):
  - Wiggle 1.5 px, applied to the captions too. CCTV and HUD boxes still get no wiggle.
  - Master louder than -14, but -11 sounded squashed. The final lost-second master is -13 LUFS: a transparent oversampled true-peak limiter (no tanh), a bed high-pass at 35 Hz with a cut below 90 Hz, and booms on the SFX bus. The talking loop ended 12.5 dB below its first level.
  - The last caption ("whose face…") holds a few more seconds.
  - Pure 1-bit was tried: a hard threshold to #000/#fff plus checker dither. It "damaged everything" and was REVERTED. Keep the B&W pass from round 2: saturate 0 plus a steep contrast curve, with one flat grey allowed.
- **lost-second is the approved bar** (user, 2026-10-28: "quedó excelente, guarda todas estas instrucciones y nivel de detalle"). Repeat its whole pipeline and every rule above for each new long-form video:
  - story, look check and board before rendering;
  - at least 3 minutes, slow pacing, varied shots;
  - sonido pro, plus QA agents (visual frame by frame and earshot) on the FINAL export;
  - only the muxed mp4 is delivered.
  The code to copy is pieces/lost-second: src/scenes.js (HUD queue, egbw, cctv, sceneLogo) and sound/mix.py (master chain).
- **Each video also ships a title and several thumbnails** (user, 2026-10-28):
  - Title like Urbn.Theory's: the one-sentence premise in Title Case, often with "(Cosmic Horror)" or "[cosmic horror]", e.g. "They Found Human Footprints At The Bottom Of Ocean (Cosmic Horror)" or "One night, the Moon blinked. [cosmic horror]".
  - Thumbnails: always SEVERAL versions (subject moved right with the title beside it, subject centred, a tight face crop, and so on), built from the strongest frame (the user picks it, e.g. lost-second 2:20). 1280x720, with a small-size check. The Urbn refs are in fuentes/urbn-theory/thumbs/.
- Thumbnails (user, 2026-10-28):
  - Follow the user's own thumbnails in `Ref 1 bit pixelated junji ito madfable/ref miniaturas/`, especially their text style; our aansa-caps title text was disliked.
  - Always overlay "borde encima.jpeg" (a white border on green screen, chroma-keyed) on top.
  - Liked look (lost-second r7): the background in red+black duotone, with the subject cut out and kept in normal B&W on top.
  - The extracted rules are in fuentes/urbn-theory/thumbs/madfable-thumb-rules.md.
- Lost-second thumbnail chosen (2026-10-28): the m2c "bold20" look (the man ×7 on the right on a red-black subway, kanji in ONE white vertical column centred between him and the border). The user calls the bold20 render "your font": Nosutaru-dotMPlusH-10 drawn at 20 px with a bold pass. The thin native dot render (12 px) was rejected. Script: pieces/lost-second/tools/thumbs_m2c.py.
- 9:16 Madfable outro (user, 2026-10-29, nure-onna): the animated card is CENTRED below the "madfable" wordmark and bigger, not bottom-right. The 16:9 outro keeps the card bottom-right.
- Nure-onna fixes (user, 2026-10-29):
  - "B&W" means a Premiere-style Black & White effect: desaturate the whole final picture to luma, with no threshold, posterize or extra contrast. Apply it to everything except the red outro.
  - The 9:16 red outro lasts only 5 s. The 16:9 long-form outro keeps about 20 s for the end screens.
  - Never repeat the same image for two beats; each beat gets its own shot.

- 2026-10-29 (bells): whenever possible split images into LAYERS (foreground/subject/background, fog, figures cut out) to give dynamic motion (parallax, independent drift), not just a flat push on one image.
- 2026-10-29 (bells): top-left tag = the user's own WoH tag from https://youtu.be/AMpBNywoQB0 (black icon box + white bar with double border, "KANJI-THE TITLE" in Nosutaru dot, dithered dots bottom-right); implemented in pieces/bells (src/tagfont.js, scenes.js). Flow style refs for characters/places: 'Ref 1 bit pixelated junji ito madfable/ref caras personajes y lugares/' ("use ONLY as a drawing-style reference, do NOT copy its scene"). End-question card uses thatthatnewpixelfamilytest-square like the madfable wordmark. Bell inscriptions engraved along the curve, not flat. Junji horror = stillness/realism; googly or vertical-slit eyes read as funny.
- 2026-10-30 (bells thumbs): user likes the World of Horror search-style thumbnails (1-bit dot shading, tight face crop, title box). Rules: characters must look like JAPANESE World of Horror / Junji Ito characters (use WoH game art from the ref folder as Flow style ref), never European/painterly; the title box is NEVER rotated; box text is Japanese ONLY (no English line).
- 2026-10-30 (bells): the coarse native-grid pass (8 px cells, 3–4 levels + cleanup) made CHARACTER FACES unreadable in the video and thumbnails. Pixelate, but faces must stay readable: for characters use a finer grid (~4–5 px) with ink-line protection (dark lines forced black first) and fine 3-px dither only in the shadows; lit skin clean white. Check every face at 50% scale before export. Thumbs: moderate shadows (between too-white and heavy dither).
- 2026-10-30 (bells): NEVER turn every mid-tone into checker dither (sky, walls, clothes, mountains all dithered = "muy feo"). The look is FLAT grey areas (black / dark grey / mid grey / white). Dither only in a few selected shadows, if at all. When fixing face readability, only refine the grid + protect lines; keep the flat palette. Always extract and look at full-res video frames before reporting a re-process.
- 2026-10-30 (bells) APPROVED ("ahora sí, a eso me refería"): pieces/bells/tools/gentle.py = the standard image pass for characters from now on: board's flat palette (black / dark grey / mid grey / white, no dither), 4-px grid, cell = median of its centre, a cell goes black only where a thin dark stroke runs through it. Faces read, look stays flat.
- 2026-10-30 (bells): pure 1-bit (no greys) tested again on bells and rejected again: KEEP the flat greys. The subtle white outline on characters/objects must be continuous: draw it in code from each cut-out mask (1 grid cell, pixel-aligned) instead of relying on Flow's outline, which breaks when cut out.
- 2026-10-30 (bells): parallax layers must not leave ghost pixels of the figure in the background (dilate the removal mask before inpainting; check first/last frame of each drift). Camera moves: one smooth motivated move per shot, never push-in/pull-back yo-yo. The reveal must escalate past earlier appearances (e.g. ALL eyes open at the reveal).

- 2026-11-04: any flashlight, lamp or sub light gets a DYNAMIC moving light (sweep, wobble or flicker), like Amigara (pieces/amigara/src/scenes.js egSpot plus sin drift). Re-draw the white outline in code wherever a cut-out lost it.
- 2026-11-04 (repeated correction, learning-faces): STILL over-whitening. Before every export, compare the gentle pass against pieces/bells/tools/gentle.py; light skin/surfaces = light/mid grey with shading, white ONLY where the source is truly white. Same for thumbnails. Pre-reveal silence ~1.5-2 s max (4.8 s was too long).
- 2026-11-04: NEVER fix too-white by area tone steps: they make "vitiligo" faces (white/grey patches, streaks). Instead apply one smooth global highlight compression on the source (white→~0.70), then the bells gentle mapping. Captions Urbn-Theory style: smaller, placed in the empty areas of each shot and moving between lines, never over faces. Hidden creatures: blend them into darkness with a pixel falloff, no hard cut-out. Reveal layers + outline must stay aligned through glitches.
- 2026-11-04 APPROVED PIPELINE (supersedes gentle.py 4-tone/highlight curve): Flow output is already the look. Only snap to the 4-px grid (median) with 7 tones (0,.18,.34,.50,.66,.84,1). NEVER few-tone "corrections" that damage the image. Code adds effects ON TOP (moving lights/torches, particles, clouds, fog), never degrades the picture. Always generate expression + head-move variants per character. Experiment with bold shots sometimes (overhead/cenital, low angle/contrapicado, dutch). Never re-export without board/look approval first.
- 2026-11-04: ANATOMY CHECK before showing any image: count hands/arms per person at full size and check left vs right (Flow made 3 arms, then 2 right hands). If an edit cannot fix it, generate a new image. Creatures in windows = one coherent Flow image, never pasted from parts.
- 2026-11-04: Cut-out layers hold ONLY the person (and what they hold); nearby objects/props/furniture stay in the background so parallax never drags them. Verify by comparing frames at both ends of each move.
- 2026-11-04 learning-faces APPROVED FINAL = the reference workflow for every next Madfable video: soft.py (4-px median + 7 tones, nothing else); Flow outline kept + subtle restore only where a cut-out lost it; code effects on top (moving lights, snow, fog); expression variants with crossfades; bold shots (overhead, low angle, Dutch) mixed in; person-only cut-outs; anatomy check at full size; Urbn-style moving captions; VHS glitch (no negative strobe); stills or board approved before every export. Copy pieces/learning-faces/tools (soft.py, outline.py, cutm.py, subplace.mjs).

metadata:

The user approved `pieces/hackeo-1834` as "excelente" and asked that its level of detail be the floor for all future videos in this style, to be raised further with each new video.

**Why:** they compare against strong references and sent back every flat, rushed or off-beat element over three rounds (depth, complete maps, route draw-ons, opening zoom, red flash, longer beats, a bass/chord bed, chords locked to the melody).
**How to apply:** before showing frames or a cut of any pixdoc piece, go through `styles/pixdoc/STYLE.md` → "Frame checklist (minimum)" and "Sound (minimum)" and meet every line: music from frame 0 with a held bass+chord bed, one harmonic map (`HAR`) so chords never drift from the melody, everything musical on the grid, present SFX for every visual event, 4-layer depth with parallax, shadows, camera life, complete maps, captions ≤ 3.5 words/s. Then add at least one improvement beyond it. Related: [[feedback-animation-richness]], [[project-pixdoc-style]].

metadata:

From the galaxia piece (2026-10-18) on, pixdoc pieces carry a narrator voice in Spanish, "like the other style" (voltamps).
**Why:** user asked: "a partir de ahora vamos a comenzar a agregarle voz de narrador a este estilo también".
**How to apply:** with the story, hand over the Spanish script as plain text only (no ids/table) so it can be pasted into the voice generator; the user generates and passes the take; Claude cuts it at word gaps and times the picture to it (see [[feedback-voltamps-voice-script]]). pixdoc keeps its own code-synth music under the voice ([[feedback-sound-per-style]]), plus captions.

**Mix with voice (galaxia, 2026-10-18):** the export's default voice mix (score at −9 dB, ducked) left the SFX inaudible — user: "súbele más volumen a los sfx". Remix from stems: voice + music −9 dB (sidechain duck 4:1) + sfx stem +4 dB (light duck 1.8:1) → loudnorm −14 + alimiter 0.84, remux into final/share. Do this by default on voiced pixdoc pieces.

name: feedback-roblox-rules

User approved rbx-thursday's final version (2026-11-03) and asked to keep these instructions for every future video of the roblox style. Full checklist in styles/roblox/STYLE.md, section "Reglas aprobadas".

**Why:** after two acting passes the user said "ahora sí quedó bien": camera zooms were liked; the constant bounce was rejected ("parecen que estuvieran bailando").
**How to apply:** start from pieces/rbx-thursday; fast eased punch-in/pull-out per shot + creep + handheld; characters move independently (look-around, weight shift, own gestures, real walk cycles) but never bounce; board before render; GreenBro is the acting reference. To study a channel, list it with `yt-dlp --flat-playlist <channel>/shorts` (it works) and watch videos with ver-youtube. Related: [[project-roblox-style]], [[feedback-storyboard-before-render]].
- (2026-11-03) GreenBro study of the 105 shorts >1M: fuentes/roblox-cartoon/greenbro-movimiento.md (13 engine changes proposed; not applied — the user's approved zooms/acting take priority unless they say otherwise).
- (2026-11-03) USER DECISION: apply the GreenBro study to the next roblox video (only the protagonist acts with held poses from a gesture library, mouth open/close per word, real walk cycles, fixed dutch on some shots, shake only on impacts) BUT keep the fast zooms exactly as in rbx-thursday's last version (punch-in at every cut, pull-out every 3rd shot, creep + handheld) — do not reduce them.
- (2026-11-03) USER APPROVED v2-greenbro as final and as the standard for all future roblox videos: ENG.MODE 'gb' is now the default in pieces/rbx-thursday/src/engine.js (v1 kept as renders/v1-final.mp4).
- (2026-11-03) The hero's age / 'Me? I'm ten.' is NOT in any of the 18 ref transcripts: never write it; introduce the hero through his quirk instead.
- (2026-11-03) SAME STRUCTURE, DIFFERENT STORY: copy only the refs' structure; every story picks its own cast and its own loved one for the plot (refs: sister 2/18, brother 2/18, mom/dad 8/18, best friend 6/18, grandma 5/18). Never repeat stock lines or characters across videos ("Me? I'm ten", "My little sister Pip is four", same hero intro). **Why:** the user noticed I reused both in rbx-thursday and rbx-sock. **How to apply:** check every new script against the previous pieces' scripts before showing it.
- (2026-11-04) Final mp4 = the TikTok viral title in the ref channels' format (Gneef/GreenBro/redfish top titles): 2–6 words, Title Case, the rule or the twist, ONE emoji at the end, optional CAPS word or "??" ("Never Sleep Outside 🌳", "You Must Be Quiet 🤫", "Lying Makes You Heavier 😱", "We REPLACED Her Pet Fish 🐟"). File name includes the emoji. Check Ref roblox/list_*.txt before naming.
- (2026-11-04) Story variety study of 132 ref shorts: fuentes/roblox-cartoon/variedad-historias.md (+ "Variedad entre historias" checklist in styles/roblox/STYLE.md). Fill the premise "ficha" and run the anti-repetition checklist before writing ANY new script: vary opening (In this world 34 %, In this town 19 %, Everyone… 14 %), world/locations from the premise, loved one rotates, 2–3 adaptation gags (not 5), no stock townsfolk, twist mostly "the rule/villain was something else" (52 %) rather than literal reading (13 %), ending mostly tender callback or dark joke. Thursday and Sock matched 5/8 traits — refs match ~2/8.

- **BGM (2026-11-07): ALWAYS** "TEMPOREX - Numbers (Instrumental | Perfect intro loop)" (youtube ecvbCDTcAco), saved at styles/roblox/bgm/bgm.wav — for every video from now on. Replaces per-piece music beds; voice clearly on top (music 9 LU under the voice (user: 20 and 12 LU were too quiet), ~9 dB margin while speaking). Applied to rbx-chess.

- **Characters (2026-11-08): replicate Gneef's hair, outfits and expressions** in every new roblox video ("me gustan porque son muy wild"). Spec: fuentes/roblox-cartoon/gneef-looks.md (from 15 Gneef shorts incl. crvPRFMpKLA); section in styles/roblox/STYLE.md. Run its checklist when building the cast and show it in the look sheet.
