- **(2026-11-08) Gneef = only faces, hair, outfits, lighting. NEVER copy their stiff movement.** Our characters keep the gb acting of rbx-chess/thursday (constant body acting + gestures); rope/prop holders still act with the body (hands locked via IK). **Why:** rbx-rope v1 froze everyone holding the rope and the user flagged it.

- **(2026-11-10) The dino-hood hero (pieces/rbx-thursday hero, brand image pieces/rbx-thursday/brand/) is the PROTAGONIST OF EVERY roblox video — the channel's face.** Never replace him (rbx-rope and rbx-checkpoint wrongly used new heroes). Gneef wild styling applies to the rest of the cast; the hero keeps his dino hood + identity, faces change like Gneef.

## memoria: `feedback-self-check-board.md`

---
name: feedback-self-check-board
description: Before showing any storyboard, check creature anatomy close-up (teeth direction/inside the mouth, floating parts, silhouette vs the reference) and fix it first
metadata:
  type: feedback
---
Before showing a storyboard, render the creature isolated and the closest panels, and fix anatomy errors myself: teeth upside down or poking outside the jaw, parts floating off the body, a silhouette that drifts from the reference image (e.g. Behemoth's wavy brow-to-snout profile).

**Why:** on behemoth (2026-10-25) the user caught teeth outside the mouth twice and upside-down teeth, and asked me to always verify these before showing the board.
**How to apply:** an isolated side + 3/4 render of every creature and a close look at its panels is part of the board step, every revision. Related: [[feedback-storyboard-before-render]], [[project-yokai-style]].

## memoria: `feedback-tapestry-rules.md`

---
name: feedback-tapestry-rules
description: Every instruction the user gave for HotD/GoT tapestry videos (Rhaenyra, 2026-10-20/21) — apply all of them to every future piece made with the Flow method
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Checklist for every House of the Dragon / Game of Thrones video (tapestry + Flow method, [[project-tapestry-style]]):

**Process**
- Script in English, ~1100 characters (~60s), opens with the protagonist's first name only, ends on a tragic or epic line; hand over the plain script; the user generates one take into `Ref amphora mitologia/Voces/` and says when; cut it at word gaps ([[project-mitos-guiones]]).
- Always show the look, then the full storyboard, and wait for approval before every export, revisions included ([[feedback-storyboard-before-render]]).
- Music: the theme the user drops in Ref (Rhaenyra Targaryen Theme always from 0:30), with strong presence (music gain +10, voice.music −1); SFX sit under it; a 0.5s dip before the payoff.

**Look**
- Linen background from v1 (visible, slightly imperfect weave) + v2 sewn borders top and bottom, close to the edges; no figure ever touches the border lines.
- Figures and dragons as close to the reference tapestry as possible (naive Bayeux, coarse stitches, detailed stitched hair, never flat); dragons with stitched texture.
- Men never have red lips.
- Figures are always fully opaque, never transparent.
- Keep secondary figures large (small bearded figures look wrong) and never leave a scene empty: bring in the main character (e.g. Viserys with the kneeling lords).
- Captions stitched (Herculanum, alternating red/navy, side words in their colour), at the top of the panel but lowered toward the figures wherever the picture leaves space.
- End card: the apple and AMPHORUS (gold capitals with a moving shine, no stitch dots) together, centred in the frame.
- The whole frame wiggles (as the other styles).

**Motion**
- Scene changes are always a slide to the right, never a cut.
- Make it as dynamic as possible: extra poses come from editing the character's own image in Flow (an arm, a head, a sword) and swap seamlessly (posepair.py: only the changed part fades).
- Anything that moves on its own (a falling crown, fire, a sword) is its own Flow sprite, the same one from start to end — the falling crown is the one she ends up wearing.
- Nothing ever appears or changes abruptly: characters walk in from the sides (bob + rock), things fall in from above, grow, or arrive with the slide; growth/pose changes are gradual.
- Fire has natural flame edges, never square cuts (it must not touch an image or panel edge).

**Why:** the user's corrections across the Rhaenyra code and Flow versions. **How to apply:** go through this list before showing a look, a storyboard, or a final.
- Slides must never cut elements at the seam (clouds, sea, dragons): only a vertical clip, both cloths drawn first (user, 2026-10-22).
- Wide elements (sea, cloud banks, flame rows) must be generated with finished, natural ends inside the image (rounded cloud puffs, waves that taper), never cut by the image edge; place every element whole inside its panel or overhanging whole.

name: feedback-verify-before-render

metadata:

  originSessionId: 1c7aad81-0e25-4506-80b3-370d9bd671ea
  modified: 2026-10-27T16:44:06.969Z
---

Before generating/exporting ANY video (and every re-export), run a full verification with as many agents as needed (high effort): visual frame-by-frame QA and sound QA in parallel, then fix, then export. Never hand the user a render with unverified changes (user, 2026-10-27: "verifica estas cosas SIEMPRE antes de generar el video, pon los agentes que necesites para no perder más tiempo").

"Wiggle" = the whole-frame fractal-turbulence displacement of the House of the Dragon (tapestry `tpWiggle`) and God of War (amphora-bf `bfWiggle`) videos: ~2.6 px, re-seeded every 3 frames, lines tremble in place. NOT a position jitter of layers (that read as an earthquake) and not a slow head drift.

**Why:** several renders went out with problems the user had to catch, and I misread "wiggle" twice. **How to apply:** for any piece, reuse that turbulence filter as STYLE.post (see `egWiggle` in pieces/amigara/src/scenes.js) and check it against a tapestry piece before export. Related: [[feedback-self-check-board]], [[feedback-onebit-flow-look]].

## memoria: `feedback-voltamps-voice-script.md`

---
name: feedback-voltamps-voice-script
description: voltamps (Ref volt y amps) pieces — plain EN script only; one voice take cut at word gaps; Ref documentary track as music; strong code SFX
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 7c471d3f-6c90-4407-9a76-9911d880ee64
  modified: 2026-10-14T04:47:35.316Z
---

For voltamps / Bitvolts pieces (from `Ref volt y amps/`):
- **Since 2026-10-23 (video 9): Claude generates the voice itself in VoiceStudio** (local API :3900, `POST /generate` multipart: text, profile_id, language=en, seed, speed) with the profile **"mathomaly" (id e4eb9da7)**, 2 seeds per line, picking the take whose whisper transcript matches best — `references/voltamps/tools/vs_gen.py <piece> e4eb9da7 1,2 1.0`. No more waiting for the user's take; still show the script. Same BGM (Ref documentary track).
- When giving the voice script, the message/block is ONLY the script text — no ids, no table, no commentary — so the user can copy-paste it straight into the voice generator. Hand it over right after drafting the story; the user generates while Claude builds style frames.
- The user generates the voice as ONE single take and drops it in `Ref volt y amps/Voces/`. Claude cuts it into lines itself and times the picture to it. Cuts must fall in the silence between words (never mid-word) — use faster-whisper word times and cut at the gap midpoint / lowest energy.
- Music: no composed background music. Use the track in `Ref volt y amps/` ("Documentary Background Music for Videos.mp3") at a good level under the voice (piece.json "music"); the code score is SFX only (to='s') and the SFX must have strong presence.
- Master louder than the skill's −14 LUFS: after export, +4.5 dB into `alimiter=limit=0.74:level=false` (without level=false ffmpeg auto-levels to ≈ −9 LUFS, peak > 0), remuxed from renders/audio.wav (≈ −11.5 LUFS, true peak ≈ −1.3 dBFS) and remux into final/share (user: "sube el volumen master", LED piece). Always measure the remuxed share.mp4 (ebur128 peak): if the true peak is above −1 dBFS, redo with `volume=4.2dB,alimiter=limit=0.68:attack=1` (≈ −12 LUFS); if still above (sharp SFX, cargar), `limit=0.6` (≈ −12 LUFS, −1.4 dBFS). Transcribe/cut helpers live in `references/voltamps/tools/` (tr.py, cut.py); zero-gap words need an energy-profile check.
- No constant noise/hiss beds in the SFX: they pump audibly in every voice pause (rayos).
- Look: push past the reference — more glow, texture, depth and animation than the ref.

**Why:** user's instructions on 2026-10-14 (first piece: rayos / "Why does lightning seek the ground?").
**How to apply:** script = condensed EN paraphrase of the Spanish reference (keep every explanation step), >60s, title card at the very start. Related: [[feedback-pov3d-language]], [[feedback-animation-richness]].

## memoria: `feedback-yokai-rules.md`

---
name: feedback-yokai-rules
description: Full checklist of the user's instructions for yokai-style videos (look, creature, card, hook, sound, workflow) — check it at story, look, board and final
metadata:
  type: feedback
---
Everything the user asked for across jorogumo and behemoth (2026-10-22..25). Behemoth's final level is the bar ("ahora sí quedó excelente").

**Topics:** alternate one proven hit from @theredarchivesyt / @earlobehuman (Trevor Henderson, SCP, analog horror… copyright is not a blocker) with one Japanese yōkai. English, first-person paragraphs, ~75 s, no voice, no badge.

**Look:**
- Very pixelated (216×384) + toon shading in 3 bands; lots of detail everywhere (code textures, props, life, rain).
- Cold teal palette but keep warm browns; never full cyan.
- The "oppressive" feel = the 2×2 warm dot screen over mid-tones (YK.DOT), measured from earlobe's whale video. It is NOT darkness. Never a vignette.
- Warm point lights (lamps, tail lights) against the teal; rain streaks.

**Creature:**
- Weird and unsettling, never cute; match the source design closely (compare with frames of the ref video and the wikis).
- Add yōkai touches (shimenawa, shide, ofuda, rust stripes) and something evil (e.g. a red pupil).
- No floating bits (spikes, plates). The neck must join the head.
- Teeth based at the gum, tips toward the other jaw, inside the mouth.
- Silhouettes: a gentle curve, not waves, not a bird beak, unless the design says so.

**Card:**
- Flow (Nano Banana Pro) with earlobe's card prints as style refs + the creature from the ref video as design ref.
- Generate several, keep the one whose design matches; reject drifted shapes (e.g. a beak).
- Drawn very low-res (~90 px wide) in the striped frame.

**Characters:** dress people in Japanese clothing (kasuri / hanten jacket, obi, hachimaki, straw hat) as earlobe does, even in modern settings where it fits (user, 2026-10-26).

**Channel badge (user, 2026-10-26):** at the end, centred at the top: the kodama figure from `Ref earlobe horror/foto perfil kodamashorts.jpg` with its black square keyed out (only the photo's background goes) + the name "kodamashorts", both ON the navy woven pixel plate like earlobe's badge — the plate stays (`ykBadge` in the kit).

**Hook:** the creature big, clear and moving in the first 2 s, upper half, lighter than its background; a warning/rule as the first line.

**Sound = "sonido pro" by default:**
- Commons beds + code layer.
- A Freesound CC0 layer picked with earshot (rank → find → realness), credits with z / p_real.
- earshot critique on the final: fix the body level and mids; ignore its launch-film flags (music presence, onset density).
- Keep the reveal loudest after exact silence.

**Technical traps (umibozu):** no logarithmic depth buffer with custom ShaderMaterials (the sea lost depth → body interiors showed at the waterline); place people after the boat's final pose each frame (feet through the deck); check the thumb side; a held prop must sit in the fist (grip point), not beside it.

**Pre-board QA is mandatory (user, 2026-10-26: "no podemos estar perdiendo tanto tiempo"):** before showing ANY storyboard, run a full self-review — ideally with high-effort review agents — over frames every 0.25–0.5 s: creature isolated (anatomy, thumb side, teeth, no floating parts, no open mesh at waterlines), every prop held IN the hand, no body/hand/camera through boat or floor (code checks like armCheck + foot height), held objects readable, water/terrain actually covering what's under it, text never hiding the key action. Fix everything found, then show. The user should only judge taste, not catch bugs. Scope is EVERYTHING, not a fixed list (user, 2026-10-26): every object, motion, transition, prop, character, camera, lighting, water, text, story readability — anything that looks wrong, odd, unclear or low quality gets fixed before the board.

**Workflow:**
- Before every storyboard, render the creature isolated and the closest panels, and fix anatomy errors myself.
- Scrub the final for camera clipping (props through the lens, camera below ground).
- Card seal: the same small red square as before, with ONE pixelated kanji for THAT creature (e.g. 犬 for Inunaki), never two glyphs, never the same glyph in every piece.
- No mirror or tiny inset shots for key story beats: use a direct, big, readable shot.
- Show the full board and wait for approval before export.

**Why:** these are the user's explicit corrections; repeating them cost several board rounds.
**How to apply:** start from pieces/behemoth (landscape/creature-head pieces) or pieces/umibozu (sea, boat, people on a moving deck, two-bone arm IK, held props, armCheck, badge) (copy src/, sound/mix.py, kit) instead of the older template; run this list at story, look, board and final. Related: [[project-yokai-style]], [[feedback-yokai-sources]], [[feedback-self-check-board]], [[feedback-earshot-sfx]], [[feedback-flow-mcp]].

**Speed (user, 2026-10-30/31):** pieces were taking 2–3 h. Reuse the previous piece's src (gashadokuro/corpo-seco), keep QA targeted (numeric + frame scan + one visual pass), board in under an hour. After render: ONE fix round only for real failures (clipping, floating parts, text over the subject, unreadable story beat); no second polish round. List remaining minor items to the user and let them decide.

**Creature motion and people (user, 2026-11-13, Teke Teke "da risa"):** creatures must move uncannily: stop-motion holds then snaps, twitchy over-rotated head tilts, out-of-sync fingers, slow pulls then sudden bursts, freezes before lunges; no smooth/symmetric/bouncy cartoon motion. Faces mostly hidden (hair, shadow), one eye visible; heavy hair with weight and secondary motion, never straight strips. People need real walk cycles (heel-toe, locked stance foot, no deep knee squat, counter-swing) and realistic faces (no dot eyes / "O" mouths). Night scenes lit by flickering street lamps with dark gaps between pools of light.

## memoria: `feedback-yokai-sources.md`

---
name: feedback-yokai-sources
description: yokai topics — adapt any proven hit (Trevor Henderson, SCP, Mandela Catalogue, analog horror, folklore) from @theredarchivesyt / @earlobehuman; copyright of the creature is not a blocker

For yokai-style videos, pick creatures from whatever has already worked as a hit on the reference accounts (TikTok @theredarchivesyt, @earlobehuman), including authored IP: Trevor Henderson, SCP, Mandela Catalogue, analog horror, creepypasta, folklore. **Earlobe's own topics (2026-10-25):** creatures earlobe already did are allowed too (pick the ones with good views), retold with a different but similar story and the creature in a similar place.

**Warm-up phase (user, 2026-10-27):** the account is new — use LOWER-view topics first (e.g. <~300 k on the ref accounts) and save the biggest hits (Moon Woke Up, Watchtower, Giant Puppeteer, Qu, SCP-169, World Eater…) for when the account has traction. Ask the user before switching back to top hits.

**How to apply:** don't filter candidates by copyright. Still write our own story text and our own models (never copy their frames or wording). Listings and downloads are in references/tiktok/. Related: [[project-yokai-style]].

## memoria: `project-amphora-style.md`

---
name: project-amphora-style
description: amphora style (Ref amphora mitologia) — video-8 parchment pencil look + video-5 meander friezes; EN paraphrased script; Odysseus bgm; Ludovico font; "Amphorus" sign-off
metadata:
  type: project
---

amphora style, started 2026-10-18 with the Alcibiades piece (remake of ref video 8).
- Look: mainly ref video 8 (parchment, pencil-hatched figures, crosshatch vignette, coloured keywords: Athens blue, Sparta red, Persia gold) + Greek meander friezes top and bottom like ref video 5; refs 6 and 7 for more of the look.
- Text: font "Ludovico W03 Woodcut.ttf" from `fonts/`. Script always in English, paraphrased from the ref's wording; push the animation past the ref.
- Voice: Claude gives a plain script and the user generates one take into `Ref amphora mitologia/Voces/` (voltamps workflow, [[feedback-voltamps-voice-script]]).
- Music: `Ref amphora mitologia/Odysseus bgm.mp3`, with strong presence: the file is very quiet (−29.6 LUFS), so loudnorm it to −14 into audio/track.wav, music gain +7, voice.music −4; sfx sit under the music (user, Alcibiades piece). The score tail normalises sfx, so balance via music gain, not sfxBus.
- Sign-off: "Amphorus" in the gold Roman-capitals look of the ARQA logo at the end of ref video 8.

**Why:** user's instructions at intake. **How to apply:** every amphora piece; see [[feedback-animation-richness]].

Two styles for this niche (user, 2026-10-19): **beige** = `styles/amphora` (pieces/alcibiades) and **orange** = `styles/amphora-bf` (black-figure puppets from refs 3–5, fondo.jpeg as asset, ITC Garamond italic white captions; pieces/alcibiades-bf). Both use the same voice/bgm/SFX workflow; keep improving both.

**amphora-bf with Flow layers (pieces/troya-bf, remake of ref video 5, 2026-10-20):** figures and sets are Nano Banana 2 layers (Flow MCP, `@{odysseus}` as style ref, magenta keyed) animated in code, instead of code-drawn puppets; the user liked it ("muchísimo mejor"). Captions: ITC Garamond Std italic (user's pick over 1689 GLC); end banner = `Ref amphora mitologia/ribbon.jpeg` (green-keyed) unrolling from the centre, not a parchment scroll.
Later on troya-bf the user switched captions to **Ludovico W03 Woodcut** (use the PostScript name "LudovicoW03-Woodcut" in canvas — the family name silently falls back), letter-spaced, shadowed, **written by hand** word by word; scenes **slide right** with no cuts (like rhaenyra); ribbon text "The Odyssey"; SFX a bit lower (music gain 10).
**Orange style is now v2 by default (user, 2026-10-20: "actualiza el estilo para que siempre sea así"):** styles/amphora-bf/STYLE.md + kit (bfLay, bfStripStage, bfCam, bfCaptions/bfPen, bfRibbon, bfSignoff) + styles/amphora-bf/assets (fondo, ribbon, apple). New orange pieces start by copying pieces/troya-bf.
- amphora-bf with Flow (Kratos, 2026-10-23, user): the core of this style is SIMPLE figures — solid black silhouettes with only a few thin orange incised lines, little detail; every figure black (no coloured/red-filled bodies); game characters adapted from their game renders (Ares, Odin, Thor) but simplified; figures that talk face each other; captions in Dalek Pinpoint Bold, brown like the "kratos 1" ref lettering.
- Before handing over any amphora-bf/tapestry video (user, 2026-10-23): run `node styles/amphora-bf/tools/capcheck.mjs <piece> '#6e2a18'` (every frame: no caption word over the top frieze or past x 945); captions are phrases of ≤7 words, ≤2 lines, each complete before the next, the last one sliding out with the cloth; fight SFX must be clearly audible (music gain 0 with the God of War track; SFX strikes ~5 dB over the music).

---

On 2026-10-23 the user switched the Bitvolts (voltamps workflow) look: "ahora será exactamente como los videos ref 1, ref 2, ref 3 y ref 4 … replica el estilo visual, subtítulos y todo". First piece in it: video 9 (charging the phone overnight).

The look (measured from the refs, 720×1280 @30fps):
- Dark charcoal / warm-brown grounds (#070707, #1c1c1c, #140b06), soft vignette, bokeh specks, depth-of-field blur on far layers.
- Semi-realistic 2.5D objects with gradients, soft shadows and highlights (card reader, phone, keyboard keys, cups), cartoon hands/thumbs (skin #e5b4a8 / #c58768 / #b57759, pink nails).
- Warm amber/gold glowing lines for fields and current (#f5b74a-ish), occasional red accents.
- Captions: word-by-word karaoke, top-centre (~19% from the top), modern geometric sans, ~60px at 1080. Spoken words appear one at a time; the current word is white semibold, earlier words fade to grey (#8a8a8a) regular; a keyword gets a blue text-selection box (navy fill, #3b82f6 outline, small round handles at two corners).
- In-scene labels: small mono or serif tags; big numbers in sans/mono with glow.

**Feedback after video 9 (2026-10-23):** next pieces must be more 2D-3D like ref 1, 2 and 3, with dynamic camera moves and seamless transitions. What the refs do (sampled in references/voltamps/new/motion.png):
- One continuous camera, almost no hard cuts: dolly out from a close-up (the reader's screen) to the whole object, crane/tilt as a new object (the card, a hand) enters from the frame edge, push-ins that end inside an object.
- Objects in real perspective (3/4 from above, tilted planes, parallax between near/far layers, DOF blur on the far ones), not flat front views.
- Transitions are motivated: the next scene slides in from below while the camera tracks down (newspaper rising under the hand), a zoom rushes through particles/sky into the next era, a match on shape (same object carries over).
- Motion is continuous and eased (springs), counters and fields animate while the camera keeps moving.

**Why:** explicit user instruction; supersedes the old voltamps line-art look and the "Georgia serif for titles / grid background" rule for these pieces (the workflow rules — plain EN script, one voice take cut at word gaps, Ref documentary music, strong SFX, louder master, storyboard before render, Bitvolts sign-off — still apply).
**How to apply:** build each new Bitvolts piece in this look; check captions and depth against the refs before the board. Related: [[feedback-voltamps-voice-script]], [[feedback-voltamps-text]], [[feedback-storyboard-before-render]].

## memoria: `project-gow-greek-style.md`

---
name: project-gow-greek-style
description: God of War Greek-era videos = amphora-bf black-figure Flow style from pieces/kratos (approved 2026-10-23); full recipe in styles/amphora-bf/STYLE.md
metadata:

---

Every God of War video set in the Greek era uses the style of `pieces/kratos`: start by copying it. Recipe in styles/amphora-bf/STYLE.md → "God of War — Greek era".
Key rules from the user: simple black figures (few lines), game characters from their renders but simplified, characters face each other, Kratos = 2 blades / 2 arms, enemies to fight when fights are narrated, Dalek Pinpoint brown captions (≤7 words, ≤2 lines, complete, slide out with the cloth, never over the frieze — run capcheck.mjs), VoiceStudio "Mad 3" voice generated by Claude, God of War Soundtrack from 0:01 at gain 0 with strong fight SFX. Norse-era style is not decided yet.

**Why:** the user approved this look and asked to keep it for the Greek saga. **How to apply:** with [[project-amphora-style]] and [[feedback-storyboard-before-render]].

Also used for Odysseus (pieces/scylla, Scylla & Charybdis, 2026-10-29): same method + Odysseus bgm. Lesson: never put a slide within ~1.5s after the HIT; merge the strike and its aftermath into one panel. Bottom captions must sit at y <= 1470 (phone UI).

## memoria: `project-ifverse-style.md`

---
name: project-ifverse-style

metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 873f4ba5-4766-4ba9-9234-63d202a0c750
  modified: 2026-10-24T02:06:09.406Z
---

Started 2026-10-23: replicate @IfverseTales "What If…?" videos. User rules: **English, 16:9 long-form for YouTube, never under 8:00** (aim ~8:20), **everything in code (no Flow)**. Narrator = VoiceStudio profile **mathomaly** (e4eb9da7, speed 0.9); each character gets a VoiceStudio profile cloned from a voice-designed sample (`instruct` e.g. "male, teenager, high pitch, american accent"; one-off characters use instruct + fixed seed).

Files: analysis + guide spec styles/ifverse/ANALISIS.md; kit styles/ifverse/kit.js (ivStage depth/DOF, ivMan rig, ivGhost, ivCounter…); tools styles/ifverse/tools/md2json.py + vs_cast_gen.py; first piece pieces/ten-seconds (BRIEF.md, SECTIONS.md, SETS_API.md, PROPS_API.md, src/sets.js, src/props.js reusable). Refs in "Ref ifverse/".

Workflow that worked: script.md with [Name] lines and [beat Ns] → voice (pauses SENT 0.85 / PARA 1.25 / CHAR 0.7, beats +1 s → ~1.7 words/s like the original) → look frames → set + prop agents → 8 section agents in parallel (dev/<sec> builds) → full board → fixes → code score → export.

**Why:** user wants a new channel style copied in look, animation and narration.
**How to apply:** reuse sets/props/kit for the next ifverse video; follow [[feedback-storyboard-before-render]]. Gotchas: plain `python3` is Homebrew 3.15 without faster-whisper — use /usr/bin/python3 and run voice.mjs with PATH=/usr/bin:$PATH; VoiceStudio fails on one-word lines ("Theo?") → generate in a sentence and cut.

Thumbnails: recipe in styles/ifverse/STYLE.md §Thumbnails; template pieces/cats-thumb (render with still.mjs, scale to 1280×720).

- Spec: fuentes/lowpolyshorts-style/especificacion-tecnica-del-estilo.md. Refs: "Ref lowpolyshorts/originales/" (top 7, git-ignored), measurements in _analisis/resumen.md.

- Tool: styles/zach3d/tools/spec_refs.py <refs> <fuentes> "<channel>" (API credits).
Related: [[project-zach3d-style]]

**Estado al 2026-10-29 (fin de la sesión):** el protagonista es el Kaneda comprado (pieces/lps-hombre/modelo-comprado/AkiraModels, git-ignorado), recoloreado: TODA la ropa azul cobalto y el emblema circular "punkpoly / shorts" en la espalda, con el rayo zigzag sobre un triángulo en el centro. Copia editada en pieces/lps-hombre/punk/ (Kaneda_punk.blend/.png, make_punk.py). El usuario lo aprobó. La moto también quedó hecha (punk/bike/Bike_punk.blend: cobalto + stickers PUNK/POLY/SHORTS, sin marcas reales). Pendiente: el primer video. El personaje hecho desde cero (out/, build_char.py) queda de respaldo.

**Decisiones del usuario (2026-10-29):** la moto NO va en todos los shorts — solo en casos especiales o cuando el short trata de verdad de una moto. Voz del narrador: perfil "mathomaly" de VoiceStudio. Antes del primer video pidió un análisis de @LowPolyShorts y canales similares (@PlipStories, @BigDanBaby y otros) para una estrategia de publicación de alto potencial viral adaptada al estilo low poly.
Estrategia escrita en fuentes/lowpolyshorts-style/estrategia-publicacion.md (4 pilares, 3/semana, primeros 10 títulos; recomendado #1 "You've Never Seen Your Own Face").

**Video #1 (2026-10-30):** pieces/lps-own-face renderizado (38.7 s, EN, sin música, sonido pro), pendiente del OK final del usuario. Reusar para los próximos: lpskit.py (Letters3D, Kaneda swap/recolor, sets), fuente propia fonts/PunkPoly-Black.ttf (el usuario pidió letras facetadas + pixeladas como el título de LPS; pixelado en post.py), revisión del storyboard antes de render. Ver pieces/lps-own-face/LOG.md.

**Feedback del usuario sobre el video #1 (2026-10-30), aplica a todos los punkpolyshorts:** voz = perfil "3d cartoon" de VoiceStudio (227af074), NO mathomaly (más animada); SIEMPRE música de fondo bajo la voz; el final NO se corta para loop (la frase termina completa); cámara siempre en movimiento rápido (punch-ins, órbitas, dutch, shake — helpers en pieces/lps-own-face/build.py); clones recoloreados de Kaneda como extras están bien.

**Más feedback (2026-10-30, v3-v4), para todos los punkpolyshorts:**
- Música: Bert Cole, que es el compositor de LPS. Pack gratis 16-Bit Starter Pack; el usuario eligió "Waiting".
  - Nivel MUY bajo: música −36 LUFS y SFX −35 LUFS en un master de −14 (voz ~−15); sin ambiencias. OJO: mix.py de real-sound MASTERIZA la cama a −14 LUFS salvo --no-master; si después se suma la voz, usar --no-master o los cambios de nivel no llegan (pasó en lps-own-face v3–v5).
  - Crédito: "Music composed by Bert Cole — bitbybitsound.com".
- Voz: perfil "3d cartoon" + EQ retro de LPS (pieces/lps-own-face/voice/retro_eq.py) + 3 dB sobre el resto. SFX bajos.
- Comas habladas: si el TTS las corre, generar el tramo aparte con punto (con coma sale como pregunta) y unir con pausa.
- Vertex wobble (snap GN, K.ps1_snap) con grilla de 240 filas; la de 640 no se ve a 1080.
- Expresiones deadpan, una clara por plano, como LPS: stern / nervous (gota de sudor) / skeptic en make_faces.py. "tired" con ojeras no se entendió.
- Personajes secundarios distintos entre sí y que ACTÚEN (p. ej., sacar las fotos); las cabezas con foto se pintan en 3D (pieces/lps-own-face/tex/paint_heads.py) para que no parezcan máscara.

**CONFIG APROBADA (2026-10-30). El usuario dijo "guarda esta configuración para los siguientes videos":** empezar cada punkpolyshort copiando pieces/lps-own-face.
- Copiar: build.py, lpskit.py, post.py, assemble.py, voice/retro_eq.py, out/audio-review/mix_variant.sh y finish_v2.py.
- Niveles finales:
  - voz +7 dB sobre la cama;
  - música "Waiting" de Bert Cole a unos −25 LUFS en un master de −14;
  - SFX a unos −35 LUFS;
  - sin ambiencias.
  - MASTER MÁS FUERTE (pedido 2026-10-31 tras lps-onoda, que salió a −14 LUFS / −2.1 dBTP): desde el video #3, master a ~−11 LUFS con limitador a −1 dBTP, manteniendo las mismas proporciones voz/música/SFX.
- Wobble con grilla de 240 filas.
- Cuadros de pared VARIADOS (2026-11-02): no solo memes; también random tipo Coraje/Bob Esponja (retratos 'gross-up' del propio personaje), realismo raro, cosas random, videojuegos cualquiera.
- SETS CON SENTIDO (corrección 2026-11-04, Erfurt): nada de vacíos negros ni escenas simbólicas que no se entiendan; cada plano = lugar concreto y legible con profundidad (fondo, piso, paredes, cielo). PS1 low poly ≠ plano y pobre: geometría con volumen, luz con dirección, set dressing. Cielo = FOTO real de cielo con nubes puesta de fondo (como LPS), no nubes 3D ni procedurales (corrección 2026-11-04). Personajes nunca flotando (pies/manos en contacto). Multitudes con caras y expresiones variadas. Ningún plano demasiado corto para leerse.
- DITHER PS1 SIEMPRE (aprobado 2026-11-01): cada frame crudo pasa por ps1_post() de pieces/lps-lowpoly-test/photoprop.py (1/4 de resolución, Bayer 4x4, color 15-bit, nearest x4) ANTES de los subtítulos (post.py), que quedan nítidos. Comparación: pieces/lps-onoda/review/dither.
- Props y partes de escenarios desde UNA foto de referencia de Flow (fondo magenta, de frente) con photoprop.prepare()/loft() (guía VLVT); mostrar un fotograma de prueba antes.
- Easter eggs: cuadros cómicos en las paredes de cada set, con el helper egg() de build.py y la carpeta tex/eggs (224 px).
  - Se pueden usar memes reales de internet; el derecho de autor no le importa.
  - También sirven parodias hechas con Flow.
  - Le gustaron: Harold "ME IN EVERY PHOTO", "Mirror of the month", la selfie de la Mona Lisa, la torta de 1977 y "Family photo (arm's length)".
  - No le gustó "ME / ALSO ME (BACKWARDS)".
- El usuario escucha en QuickTime, porque VS Code no reproduce audio: abrir los renders con `open -a "QuickTime Player"`.
- **Para el video #2 en adelante (2026-10-30):**
  - Wobble: vuelve a la grilla de 240 filas. La de 180 se probó en Onoda y el usuario la pidió más baja (2026-10-31).
  - Más expresiones de Kaneda por video, todas las que el guion permita: nuevas texturas en make_faces.py y cambios dentro del plano.
  - Más personajes secundarios distintos que actúen.
  - Foto de perfil del canal: pieces/lps-own-face/avatar (avatar.py + post_avatar.py; fondo de fuego y CRT, aprobada).
- Carteles, cuadros y pantallas siempre llevan imágenes reales de internet o con un toque cómico (memes, fotos reales: un panda real, el Bigfoot de Patterson-Gimlin). Dibujos procedurales solo como último recurso.
- Enumeraciones de la voz ("one year, ten, twenty"): generarlas con pausas leves entre cada ítem; si el TTS las corre, generar cada ítem aparte.

**2026-11-04 PIVOT:** new shorts = exactly like @zawpolyshorts (159K subs, cat-behaviour shorts "Your Cat Thinks You're X When You Y", 3–20M views) but with a DOG protagonist, same low-poly PS1 style. Notes: fuentes/zawpolyshorts-style/ (look: big yellow captions with black stroke, crude human owner, cosy home sets, cat with tears/expressions, "Zaw Poly Shorts" graffiti signature). Dog build learned from 4 tutorials in fuentes/blender-lowpoly-perro/ (half-model + Mirror from a side photo, UV + painted texture; Rigify "Wolf" metarig or hand armature with IK legs + poles; walk cycle keyed, looped in NLA, follow-path). Erfurt #4 left at "CASI" (14 issues in its _revision.md), parked.
**Dog channel rules (2026-11-05):** dog = pieces/zaw-dog-test/zaw_dog.blend (+README). Sets must REPLICATE ZawPolyShorts' sets: real low-poly modelled furniture/rooms in Blender (tutorial method: model from reference photo, UV + painted/PS1 texture), not odd code-generated shapes. Also replicate Zaw's camera moves (study their frames). First script: pieces/zaw-dog-01/guion.md (smell clock), approved.
**Dog look rule (2026-11-06):** the dog must look like a REAL dog (realistic proportions + photo-real fur/face, like zaw-dog-test faces2), never anime/toy; "cute" = cute real dog. One colour-consistent texture, no patches/stickers. v2 rig/walk/happy_wag approved.
**Dog channel BGM (2026-11-07, correction):** dog videos use ONLY Bert Cole "A Little R & R" (zaw-dog-01) or Bert Cole "Waiting" (Kaneda/punkpolyshorts). "Simpler Times" (used in zaw-dog-02) was rejected.
**Photo-humans (2026-11-07, correction):** arms must attach to the shoulders (no detached sleeves/gaps), visible real hands holding props (nothing floating), faces blended into the head and neck (no stuck-on mask, no doubled face).
**Correction (2026-11-07, zaw-dog-02 v3):** the opening bark must be audible but must NEVER mask the words. Place it in a gap or keep it around +3 dB over the voice, not +8. Voice a bit louder overall. People's hands are built from Flow photos (VLVT method), like the rest; never procedural code hands. The snack is a real bone-shaped biscuit.
**Channel name (2026-11-07):** the dog channel is "Doggo Poly Shorts" (not Pup Poly Shorts). Branding in pieces/pup-branding: avatar.png and banner_lps.png have no text; the wall tag/decal still says "Pup Poly" and needs updating if reused. Video 2 final was approved 2026-11-07.
**Set strategy (2026-11-07, analysis of all 21 Zaw shorts, fuentes/zawpolyshorts-style/escenarios.md):** Zaw reuses one fixed world. Each video uses 2-5 sets, and a new set appears only every 2-3 videos, for the hook. Ours: a reusable kit (living room, hallway + front door, bedroom, kitchen-dining, street, yard or park), plus at most 1 new hook set per video, which then joins the kit. Vary props, colours and light.

- Doggo camera (user correction 2026-11-09, video 4):
  - Use Zaw's varied angles: ~55% level at dog height, ~20% gentle high angle, ~16% humans at human height, top-down inserts for objects, at most 1 low angle per video.
  - The camera MOVES in every shot: push, pull, track, orbit or crane. Never all static.
  - The yellow 3D texts get ~1/11 cap-height edge steps and must stay readable.
  - Details: styles/zawdog/STYLE.md "Planos".

## memoria: `project-mitos-guiones.md`

---
name: project-mitos-guiones
description: Myth/fantasy narration series — 7 English scripts (~1100 chars, ~60s), visual style per theme, and the voice workflow
metadata:
  type: project
---

Series of ~60s narrated videos, English voice, scripts in `scripts/guiones.md` (project root). Topics: Odysseus (Polyphemus), Kratos (Greek + Norse God of War), Rhaenyra (House of the Dragon), Ned (Game of Thrones), Baldr, Prometheus, Harry Potter.

- Script pattern (from refs 2–5): open with the protagonist's first name, rising costs in short sentences, a "But"/"So" turn, close on a tragic or epic line. Use first names only in most scripts (the user: the audience recognises them).
- Visual style per theme (user, 2026-10-20): House of the Dragon and Game of Thrones → **Tapestry** (`styles/tapestry`, built on pieces/rhaenyra; slides right between scenes; men without red lips; music = the theme the user drops in Ref); God of War Greek era → amphora-bf as in pieces/kratos (see project-gow-greek-style); Harry Potter → undecided between the "Three Brothers" tale and the Marauder's Map look.
- The God of War Egypt saga was a mistake: the user means the Greek and Norse sagas.
- Voice workflow: Claude gives the plain script only; the user generates the voice; the user announces the file; then Claude builds the video.
- Facts checked: Egypt is a rumour only (PushSquare, 2026); Lucerys' death closes season 1 of HotD; Ned's execution is at Baelor, King's Landing, not Winterfell; Baldr and Harry details per the sources in the session.

**Why:** the user's brief for a series of varied myths and fantasy franchises. **How to apply:** keep ~1100 chars per script; reuse the amphora workflow when a script goes to a video.
- Rhaenyra Targaryen Theme (Ref amphora mitologia) always starts at 0:30; HotD mix: music gain +10, voice.music −1 (user, 2026-10-20).

## memoria: `project-odyssey-long.md`

---
name: odyssey-long
description: long-form pilot "The ENTIRE Odyssey, Told on a Greek Vase" (16:9, ~30 min, amphora-bf); state and approved look
metadata:
  type: project
---

Strategy approved 2026-10-29 (fuentes/estrategia-largos/estrategia-mitos-largos.md): whole myths, long-form, in the art of their era; shorts = chapters.
Piece: pieces/odyssey/. Script approved and humanized: script.md (15 chapters, ~5,100 words; ch 9 = Scylla short word for word, reuse its voice).

**Look approved 2026-10-30** (look/look2a.jpg) for the ch 3 Cyclops test:
- assets/bg.jpg 1920x1080 built from the Scylla vase: top meander (the bottom band flipped), picture y 90–922, wave + meander below.
- Flow layers in gen/ → cut/ (key.py): cyclops_sit, ody_offer (Odysseus as a traveller, no helmet; armour only in combat chapters), cave (16:9 set squashed to 1920x832 at y 90, floor ≈ y 850), ram. Refs in Flow: @{styleref} = kratos 1.jpeg at 900px; do NOT use odyref (Flow copies it).
- 5px orange ring on figures.
- Captions: SMALL, Dalek Pinpoint 40px, cream (240,222,190), soft black shadow (blur 3), NO white edge, centred at the bottom y≈868 just above the wave. The user rejected big captions with a white edge.

Ch 3 (Cyclops) 16:9 test EXPORTED 2026-10-30: pieces/odyssey-cyclops/renders/{final,share}.mp4, 4:38, −14.0 LUFS, TP −1.5; 28 panels, 54 voice lines (Mad 3, voice/trim.py). Awaiting user feedback; then the remaining chapters the same way.

Revision 1 (2026-10-30, user feedback):
- Music: the Odysseus bgm is copyrighted. Approved by the user ("genial", volume OK): "Temple of the Manes" by Kevin MacLeod (CC BY 4.0, harps and flutes in a mode), in audio/track_mix_greek.wav, mixed as 32-bit float. The alternative is "Noble Race" (track_mix.wav). Attribution goes in the YouTube description (audio/SFX_CREDITS.md).
- SFX are real CC0 Freesound recordings: audio/sfx_pro.wav, built by audio/tools/sfxmix.py from cues.py. They are premixed with the music into audio/track_mix.wav, and the code SFX in score.js are off.
- Slides (user, 2026-10-30): the incoming panel slides in over the previous one, opaque, carrying its own paper and with a soft shadow on its leading edge. The previous panel drifts 0.3W to the left. The incoming figures lean out over the seam (slideOverflow). The user rejected crossfaded sets. Final rule (user, 2026-10-30): the frieze should feel like ONE long strip moving right. Panels that are mostly paper (sea, ship, outdoors) move together on the same paper. Only full-set panels (FULL_SET: the cave) slide in over the previous one.
- Every sailor is his own layer, animated with crew().

**Parts → one video (2026-11-01):** each chapter group is its own piece (odyssey-p1 = ch 0–2, odyssey-cyclops = ch 3, …), approved and exported one by one, then concatenated into the single long video with continuous slides and a joint −14 LUFS master. Part 1 done (sonido pro, approved). Title + thumbnail + title-named mp4 ([[feedback-title-thumb-every-delivery]], [[feedback-render-filename-title]]) only on the final joined video, not on each part.

**Ground + voice (2026-11-01):** ground = Flow Nano Banana Pro recreation of the original (user-approved; a code-redrawn one was rejected): pieces/odyssey/assets/bg_flow_pro.jpg, copy as assets/bg.jpg in every part. Louder voice: music mix gain −6 in piece.json (voice ~4 dB over the bed).

## Chapter titles hold (2026-11-01)
From part 3 on, every chapter title card (e.g. "V · The Laestrygonians") stays on screen 1.5 s longer than in p1/p2. Parts 1–2 stay as exported (user said not to re-export).

**Part 3 (2026-11-01):** pieces/odyssey-p3 = ch 6 Circe + ch 7 Underworld, 48 panels, 5:00, 66 Mad 3 lines; board at pieces/odyssey/board/p3 (pending approval, no sound yet). New Flow layers in odyssey/cut/p3 (ring via odyssey-p3/tools/ring_p3.py); ghosts = layers at ~0.6 alpha + cream haze, solid after drinking. Flow MCP alternates "Could not remove the previous reference images" errors — just retry; check each download, it can lag one image.
Part 3 EXPORTED 2026-11-01: renders/{final,share}.mp4, 5:00, −14.0 LUFS, −2.1 dBTP; sound pro (80 CC0 Freesound files, credits in audio/SFX_CREDITS.md); voice.music −2 in piece.json (−1 gave 9 dB under speech; −2 gives ~10 dB like p2). Music gain in piece.json has no effect on the ratio (export normalises the score).

**Part 4 (2026-11-01):** pieces/odyssey-p4 = ch 8 Sirens + ch 9 Scylla/Charybdis + ch 10 Cattle of the Sun, 48 panels, 4:49, 60 Mad 3 lines; board at pieces/odyssey/board/p4 (pending approval, no sound yet). New Flow layers in odyssey/cut/p4; Scylla/necks/Charybdis/fig tree/armoured Odysseus reused from pieces/scylla (ring via odyssey-p4/tools/ring_p4.py). Ends on the DC → I tally; part 5 starts with ch 11 Calypso.
Part 4 EXPORTED 2026-11-01 (board approved as is): renders/{final,share}.mp4, 4:49, −14.1 LUFS, ≈ −2.5 dBTP (export audio + alimiter −3 dBFS, re-muxed from frames). Sound pro: 84 CC0 Freesound files (credits in audio/SFX_CREDITS.md); Sirens = real female humming/vocal recordings; premix music −2.7 dB / SFX +7.3 dB so voice-over-bed in speech = 3.7 dB on the stems, same as p3.

**Part 5 (2026-11-01):** pieces/odyssey-p5 = ch 11 Calypso + ch 12 Phaeacians (ends "just as the Cyclops had prayed"), 43 panels, 3:19 (short: these chapters have less text), 45 Mad 3 lines; board at pieces/odyssey/board/p5 (pending approval, no sound yet). New Flow layers in odyssey/cut/p5 (ring via odyssey-p5/tools/ring_p5.py). Strip rule used: a character repeated in consecutive strip panels stands further right in the second, so he is never on screen twice. Part 6 = ch 13–14.
Part 5 EXPORTED 2026-11-02: renders/{final,share}.mp4, 3:20, −14.1 LUFS, −1.5 dBTP (alimiter −2.5 dBFS on export audio). User: no nudity ever (Odysseus gets a ragged loincloth: ody_crawl/ody_branch redone by Flow edit); "Phaeacians" was misheard by Whisper — real spelling + comma ("The Phaeacians, sat…") gave the clearest take (phonetic spellings were worse). Sound pro: 80 CC0 files (credits audio/SFX_CREDITS.md); premix music −2.7 / SFX +8.6 → 3.7 dB voice-over-bed on export stems (audio/tools/stemratio.py). The style animates on 2s, so a pop scan shows slide "jumps" on even frames only — expected.

**Part 6 (2026-11-02, last part):** pieces/odyssey-p6 = ch 13 Ithaca + ch 14 Penelope's Bed + AMPHORUS sign-off card (apple + gold logo, not spoken), 63 panels, 4:59, 62 Mad 3 lines; board at pieces/odyssey/board/p6 (pending approval, no sound yet). 24 new Flow layers in odyssey/cut/p6 (ring_p6.py also turns coloured fills black). Nano Banana Pro timed out in Flow this session → most layers are Nano Banana 2. Card slides now fade out of the old card any character the new card also shows (WHO() aliases in scenes.js), so nobody appears twice.
Part 6 EXPORTED 2026-11-02 (board approved as is + AMPHORUS end card held 10 s longer for YouTube end-screen, calm slow drift, music fades last 5 s): renders/{final,share}.mp4, 5:09.2, −14.1 LUFS master (−14.2 in the mp4), −1.5 dBTP; sound pro 85 CC0 files (credits audio/SFX_CREDITS.md), premix music −1.9 / SFX +9.4 → 3.7 dB voice-over-bed on stems. earshot critique launch-grade 0.946 (only flag: the fade-out ending, by request).

## memoria: `project-pov3d-hd-style.md`

---
name: project-pov3d-hd-style

New style `styles/pov3d-hd/` (2026-10-25), first piece `pieces/wave-grew` (8:30, EN, no voice, 1080p30, approved look + board).
- Refs in references/couldnt-stop/ (only the most-viewed videos count, user rule). Detail bar = Minute Zero "Jumped Higher" (4pjb8dBlTM0): lush trees, detailed houses, soft clouds, never faceted.
- HUD in glass panels (user likes the "twice as big" ylnTesFVoOo glass) + glass fact cards with record-vs-you bars; italic serif captions; teaser of a later moment at 0:00 (Minute Zero trick).
- End card ends with "relax, this could never happen... / could it?" (EN of the pov3d sign-off).
- BGM: user picks by tone — comic → Ethernight Club, awe/epic → Floating Cities (K. MacLeod, CC BY). Sound = "sonido pro" pipeline ([[feedback-earshot-sfx]]).
- Build: core3d.js (wave, rider, camera) by the lead + one stage file per agent (AGENTS.md contract); export ~4 h with 5 workers.
- Thumbnails (refs' 2M-view ones): no HUD panels; one giant left block = small-caps label / huge serif number (a real value from the video) / small-caps "AND STILL ..." / italic serif line bottom-left; subject on the right half, left darkened. Made with pieces/wave-grew/dev/thumb (THUMB mode + thumbcam.js down-the-line camera), 1280x720 via still --scale 0.6667.
**How to apply:** start the next "couldn't stop" video from pieces/wave-grew; check topics on YouTube first (search script in references/couldnt-stop/search*).

**Character variant (luckier, 2026-10-31):** start from pieces/luckier — src/char.js (chBuild/chPose/chExtra for sculpted extras), one set file per agent. The shared hero rig must be re-added to the active scene every frame (export workers render out of order). Music: comic → Ethernight Club, epic → Floating Cities. Exports are ~2.8 MB/frame PNG (~43 GB for 8:30): render in chunks + encode/delete (pieces/luckier/renders/seg/run.sh) when the disk is tight.

## memoria: `project-tapestry-style.md`

---
name: project-tapestry-style
description: tapestry style = the approved look for every House of the Dragon and Game of Thrones video (pieces/rhaenyra is the reference)
metadata:
  type: project
---

Every House of the Dragon / Game of Thrones video uses `styles/tapestry` **with the Flow method** (approved 2026-10-21): Nano Banana layers via the Flow MCP, animated in code. Start from `pieces/rhaenyra-flow` (scenes, assets/bg.jpg, score, piece.json); the full method is in styles/tapestry/STYLE.md → The Flow method. `pieces/rhaenyra` (all drawn in code) is the older variant.
- Look: embroidered linen with an imperfect weave; borders top (y 58–268) and bottom (y 1652–1862); stitched Herculanum captions at y 470, alternating red and navy; figures with layered clothes, detailed faces and stitched hair locks; dragons on an S spine; the Iron Throne as a chair of swords; wiggle on 3s.
- Scene changes: always a 0.8s slide to the right along one strip (no cuts); Bayeux trees as dividers.
- Rules from the user: men have no red lips (`male: true`); changes of pose must be gradual (no jumps); the end card is the apple close above AMPHORUS in gold capitals with a shine (no stitch dots).
- Sound: English voice cut at word gaps; music = the theme the user drops in `Ref amphora mitologia/`, loudnorm −14, gain +10, voice.music −1, a 0.5s dip before the payoff. The Rhaenyra Targaryen Theme always starts at 0:30.
- Always show the look and the storyboard before exporting ([[feedback-storyboard-before-render]]).

**Why:** the user's approval of the Rhaenyra piece. **How to apply:** Ned (GoT) and any later HotD/GoT script; see [[project-mitos-guiones]] and styles/tapestry/STYLE.md.

- Flow method rules (user): poses must swap seamlessly (posepair.py: only the changed limb fades); moving props are their own Flow sprite, the same one throughout (e.g. the falling crown = the worn crown); nothing ever pops in; figures fully opaque, entering by walking from the sides; fire without square edges.

Style `styles/yokai/` made 2026-10-22 from `Ref earlobe horror/` (5 reels, #5 the main ref). First piece: `pieces/jorogumo` (75 s, English on-screen paragraphs, no voice, no badge top-left).

User's standing notes for this look: lots of detail everywhere; very pixelated (216×384 render) + cel shading (MeshToon 3 bands); muted, dark, cold teal with fog and dithered gradients — but keep warm browns, don't go fully cyan; creatures must be weird and unsettling, never cute (noh mask, long neck, mask splitting into eyes); the card image = a legend-style print (Flow Nano Banana Pro, Edo woodblock look) shown very pixelated in a striped frame.

**Opening hook (user, 2026-10-22):** the first shot must show the creature clearly: still dark, but big in frame, silhouetted or rim-lit against lighter fog or sky, with its defining feature visible. Jorōgumo's opening was too murky. Reference accounts: TikTok @earlobehuman (the style itself) and @theredarchivesyt (creature ideas + hook grammar, adapted to yokai). Downloads and analysis in references/tiktok/, hook rules in styles/yokai/STYLE.md.

**Look correction (2026-10-25):** the "oppressive" feel is a regular 2×2 warm dot screen over mid-tones (YK.DOT), not darkness; no vignette ever. See STYLE.md.

**Quality bar (user, 2026-10-22): jorogumo's level is the minimum for this style; future pieces improve on it.** Full rules in styles/yokai/STYLE.md.

**Current bar (2026-10-25): pieces/behemoth** — start new pieces from it; full checklist in [[feedback-yokai-rules]].

**How to apply:** start new yokai pieces from pieces/behemoth (or styles/yokai/template/, jorogumo's source); sound = Commons recordings + code layer in sound/mix.py. Local ffmpeg lacks drawtext → run review from a copy of review.mjs with the drawtext filters removed. Related: [[feedback-flow-mcp]], [[feedback-pov3d-sound-synth]].

## memoria: `project-zelda-fairy.md`

---
name: project-zelda-fairy
description: Zelda OoT remake Short "The boy without a fairy" — bright woven tapestry, hieroglyphic woven figures, Mad 3 voice, AMPHORUS sign-off
metadata:

---

pieces/zelda-fairy (9:16, EN, 1:05.8, 14 panels). Golden frame fixed (assets/bg.jpg, Flow), the field slides right; Link is one strip actor (never twice on screen, pose crossfades across seams).
- User 2026-11-02: KEEP the colours, the border, the falling leaves. REJECTED anime-looking characters: all figures must be flat, semi-hieroglyphic WOVEN figures like sleeping Link in Ref Zelda2/Zelda3 (simple woven shapes, rust/cream thread outlines, no anime shading), woven INTO the cloth (tools/weave.py presses the bg weave in + thin cream edge). Flow trick: reference @{zeldaclose} "ONLY as a style reference" + "completely flat solid magenta, no texture" or Flow copies the ref with its background; derive all other figures from @{linkstand}.
- Magenta clothing gets keyed out: recolour (Zelda's tabard → wine red) before keying.
- Voice: Mad 3 via local TTS 127.0.0.1:3900 (Odyssey ref), speed 0.9, seeds 7/21, voice/{gen,score,trim}.py. Hook "You know the Hero of Time…" approved as an exception to the first-name rule. End: AMPHORUS + apple, small "Beyond time, the boy becomes a hero" under it. Music: the user provides it.
- Round 3 (user): figures STILL too anime → exact design language of the sleeping Link crop (refs/sleeplink_full.jpg as @{wovenlink}): flat woven shapes, eye = ONE line, mitten hands, flat band belt, simple boots, no sleeves/folds; Ganondorf = flat silhouette. Base figure gen3/link.jpg (@{linkbase}); other figures derived from it, then Flow edits to strip leftover eyes/brows. Side border bands REMOVED (only top/bottom). End card: apple higher, AMPHORUS plaque right under it, small line below.
- Round 4 (user): still anime → NEVER use character names in Flow prompts (they pull Nintendo renders); describe generically + "crude naive figure woven into coarse wool tapestry, Bayeux/hieroglyph, few flat colour blobs"; refs = only ref crops (refs/sleeplink_full.jpg, tree_ref.jpg, band_ref.jpg, Zelda4). Bands = woven figure frieze tiled from one period (gen4/band.jpg). Flow MCP often 'Timeout 5000ms' with 2 refs → new project / single ref.
- **v4 APPROVED (2026-11-02)**: pieces/zelda-fairy (gen4 layers, board/). v5 rustic variant (pieces/zelda-fairy-v5, gen5, board_v5) REJECTED: the near-literal copy of the sleeping-Link ref was unreadable (an orange blob), poses misaligned for crossfades. Do not use v5.
- Sound: sonido pro from odyssey-p6 audio/tools (CC0 Freesound + earshot screen); music supplied by the user (not sourced).
- EXPORTED 2026-11-02: renders/'Link Slept 7 Years and Woke Up a Hero.mp4' + share.mp4, 1:05.8, -14.0 LUFS, -1.1 dBTP. Music = user's "Zelda's Lullaby cover.mp3" from 0:30 (audio/track.wav), premix music -3.7 / SFX +9.4 -> voice 3.9 dB over bed. Sound pro: 26 CC0 Freesound + Odyssey libs (audio/SFX_CREDITS.md); rejected AI-ish drones (earshot 'likely code-synthesized'). P12 red wash now fades with the slide (was a pop). Package in youtube.md. (board/board.md); no sound/export yet.

## Captions position (2026-11-02)
For the NEXT Zelda tapestry videos, place the subtitles lower than in zelda-fairy: there was too much gap between the captions and the elements at the bottom. zelda-fairy itself stays as exported.

Este cambia las fuentes, el caption y los gráficos: fondo crema plano, título serif blanco en minúsculas palabra por palabra, caption gris translúcido, collage recortado con parallax, burbujas de chat. Todo lo medido abajo sale de la copia 1080p de la ref. **APROBADO 2026-11-12 ("quedó excelente"): nivel mínimo = réplica McDonald's, `pieces/ali-abdaal-2-test/storyboard/v1/board_1-5.jpg` + `storyboard/v1/motion_test.mp4`.** No hizo falta el render de 55 s. Fase 2 (contenido propio: raw de Ashton) en `storyboard/ash_v1/`.

# Ali Abdaal 2: análisis de la ref

## Fuente y material
- Ref: IG `C_QLaqdI0Wd`; IG da 720x1280. Mismo short en YouTube: `3Uuwe4BxYJE`, 1080x1920, 29.97 fps, 55.31 s. Se usa este.
- `fuentes/ali-abdaal-2/`:
  - `reel_yt.mp4` (master), `reel_ig.mp4`, `r/words.json` (Whisper);
  - `frames30/w_*.md`: análisis por API de TODOS los frames a 29.97 fps, en ventanas de 3 s;
  - `captions_ocr.md`: los 61 chunks de caption con su primer frame (OCR por API);
  - `cuts.txt`, `diffs.json`, `sheets/` (hojas por frame y recortes 1080), `hi/` (frames 1080);
  - `tools/`: diffs, sheet, grab, strip, fontsheet, framelevel, capocr, capbox.
- Análisis cuadro a cuadro en `CATALOGO.md` (25 planos, 8 tipos).

## Ritmo
- 41 cortes en 55.3 s (un plano cada 1.35 s). TH 77 % del tiempo, collage 23 % en 5 bloques (P07, P09, P11-12, P16-22).
- Jump cuts de TH: alternan encuadre abierto y punch-in de x1.08, x1.18, x1.22 o x1.38. El salto de escala ocurre en el frame exacto del corte; no hay zoom animado sobre el TH.
- Transiciones:
  - TH <-> collage: **corte seco siempre** (0 frames, sin blur, sin flash).
  - Una sola transición con desenfoque, TH -> TH en 3.27-3.37 s: f98 plano viejo a 8 px, f99 nuevo a 25 px, f100 a 12 px, f101 nítido.
  - Entre planos de gráficos: nunca corte seco. Se usa un **paneo en parallax** (P09) o un **push lateral** (P11->P12).

## Cadencia
- **Gráficos a 12 fps** (patrón 3-2-3-2 sobre 29.97; poses en f466, 469, 471, 474...): capas del collage, cámara, sobres, cajas de burbuja, barras de resaltado.
- **A 29.97 fps (suave):** TH, aparición de cada palabra del título, subrayado ondulado, relleno de palabras del caption.
- **Motas de tinta:** el patrón cambia cada ~15 frames en las pausas y en cada paso cuando hay movimiento.
- **Boil de recorte:** tótem, coche y sobres tiemblan ±4-5 px y ±0.6-1.2° con una pose nueva por paso cuando están quietos.

## Color
| Uso | Valor |
|---|---|
| Fondo del collage | crema plano **#FFFBE8**, sin degradado ni viñeta en el master |
| Motas | tinta negra, 3-90 px por mancha, ~1100 px oscuros por frame |
| Caption | caja negra al **30 %**, texto blanco al 93 % (dicho) / 38 % (no dicho) |
| Subrayado ondulado | amarillo **#FFCF3C** hasta el 30 % del largo, transición hasta el 48 %, luego azul **#46A0FF** |
| Burbujas | naranja **#FF950F** (izquierda), azul **#07A2FF** (derecha), texto negro |
| Barra "Monday" | rojo **#EF5838** (el del sobre) |

## Nivel aprobado y reglas (2026-11-12)
- **Barra de calidad:** storyboard v1 + motion_test.mp4 de la réplica McDonald's. Cada pieza nueva se compara contra eso.
- **Método aprobado:** copiar la ref 1:1 con medidas por frame (cajas de texto, keyframes de capas, colores muestreados) y cambiar solo los assets.
- **Fuentes del estilo:** Instrument Serif (trazo 1.25 %, espacio ×0.75) para títulos; Neue Haas Display Bold (-3 %) para la palabra con barra; FreeSans Bold para captions (70 px) y burbujas (49 px).
- **Fondo crema plano #FFFBE8 sin viñeta**, motas de tinta del overlay del usuario por encima de todo (caption incluido) en los collages.
- **Captions solo en TH y en collages de sujeto/paneo**; nunca en los planos de objeto + palabra con barra ni durante el chat.
- **Gráficos a 12 fps**; TH, palabras del título, subrayado y relleno del caption a 29.97 fps.
- **TH <-> collage con corte seco**; entre planos de gráficos, paneo en parallax o push lateral, nunca corte seco.

## Reglas heredadas del estilo Ali Abdaal (aplican)
- Todo por capas con movimiento propio y parallax medido.
- Nunca corte seco entre planos de gráficos.
- Los recortes que tocan un borde siguen fuera del cuadro; recortes sin halo (alpha erosionado 1 px).
- SFX solo en eventos reales, sin shimmer.
- Ningún frame negro; el salto de escala del TH cae en el frame del corte.
- Imágenes solo de Google Flow (srz-google-flow-mcp, cuenta tiktokeeuu691), verificando cada archivo: en esta sesión Flow devolvió imágenes viejas de otro proyecto y hubo que abrir un proyecto nuevo.

## Pipeline (pieces/ali-abdaal-2-test)
1. `prep/assets.py`: recortes Flow -> `assets/img/*.png` (rembg birefnet-general, alpha erosionado 1 px).
2. `prep/specks.py`: overlay de motas del usuario (`Overlays/a-dirty-film-texture...mp4`, rotado a 9:16), filtrado al tamaño y la densidad de la ref -> `assets/specks_clean/`.
3. `prep/board.py`: todo es función del tiempo absoluto de la ref.
   - `board` genera el storyboard (ref | nuestro + notas);
   - `motion` genera la prueba lado a lado con el audio de la ref;
   - `frame T` genera un frame suelto.
4. Fase final, pendiente de OK: render completo de 55 s desde el mismo `render(T)`, audio, -14 LUFS, revisar_render, earshot.
