## v3b (2026-11-11): reglas generales del usuario. MANDAN sobre lo anterior
Storyboard en `pieces/docucollage-test/storyboard/v3b/`, código en `prep/board3b.py` (escenas como funciones de t: el board y la prueba en video salen del mismo código) y `prep/assets3b.py`.
- **Todo por capas, nunca una foto entera de fondo.** Fondo plano (color + brillo) como capa propia, escenario (casas, piso, gradas, banco) en otra y personaje en otra, cada una con su movimiento.
  - Parallax medido en la ref: título 1.4-1.5x (o fijo en la zona segura), sujeto 1.0, escenario 0.45-0.6, fondo 0.15-0.3, primer plano (gradas/espectadores) 1.5x.
  - ARR Jane: la mujer sube desde +620 px (decay 0.62 por paso) y crece 0.8→1.0; la mansión sube 180 px a la vez y luego queda casi quieta (±10 px).
  - GOLD P20: ráfaga +3/+7/+6/+3/+5 % en 5 pasos; el estadio recibe el 45 % del zoom.
  - GOLD P10: entra a x1.3 con pan 186 px y blur 12/8/4/1.5, asienta en 5 pasos y luego pull-out -2.4 %/s.
  - JAM P53: la cabeza a color es una capa aparte sobre el cuerpo B/N y se mueve sola (±3.5° de inclinación, ±10-25 px).
- **Grunge encima de casi todos los planos de motion graphics**: textura de papel del usuario (`Overlays/scracth bueno que cambia.mp4`) × motas (`Overlays/grunge 1.mp4` invertido), en multiply al 22-32 %. Cambia cada 2 pasos y deriva 36 px/s. Va debajo del host y de la píldora. Frames en `assets/grunge/g_###.png`.
- **Fondos con brillo blanco suave** en el centro, un poco arriba o a la izquierda (S19). Es una elipse con smoothstep en ambos extremos (sin borde visible), al 8-17 % (sol de S18: 55 %), con dither para que no haya banding. Puede oscurecerse hacia un lado (S19: -38 % a la derecha).
- **Fades a negro u oscuro siempre con mucho feather**: smoothstep^1.5-1.8 a lo largo de 640-1000 px, nunca un degradado lineal corto. Fade inferior de S22: 42 % máximo.
- **Halftone solo donde la ref lo tiene.** Puntos claros sobre fondos oscuros (navy, rojo, granate) y oscuros sobre fondos claros (cielo). Pitch 11-17 px a 1080 (el de 7 px era demasiado fino).
  - Lo tienen S06, S10, S13, S14, S15, S16, S17, S18, S19 y la pista B/N de S12.
  - No lo tienen S01, S07, S08, S11, S22 ni S24.
- **Recortes:** nunca se ve el borde de un recorte. Lo que toca un borde de su imagen fuente tiene que seguir fuera del cuadro durante todo el movimiento.
  - S01: cabeza y lado derecho siempre fuera.
  - S08: el brazo termina 340 px fuera.
  - S11: los pies nunca entran.
  - S07: el cuerpo termina detrás del mostrador.
  - S24: la cuerda va a un piton y cuelga fuera del borde inferior.
- **Títulos apilados juntos**: cada línea se apila por su caja de tinta. Hueco = 0.09 × cap (0.12-0.15 donde la ref es más suelta: S24, S11, S16).
  - Medido en la ref: 8-14 px (SYNDROME, CLIMB) y 29-30 px (MEDAL, DREAM). En v3 eran 37-86 px.
- **Grosor de la serif:** EB Garamond 800 + stroke del mismo color de round(size × 0.013) px (2 px a 150, 3 px a 230). Comparado con SYNDROME en `storyboard/v3b/font_weight_compare.jpg`. Bebas lleva +2 px.
- **Palabras héroe grandes**: llenan 930-990 px de ancho cuando hay margen (la ref llega a 930-967 px). Ejemplos: COMPANY, PRICE, YOUR CLUB, COACHES (240 px), NEEDS (~330 px), CASH, FREEDOM.
- **El color sigue al texto, no a la ref:** si la ref es triste (cielo rojo de LOST) y nuestra frase no lo es, se copian la composición y la técnica con otra paleta. S18 usa amanecer dorado, barrio con ventanas encendidas y silueta navy con borde dorado.

## v3c (2026-11-11): valores finales aprobados. MANDAN sobre v3b
Storyboard en `pieces/docucollage-test/storyboard/v3c/`, código en `prep/board3c.py`.
- **Wiggle del título (aprobado en title_test_v3b, vuelto a poner):** ruido suave Catmull-Rom por letra, 3.5 poses clave por segundo, 60 % de amplitud.
  - x = 0.6 × 0.029 × h y y = 0.6 × 0.055 × h, con h = 0.70 × tamaño de la fuente.
  - Solo posición, muestreado a 12 fps. Es la función `wiggle_xy` (mismo hash que `wiggle_test.html`).
  - Medido: desviación de 2.3/4.4 px y salto medio de 0.9/1.6 px por paso a 230 px. NO usar una pose aleatoria nueva en cada paso: eso es el wiggle rápido rechazado.
- **Shine:** una sola pasada de blanco casi puro (95 % hacia #FFFFFF) dentro de las letras. Perfil triangular-smoothstep de ±120 px, inclinado 105°, a 1300 px/s, al terminar el tipeo.
- **Grunge:** la textura de papel × motas del usuario en multiply. La opacidad efectiva queda en 31-45 % (ganancia 1.4 sobre los valores por escena). En la pared blanca de S03/S04 baja a ~10 % para que la pared siga blanca.
- **Halftone (FFT sobre DK 28.8 s y GOLD 13 s):** trama a 30° con un pitch de 7.9 px (DK) a 9.6 px (GOLD) a 1080. Usamos 8 px en las refs de DK (S10, S17, S19) y 9 px en el resto.
  - Fusión LINEAL: el punto suma (o resta) el mismo valor en R, G y B (+34 niveles sobre navy). No es multiply.
  - Puntos claros: a = 0.09-0.10, radio 0.25 del pitch.
  - Puntos oscuros sobre cielo o teal: a = 0.14-0.17, radio 0.30.
  - Comparado con zoom 2x contra la ref.
- **S13:** el fade de arriba termina en el navy de la ref, #111B29 (medido de y 0 a 80), nunca en negro.
- **S03/S04 = un solo plano continuo, como GOLD P04:**
  - Capas: pared BLANCA codificada (#EFEAE6 → #E2DCD5, brillo arriba a la izquierda) a profundidad 0.4, piso de madera gris con zócalo blanco a 0.55, niña al 93 % con los pies en el piso a 1.0, y "$5,000" a 1.45.
  - Copia de JESSICA medida frame a frame: color #F5B814, tinta de unos 100-110 px, centro en y 206. Se escribe de izquierda a derecha a 1370 px/s desde 0.12 s, con letras parciales en cada paso, y se queda quieto.
  - Después la cámara empuja con aceleración de ×1.0 a ×1.25 en 0.64 s y el texto sale por arriba por parallax (ref y 205 → -60).
  - Luego el abanico de billetes hace pop a ×1.28 durante 2 pasos y la medalla cae al pecho.
- **S22:** la copa más abajo (arriba en y 340). CASH queda en y 190 con el borde inferior metido detrás del dinero de la copa. TO INVEST va justificado exactamente al ancho de FREEDOM (opción `fit` de `tline`).
  - Tiempos de JAM P50: CASH sube con el papel (+260/+110/+30 px), FREEDOM aparece 190 px más abajo, la copa cae en 2 pasos con un rebote de 16 px y TO INVEST se teclea a 2.5 caracteres por paso.
- **S11:** AMOUNT de 970 px de ancho, como MEDAL (cap de unos 175 px). Está bien que el ramo tape una letra.
- **S24:** roca, escalador y cuerda forman UN grupo que pasa 700 px más allá de los bordes derecho e inferior. Entra junto desde +330 px y nunca se despega del borde con el pull-out.

## Final (2026-11-11, render v3c aprobado): pipeline plantilla para los próximos reels
- **Shine final:** a mitad de camino entre v3b y v3c. Va al 75 % hacia un blanco cálido #FFF8EA, con perfil smoothstep de ±170 px inclinado 105° y la velocidad de v3c (1300 px/s). Una sola pasada, 1 paso después de terminar el tipeo.
- **Todos los títulos** se teclean con el wiggle aprobado y luego hacen el shine. En los planos cortos la velocidad de tipeo sube sola, para que el título termine al 55 % de la duración del plano (`title()` en modo CTX).
- **Ajustes finales de escena:**
  - S15: sujeto x1.45 con la cabeza justo debajo del título, que arranca en y 170.
  - S17: sujeto 80 px más arriba.
  - S13: las dos líneas se teclean (no aparecen de golpe).
  - S24 termina como la ref P34: el grupo se hunde, el título sale volando hacia arriba y "LINK IN BIO" se teclea con shine.
- **Pipeline** (`pieces/docucollage-test`, copiar la carpeta para un reel nuevo):
  1. `prep/board3c.py board`: storyboard. Las escenas son funciones de t, con boards y láminas antes/después contra la ref.
  2. `prep/board3c.py motion`: prueba lado a lado con la ref.
  3. `prep/render3c.py`: pista de GRÁFICOS a 12 fps en RGBA → `assets/gfx3c.webm` (VP9 con alpha).
     - Los planos de collage son opacos.
     - Los planos de TH son transparentes, salvo el título y la franja oscura de arriba.
     - Los planos sin movimiento propio llevan push genérico (+4.5 %) y deblur de 10/5/2 px después del corte.
     - La lista de planos es `SHOTS`.
  4. `prep/gen3.py`: `index.html` de HyperFrames. Capas: TH `th_big.mp4` (z5) → gfx (z10) → recorte del host `cutout_big.webm` (z20: host abajo en S01-S02, delante del título en los TH, subida en S20) → píldora karaoke (z80, y por plano) → outro (z90).
     - Audio: voz 1.0, música 0.11 y SFX en los eventos (teclas en cada tipeo, pop, whoosh, rip, hit, shimmer en los shines).
  5. `npx --yes hyperframes@0.9.16 check`, luego `render`, luego `python tools/revisar_render.py --estilo docucollage <mp4>`, luego earshot (mezcla ~-14 LUFS).
- **Encuadres del TH:**
  - TH simple: `th_big.mp4` + `cutout_big.webm`.
  - TH con el título detrás de la cabeza: el encuadre "ancho" del board = `edit.mp4` recortado en (270, 548) a ×1.65. Se hace con un transform de GSAP sobre el wrapper `{x:-445.5, y:-904.2, scale:1.65, origin 0 0}`, con `cutout_fix.webm` y `th_blur.mp4` alineados.
  - La franja oscura de arriba (820 px, smoothstep) dura TODO el plano para que el neón no salte.
- **Mezcla:** HyperFrames saca -15 LUFS. Se suma +1 dB en el mux final (`ffmpeg -c:v copy -af volume=1.0dB`) → -14.0 LUFS y -0.6 dBTP.
  - earshot critique: launch-grade, 20 de 21 métricas. El único menor es la mezcla casi mono.
- **Render final v3c:** `pieces/docucollage-test/renders/docucollage-v3c-final.mp4` (copia en `pieces/Docucollage/`). Enviado a Telegram el 2026-11-11.
  - `revisar_render` marcó como fallos varias reglas del spec v1/v2 que el usuario cambió después: Besley, solo dorado, x ≤ 940, píldora solo en 900/1384, mano solo para marcas. No se tocaron.
  - Se corrigieron dos fallos reales: la barra al escalador de perfil y una cuña blanca en la roca (la textura salía de la zona de cielo de la foto).

## Regla (usuario, después de v3c-final): NUNCA corte seco entre planos de gráficos
- Cada cambio de plano de gráficos se hace capa por capa, como en la ref: lo anterior sale y lo nuevo entra desde abajo, escalonado.
  - Entrada, modelo S13/Jane: el fondo cambia en el corte.
    - El escenario sube (180-520 px, decay 0.55-0.6 por paso a 12 fps).
    - El sujeto sube 1 paso después (600-820 px, decay 0.5-0.6).
    - Los props hacen pop de a uno (escala 0.55 → 1.12 → 0.97 → 1, cada 1-1.5 pasos), con caída de 2 pasos + 16 px de rebote para objetos (jarras).
    - El título se teclea.
  - Salida, en los últimos min(0.34 s, 30 % del plano): ease-in de 100 / 560 / 1600 px por paso.
    - El título sale primero hacia arriba y el sujeto o escenario baja 1 paso después.
    - Lo que entra por un costado (brazo, banco de S02, hombre de S01) sale por ese mismo costado.
  - Con habla rápida (S01 → S02), la transición se hace corta pero escalonada: el título y el hombre salen a la izquierda en 4 pasos y el banco sube 1 paso después del cielo.
  - Excepciones (continuidad):
    - S12 → S12b es un punch-in de la misma foto.
    - S19 → S20: el collage queda congelado y el host sube encima.
    - S03 → S04 es un solo plano.
- Código: `E()`, `POP()`, `X()` y `title_x()` en `board3c.py`. Las salidas existen solo en el render final (`FINAL`), así que el board muestra el plano completo.
- **S06:** el documento baja, el lector sube, la lupa busca por la página siguiendo una trayectoria de 5 puntos y se detiene en la cláusula, y el aro rojo se dibuja en 4 pasos.
- **S14:** el balón gira a 40°/s (30 frames de `ball3d.py`). A 22.5°/s no se notaba en el render.
- **Grunge final:** la textura va centrada en su media, como soft-light, y no oscurece. Ganancia 0.4 sobre los valores por escena, apenas perceptible (±1-2 %). El usuario la bajó dos veces.
- **Sin SFX de shimmer en los shines.**
- **S20:** el host sube con un clip de alpha endurecido (`cutout_s20.webm`), para que el collage no se vea a través del balón.
- **Render final corregido** (transiciones capa por capa, S06/S08/S10/S14/S15/S18 dinámicos, grunge sutil, sin shimmer, S20 opaco): -14.0 LUFS y -0.6 dBTP.
  - earshot: launch-grade.
  - revisar_render: CASI. Lo que queda son reglas del spec viejo y frames de salida.
  - Los TH duran 0.12 s más allá de su corte, para que la pista de gráficos a 12 fps nunca deje ver negro (había 1 frame negro en 38.61).
- **S01 → S02** (ref P02, rechazado el push de tarjeta): el FONDO no se desliza, solo cambia de color hacia el cielo de S02 (crossfade de 5 pasos). Lo único que se desliza a la izquierda es el hombre + el título, con ease-in de 50/170/400/760/1300 px (el título va 1 paso adelante). El hombre es un recorte nuevo de Flow (`assets/img3b/medalman2.png`): cabeza y costados enteros en cuadro, piernas estiradas fuera del borde inferior. Así nunca se ve un borde cortado.
- **Vendedora (S07):** la costura sigue la línea REAL, trazada a mano sobre una grilla 2x: pelo sobre la camiseta en los hombros, borde interno de cada tirante y escote. Lleva antialias de ~1 px y el recorte erosionado 1 px (sin halo). El cuerpo B/N es el complemento exacto, sin piel de cuello. La capa de la cabeza lleva una falda de 10 px con los MISMOS píxeles B/N de la camiseta, invisible pero que evita huecos al inclinar (±1.8°, sin deslizar, cabeza ×1.0).

# f1motion: explainer collage con caras recortadas (vertical)

Referencia: reel IG `DdolSnYt_iX` ("F1 explicado", 181 s, 1080×1920, 24 fps). El original está en `fuentes/f1motion/ref/reel.mp4`.
El análisis cuadro a cuadro se hizo por la API en ventanas de 20 s a 4 fps (`fuentes/f1motion/ref/analysis/w_*.md`); la síntesis está en `SPEC_api.md`.
Las 16 capturas del usuario marcan lo que más le gusta.
Regla del usuario: copiar el lenguaje visual y el movimiento, pero sin marcas, equipos ni pilotos de F1. Todo se re-tematiza a fútbol y camisetas personalizadas (Stimulus).

## Medidas del reel

### Ritmo
- 97 planos en 181 s. Media 1.87 s, mediana 1.75 s. Ningún plano supera 3.5 s, salvo un scroll de tarjetas de 7 s.
- Reparto del tiempo:
  - Cabeza parlante (TH): 37 %.
  - Gráficos diseñados: 31 %.
  - Metraje encontrado en B/N: 32 %. Este estilo NO lo copia: con nuestro raw se reemplaza por más gráficos.
- Cada gráfico lo dispara una palabra:
  - nombre propio → cara sobre vehículo o cuerpo;
  - número o lista → cascada de filas;
  - fechas → calendario con stickers;
  - jerga → explicador pixel con pill y tab;
  - CTA o compra → tarjeta UI con cursor.

### Audio (earshot timeline, 0-60 s)
- Mezcla: -14.2 LUFS, true peak -1.6 dBTP, LRA 1.7 LU.
- Música:
  - 0-40 s: house/tech-house "confident & cool" de ~132 BPM, con vocal chops y celesta/glockenspiel.
  - Desde 40 s: corporate de pizzicato.
- Sincronía con los 57 cortes: el 63 % tiene un onset a ≤1 frame (el azar da 51 %) y el 93 % a ≤100 ms. La mediana es de 25 ms.
- SFX pocos y cortos:
  - bubble pops en entradas de pills y badges;
  - whoosh rápido en salidas de vehículos y cambios de escena;
  - clics en el cursor;
  - swells suaves en algunos cortes.
- No hay SFX en cada palabra.

### Paleta (muestreada de las capturas)
| Rol | Hex |
|---|---|
| Fondo gráfico | #FDFDFB |
| Tinta display / thin | #111111 / #222222 |
| Palabra fantasma (antes de decirse) | #C9C9C9 (reel #9A9A9A-#BBB) |
| Piso halftone teal | dots #5FB39C sobre #D6EFE8→#A9DACD (muestras #ABDACF→#72BFA9) |
| Tab teal | #86C9B8→#BFE6DA→transparente |
| Pill dorada | #F1DEA8→#E6C470→#DDB75A, borde #3D3A3F |
| Escena roja | #EA2C26; paralelogramos #B81D1A→#8E1512 |
| Sticky rojo / oro / teal | #F3413D→#F07C88 / #E3C675→#D7B159 / #8FD0BF→#4AAB90 |
| Círculo a mano | #E8312B o #3E9D86 (contrasta con el sticky) |
| Tarjeta UI / filas / clic | #151515 / #E6E3E6 / #3E9D86 |
| Barras crema de la lista | #FBF3E1 con dots #EED9A9 |

### Tipografía
| Rol | Reel | Nuestro (local/libre) | Tamaño a 1080 px |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lead-in fino ("let's do a") | geométrica fina en minúsculas | Poppins Light | 50-64 px, #222, centrado |
| Display ancho ("BREAKDOWN") | futurista extendida, unicase con n/d con muesca | **Turret Road ExtraBold** `scaleX(1.30)` + trazo de 2 px | 110-190 px, ajustada a ≤900 px de ancho |
| Pill | sans media, 2 líneas | Poppins Medium | 34 px |
| Captions TH | sans regular blanca, cortes duros | Poppins Regular | 50 px, y=420 (bajo el neón Stimulus) |
| Script sobre nombre | firma manuscrita | Photograph Signature (fuentes del usuario) | 130 px, -9°, blanco con borde #222 |

- Fuentes candidatas descartadas: Michroma, Krona One, Audiowide, Zen Dots, Akira, Grandis, Halenoir, Evogria. La hoja comparativa está en el scratchpad de la sesión del 2026-11-10.
- Revelado de palabras:
  - Todo el título está en gris fantasma desde el primer frame del plano.
  - Cada palabra pasa a tinta justo cuando se dice: 0.17 s, power1.out.
  - Las palabras finas además suben 6 px.

### Movimiento (frames a 24 fps)
- Entradas:
  - pill: scale 0.4→1 en 5 f con back.out(2.2) y bubble pop;
  - tab teal: wipe desde el centro (clip-path) en 6 f;
  - vehículo: entra desde la izquierda en 10 f con power3.out y sale en 5 f con power3.in;
  - sticker: peel en 7 f con back.out(1.6), desde la esquina inferior derecha;
  - círculo a mano: trazo en 7-10 f;
  - filas de lista: cascada de 2 f por fila.
- Cámara sobre gráficos:
  - push lento del +4-6 % en todo el plano;
  - zoom-out settle 1.32→1 con blur 12→0 px en 7 f al entrar;
  - pull-back al final (0.9, y -60) antes del corte;
  - zoom-through ×2.2 en power3.in hacia un elemento, para pasar al primer plano.
- Caras: bob de ±8-10 px con ciclo de 6 f (0.25 s), rotación de -4°/+5° y squash del 2.5 %. Las alas (chevrons) aletean ±8° en el mismo ciclo.
- Transiciones:
  - corte duro ≈72 %;
  - rack-focus con blur al entrar a TH ≈20 %;
  - whip/blur lateral;
  - peel;
  - pixel→real;
  - flash cuts de 2 f, raros.
- Sin crossfades.

### Zonas seguras (vertical)
- La UI de IG/TikTok tapa los 280 px de abajo y los 140 px de la derecha.
- Todo texto va entre y=168 y y=1330, y a la izquierda de x=940.
- Los pisos, pistas y la lista pueden invadir abajo, porque son decoración.

## Tipos de escena reutilizables
1. **name-on-vehicle**: la cara va en la ventana de un vehículo de lado, con mano 👍 (twemoji) y brazo amarillo. Abajo, piso teal halftone con reflejo al 28 %. Arriba, thin + display flanqueados por chevrons teal que aletean.
2. **jersey-callout**: camiseta de espalda (vector, damero verde Stimulus) con un círculo rojo a mano sobre el nombre. Pill dorada arriba.
3. **walker**: la cara va sobre un cuerpo de palitos con zapatillas y sombra elíptica teal que crece. La pila de palabras va alineada a la derecha (x 57-92 %).
   - Variante: cara gris en un octógono dorado con gafas pixel "deal with it" que caen con bounce.
4. **calendar-stickers**: cuadrícula inclinada -14° (líneas de 2 px #222, celdas de 560 px).
   - Entran 3 stickers con peel, fecha circulada, título display, ⏱ y 📍.
   - La cámara pasea de celda en celda (0.38 s, power2.inOut) y el sticker anterior baja al 25 %.
5. **red-stack**: fondo rojo con dots, paralelogramos en las esquinas, carril blanco con damero y cajas pixel que van y vienen. Pila de líneas display con borde blanco escalonado; cada línea pasa de rosa fantasma a blanco.
6. **face-on-kit**: la cara va sobre un torso de camiseta enorme (equivalente al casco y visor de F1), con piso gris halftone. Settle 1.35→1 al entrar y pull-back al final.
7. **pill-tab-pixel-road**: pill, tab teal con 2 líneas display y subtítulo fino, sobre una carretera gris con guiones que corren y un sprite pixel (camiseta, ✓, moneda).
8. **top-down-lane**: carril dorado vertical (x 405-675) con hairlines de velocidad. Una van vista desde arriba cae con blur, gira 180° ("both ways") y sale.
9. **manga-burst**: líneas radiales negras que se redibujan cada 0.1 s (3 variantes). Display tachado con trazo rojo, moneda pixel girando y pill.
10. **pixel-delivery**: van pixel con la cara real al volante, que llega a una casa pixel. Cae una caja con pop.
11. **talking-head**: el raw a pantalla completa con rack-focus de entrada (copia con gblur 22 que se desvanece en 0.22 s) y push del 6 %. Captions blancos finos de 1-3 palabras, con corte duro.
12. **ui-card-cursor**: tarjeta #151515 de radio 44 sobre un swoosh rojo a rayas.
    - Las filas entran en cascada; cada una lleva un sprite pixel y nombre display + script.
    - El botón cuadrado tiene sombra dura de 8 px.
    - El cursor se desliza 0.45 s y el clic pone el botón en teal.
13. **pixel-to-real**: el torso del presentador pasa de mosaico a real (36→22→12→6 px→real, 0.13 s por paso) con la cabeza siempre real. Encima van el script "at", el display "STIMULUS" y una cápsula que se abre desde el centro.
14. **strip-list**: 11 franjas con degradado de blanco a color, cada una con un sprite pixel, una barra crema halftone y un número fino 01-11. Las etiquetas aparecen en su palabra y la escena acaba en zoom-through.
15. **close-up-stack**: sprite pixel gigante y pila display a la derecha ("WE / REMAKE / IT."), con un subtítulo fino.
16. **cta-button**: pill "free design", tab "START YOUR REQUEST" y botón pill negro "LINK IN BIO →". El cursor hace clic y el botón pasa a teal. Luego viene el outro Stimulus deslizando encima (obligatorio, ver `styles/stimulus`).

## Sonido
- Voz: la del raw, limpia con afftdn 18, agate, compresión y -15 LUFS.
- Música: house con vox y campanas, como el reel. En la prueba se usó Freesound 277448 "vox and bells" (frankum, CC0): cama a 0.13 y outro a 0.30.
- SFX reales, todos verificados con earshot `rank`:
  - pops de `sound-layer/kit/pop`: 507006, 796298, 244657;
  - whooshes de `kit/whoosh`: 60004, 449988, 60011;
  - pase de auto: Freesound 19982;
  - sticker / cinta: 422727 y 245196;
  - marcador: `kit/paper` 428338;
  - clic: `kit/click` 399443;
  - moneda: kenney rpg coins;
  - riser: reverse cymbal 148930.
- Las tomas repetidas se rotan.

## Pipeline (HyperFrames)
1. `prep/face_cut.py`: recorte de solo la cabeza (gorra + cara) sobre `edit.mp4`.
   - Usa una máscara BiRefNet-portrait por una elipse que sigue el matte y corta en la barbilla.
   - Solo procesa los rangos que usan cara (~9 s por frame en CPU).
   - Sale `face.webm` con alfa; `face_gray.webm` se hace con `hue=s=0`.
2. `prep/torso.py`: un still del torso y sus variantes pixeladas.
3. `prep/gen.py`: genera `index.html`. Los SVG y sprites se escriben en Python, los tiempos salen de `words_edit.json` y los SFX se colocan por evento.
4. `npx hyperframes check`, luego `render --quality delivery`, luego `tools/revisar_render.py` y earshot `critique`.

## Prueba 1 (pieces/f1motion-test, 2026-11-10)
- Raw: stimulus-05 (37.7 s) con 16 escenas y el outro; dura 39.6 s. Hay 2 rondas de revisión.
  - Ronda 1: `revisar_render` dio CASI.
  - Correcciones: fecha del sticker tapada por el badge, cursor sobre el botón equivocado, texto pasado de x=940, restos de capucha bajo la barbilla (`prep/face_clean.py`), el pixel "13" ahora es "12" y los captions están sincronizados.
- earshot critique: launch-grade, 21/23 métricas. Quedan dos menores: mezcla casi mono (música CC0 mono) y poco sub.
- Pendiente para el siguiente: música estéreo con más graves. En manga-burst falta un vehículo de frente con líneas de velocidad, como el "300 KMPH" del reel.

## Reglas v2 (correcciones del usuario, 2026-11-10) — OBLIGATORIAS
- **Gráficos a 12 fps (en dos).** Medido en el reel: en las escenas gráficas cambia 1 de cada 2 frames a 24 fps (25/45, 25/47, 19/36 frames únicos). El talking head y los b-roll van a 24 fps completos.
  - Render con `--fps 24` y `data-fps="24"`.
  - Todo tween gráfico va en `tlg`. Un tween conductor en `tl` lo busca en la grilla de 1/12 s: `tlg.totalTime(floor(t*12)/12)`, dentro de su ease, que corre en cada seek.
  - Las caras se reprocesan a `face*12.webm` con `fps=12,fps=24` (exacto 24, alineado a la grilla).
  - Bobs y aleteos: medio ciclo de 1/6 s.
- **B-roll en B/N ≈32 % de los planos.** Clips de YouTube con yt-dlp: niños jugando, entrenadores, árbitros.
  - Tratamiento: recorte 9:16, gris, contraste 1.3, grano 7, trama de líneas, blur de 2 frames al entrar.
  - Caption Poppins SemiBold 110 px, blanco, alineado a la izquierda en x=114, y≈1110, con sombra suave. Pasa de gris a blanco en 3 frames.
  - La trama medida en el reel son **líneas VERTICALES**, no horizontales: periodo 8 px, perfil sinusoidal ±7.5 niveles (≈ ±10 %), estática (fase constante). Se replicó tal cual.
- **Nada técnico dibujado en código.** Vehículos, camisetas, zapatillas, balón, caja, casa, moneda, chevrons teal, mano 👍 con brazo y mano del corazón se generan en **Google Flow** (srz-google-flow-mcp, Nano Banana Pro).
  - Se usan recortes del reel como referencia de estilo (`pieces/f1motion-test/flow/ref`, el F1 car = look vector brillante).
  - El fondo se quita con rembg birefnet-general (`prep/flow_cut.py`).
  - Los sprites pixel son las imágenes de Flow pasadas a mosaico NEAREST de ~26 bloques, recoloreadas (`prep/assets2.py`).
- **Caras siempre en B/N** en las composiciones.
  - El brazo de la mano 👍 pasa **por detrás** de la cabeza (capa z15 bajo la cara z20).
  - En camisetas, la barbilla entra en el cuello en V. Se usa `jersey_front_open.png`, con el interior y la parte trasera del cuello transparentes.
- **Calendario:** los stickers van DENTRO de las celdas de la cuadrícula (celda 600 px, sticker 596 px alineado a la línea). La cámara pasa a la celda vecina de la misma fila.
- **Walker** (como 55.png):
  - octágono dorado con degradado #EBD49A→#D4AE55 y borde #3A3A3A;
  - cara en B/N que lo llena (470 px de alto);
  - gafas pixel que caen con bounce;
  - brazos negros finos que salen del vértice inferior, balón en una mano (Flow) y mano del corazón en la otra (Flow);
  - piernas curvas en degradado #6F6F6F→#E2E2E2, de 13 px, cada una girando en su cadera (`svgOrigin`);
  - zapatillas Flow que se deslizan con el pie y elipse teal bajo los pies;
  - texto a la derecha (borde x=930): dos líneas thin de 44 px, la palabra héroe display de 112 px y la segunda display de 78 px, de gris a tinta palabra por palabra.
- **Camiseta del jersey-callout:** de Flow, más arriba (y=560), reflejada en el piso halftone teal como el vehículo de la apertura. El reflejo es una copia con `scaleY(-1)`, origen 50 % 50 % y máscara "to bottom".
- Texto display ajustado a ≤760 px de ancho (zona segura x≤940).

## Reglas v3 (feedback del usuario, 2026-11-10)
- **FPS remedido.** Revisé 18 tramos del reel (motion por correlación de fase entre frames).
  - En todas las escenas gráficas hay movimiento real exactamente cada 2 frames a 24 fps, y los frames intermedios son idénticos: **12 fps fijos, no variables**.
  - Las escenas a 24 fps son grabaciones de pantalla o scrolls (42-45 s, 47-50 s, lista 116-121 s, final 171-176 s).
  - La sensación de "posterize más lento" viene de los saltos grandes por paso y de las pausas largas al final de cada ease. Se mantiene 12 fps.
- Chevrons pegados a la línea thin: 6-8 px del texto.
- **Círculos de marcador:** el trazo se dibuja (dashoffset por el plugin `attr`: `attr:{"stroke-dashoffset":1→0}`; el tween CSS no funcionaba).
- **Cabeza sobre cuerpo:** siempre dentro del octágono dorado, como el walker del reel. La camiseta cuelga del vértice inferior del octágono; nada de cara pegada sobre un cuello.
- **Sombra bajo los pies:** elipse con degradado #3FAE8A→#7FCFB3→#C9EDE0 de izquierda a derecha y bordes suaves (máscara radial).
- B-roll: elegir planos donde el sujeto no quede cortado en el borde (una camisa blanca cortada se lee como un borde blanco). Recorte con un 6 % de zoom extra. TODOS los b-roll llevan caption.
- **Peel del sticker** (reel 67.2 s y 75.75 s): la nota entra con una esquina doblada gigante, brillante y con degradado del color oscuro al blanco, que se repliega hacia abajo a la derecha.
  - En 0.5 s pasa de 560 a 70 px con power2.out, mientras la nota baja de 118 % a 100 %.
  - Después la esquina queda levantada y respira (70↔95 px, ciclo de 1/3 s).
  - Se hace con clip-path polygon en el cuerpo y un polygon SVG para el doblez.
- Poner un talking head real (con blur de entrada y captions finos) también a los ~10 s: más presencia del presentador entre gráficos.
- La línea vertical del tab teal se desvanece en los extremos igual que el degradado: `.tab::before` con un degradado vertical.
- Primer plano "WE REMAKE IT.": camiseta de Flow sin pixelar, de pie sobre el piso teal con reflejo, y la pila display arriba a la derecha.
- Las caras, el torso pixel→real incluido, siempre en B/N.
- Vehículos coherentes: lateral, cenital y frontal son el mismo modelo, generado en Flow con la van lateral como referencia. Se borran los logos de marcas reales (el frontal traía uno).
- Display: `letter-spacing: .035em`, para que "IT" y "TI" no se peguen.
- **Música:** recursos del usuario permitidos. v3 usa "Dr Delight – Feel It (instrumental)" de `D:\Alan\...\Audios musica Fiesta`.
  - Funk / tech house, "confident & cool", vocal chop, celesta y pizzicato; es la más cercana al reel según earshot compare.
  - Estéreo, con más graves, a partir de 4 s.

## Reglas v4 (feedback del usuario, 2026-11-10)
- **Bordes blancos del b-roll.** La causa era el SAR no cuadrado que deja el recorte con ffmpeg (p. ej. 51611:51750): HyperFrames lo encaja con `contain` y deja 2 px blancos a cada lado.
  - Siempre `setsar=1` al final del filtro y `object-fit:cover` en el `<video>`.
  - Verificar las columnas 0-3 y 1076-1079 del render: no deben valer ~252.
- **Esquina curvada del sticker** (reel 75.7-76.6 s, cuadro a cuadro). Es un rollo de página curvo, no un triángulo:
  - lados cóncavos que terminan en una punta;
  - el borde del pliegue abombado hacia la esquina;
  - degradado color claro → banda blanca brillante (≈22 %) → color → tono oscuro en la punta;
  - línea de brillo blanca justo dentro del borde y sombra suave (feDropShadow −6/−4, blur 7, 28 %);
  - la página se corta siguiendo el mismo pliegue curvo: clipPath SVG con `path` animado por `attr` (un clip-path CSS `path()` no se anima en GSAP).
  - Movimiento: de 640 a 78 px en 0.5 s con power2.out (6 pasos a 12 fps); luego respira entre 78 y 96 px.
- "at STIMULUS": el ícono del logo Stimulus (de `styles/stimulus/assets/logo_lockup.png`, en #111) entra girando de −200° a 0° y de escala 0 a 1 en 0.42 s con back.out(1.7), en lugar del torso.
- **Walker:**
  - los brazos también son trazos plateados con degradado (#5E5E5E en el hombro → #DCDCDC en la mano), de 11 px, como las piernas;
  - las gafas caen UNA sola vez: van en su propio wrapper interno (el bob del cuerpo va en el externo), con power3.out y sin bounce.
- **Cabeza en la ventana de la van:**
  - máscara con la forma exacta del vidrio (`van_window_mask.png`, medida por píxeles grises de baja saturación) y fondo de cabina oscuro (#4A5666→#1A1F26) detrás de la cara;
  - un reflejo de vidrio encima, la puerta y el marco por delante: la capa baja se corta en el umbral real (y=226) y es transparente dentro de la ventana;
  - cabeza de 185 px, centrada en la ventana y al 62 % de su altura.

## Regla v5 (2026-11-10): posterize de 8 fps en gráficos, zooms y transiciones (preferencia del usuario sobre los 12 medidos)
- Todos los tweens van en `tlg`, buscado a `floor(t*8)/8`: gráficos, cámaras, push-ins y settles del talking head, y fades de transición. Inicios y duraciones van a la grilla de 1/8 s.
- El contenido de video (talking head y b-roll) sigue a 24 fps por dentro; las caras recortadas se reprocesan a `face*8.webm` (`fps=8,fps=24`).
- Bobs y aleteos: medio ciclo de 1/4 s (2 pasos).
- Se mantienen las frenadas largas (ease-out).
- Verificado en el render: patrón `..x..x` (8 fps) en las escenas gráficas.

## FINAL APROBADO (2026-11-10): v4 + 12 fps
- **12 fps final; 8 fps se probó y se rechazó.**
  - Todos los tweens (gráficos, cámaras, push-ins del TH y transiciones) van en `tlg`, buscado a floor(t*12)/12.
  - Caras a `face*12.webm`; bob con medio ciclo de 1/6 s.
  - El contenido de video sigue a 24 fps.
- Pieza aprobada: `pieces/f1motion-test` (render final `renders/f1motion-test.mp4`, enviado a Telegram). Es la plantilla para los siguientes videos de este estilo.

# gta6 — loading-screen key art in parallax layers

Vice-City-at-sunset key art (hand-painted comic, bold ink, cel shading) cut into Google Flow layers and moved in code with depth parallax, **everything stepped at 12 fps**. Made from `fuentes/gta6-style/` (reel by sanji.chien) + the user's beach-bar still. Look test: `pieces/gta6-look` (v2 art; start new pieces from its `src/main.html` + `tools/key.py`). v1 art (flat comic, rejected as "AI-made, ugly") is kept in `assets_v1/` and `src/main_v1.html`.

## Legal / originality
- No real people (no lookalikes, no names in prompts), no Rockstar/GTA logos, no Pricedown font, no copies of the GTA VI characters. Fictional cities only ("Miami-like beach city"), no "Vice City"/"Leonida" text on screen.
- Our title lettering: heavy condensed caps (Impact family), white→cream fill, thick near-black outline `#140818`, hard plum drop shadow `#2A1036`, tilted -4°, + yellow sticker tag `#FFE14D`.

## Palette (hex)
| Role | Hex |
|---|---|
| Sunset sky top / hot pink | `#EC5F8E` → `#EC797D` |
| Sunset mid / peach | `#F4A27A` |
| Horizon / pale yellow sun | `#FBE7A6` |
| Palm silhouettes, lilac | `#6E5A9E` (inner `#8C7BC0`) |
| Shadows, lavender-purple | `#6C4969`, deep `#422734` |
| Day sky turquoise | `#8CAABA` / `#5FB8C4` |
| Buildings lavender / mint | `#A78C9C`, `#BFE3D6` |
| Neon pink / cyan | `#FF5FA2`, `#5FE6FF` |
| Teal shirt (hero) | `#4FA39A` |
| Ink | `#211E26` |
| Skin warm rim | `#F08A4B` |

## Rendering traits (from the official refs in `fuentes/gta6-style/refs/`)
- Semi-realistic proportions and faces: real anatomy, asymmetric features, wrinkles, pores, stubble, hairy forearms, tattoos; realistic hands.
- Thin dark contour, heavier on the silhouette, light on interior forms; faces modelled with fine painted lines, not comic hatching.
- Posterized hard-edged light shapes: sunlit skin/cloth bleached to pale cream-yellow; shadows saturated pink-magenta-violet; thin cyan bounce on the shadow edge.
- Character more saturated and contrasted than the background; the background is a pastel haze (lavender, mint, peach, cyan) with airbrushed gradients and less detail.
- Composition: cropped at chest/waist (or knees for full-body poses), low camera, slight wide angle, props in the foreground (table, bottles, map, car hood), character leaning towards the lens.
- Expressions: cool, bored, unimpressed, mid-sentence; never a posed smile.
- The reel adds a halftone + grain print layer; the official art is clean, so keep halftone subtle (soft-light 25 %).

## Flow recipe — the winner (v2, 2026-11-13)
Tested: (A) Nano Banana Pro + refs, isolated on magenta → flat comic look; (B) NB Pro text-only → better colour, still comic; (C) NB Pro refs + text → comic; (D) **Nano Banana 2 + refs + text → best composition, props and faces**; (E) D + a relight edit → closest to the official art. Pro ignores the refs' rendering; NB2 follows them.
1. New Flow project; upload 3–4 official artworks as `gtaref1..4` (character art: Brian Heder, Cal Hampton, Jason & Lucia motel, Real Dimez; for backgrounds the Vice City BG).
2. **Full scene with the character in it, Nano Banana 2** (never ask for an isolated character first: magenta isolation turns everything into sticker-comic):
```
Painting technique reference (technique only, never copy people, faces, poses, props, labels or places):
@{gtaref1} @{gtaref2} @{gtaref4}. Make a new Grand Theft Auto VI style loading-screen artwork: polished
semi-realistic digital painting, not a cartoon or comic. No logos, no readable text.
Subject (new original <man|woman>): <age, ethnicity, build, ASYMMETRIC face details: crooked nose, scar,
heavy eyelids, stubble, wrinkles>, <outfit>. Pose: <body turned 30°, leaning on X, holding Y with natural
relaxed fingers, head to viewer, bored unimpressed look>. Framing: cropped at <mid-chest to waist>, camera
slightly below eye level. Foreground: <prop>. Background, softer and pastel: <place details>.
Lighting: hard low sunset sun from the left, lit skin and cloth bleached to pale cream-yellow with sharp
light-shape edges, shadows saturated pink-magenta-violet, thin cyan rim light, smooth airbrushed gradients,
dark contour on silhouettes, fine painted wrinkles, pores and stubble.
```
3. **Relight edit** (upload the result under your own name, e.g. `barman`; Flow's auto names get truncated):
`Edit @{barman}: keep the man, face, pose, hands, clothes and composition exactly the same. Only repaint the light and colour to match @{gtaref2}: hard low sunset sun from the left; lit skin and cloth bleached to pale cream-yellow with sharp-edged light shapes; every shadow saturated pink-magenta and violet; thin cyan rim; more contrast on the man; background pushed into a soft pastel lavender, mint and peach haze; smoother painterly shading, fewer interior ink lines, crisp dark contour on the outer silhouette.`
4. **Split into layers by editing the same image** (alignment is pixel-exact):
   - Character layer: `Edit @{x}: keep the <man + the counter corner> exactly as they are (same pixels, position, size). Replace everything else with a perfectly flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF. No shadow, no gradient, no glow.`
   - Clean plate: `Edit @{x}: remove the man completely and paint in what was behind him … same camera, composition, lighting and style. No people.`
5. Backgrounds without people: NB2 + `@{gtaref5}` (Vice City BG) + `@{gtaref3}`, "painting technique only, do not copy the buildings, signs, layout or text", "leave the lower-middle open for a character".
6. Second character on an existing plate: `Edit @{street}: keep the street … exactly the same, and add in the foreground <new character + car> painted in the technique of @{gtaref4} and @{gtaref3}` → then the magenta edit for the layer. The plate itself stays the background, so the layer lands at offset 0.
- Never: real names or lookalikes, Jason/Lucia faces, Rockstar logos, labels copied from the refs (NB2 copied "AZAS" beer once: check props), car badges (ask to remove the emblem).
- Self-check every character before using it: 5 fingers and real knuckles, asymmetric face, no plastic skin, line weight close to the refs, cream highlights + pink shadows present.
- `python tools/key.py in.jpg out.png magenta|green` → full-frame RGBA; check on a cyan sheet.

## v3 — photo base + code (`styles/gta6/tools/rockstarize.py`, 2026-11-13)
Human method (21DPS time-lapse, notes in `fuentes/gta6-style/vice-city-vacation-gta-vi-art-style-study.md`, target frame `fuentes/gta6-style/tutorial/final.png`): line sketch → flat colour per material → hard pink/violet shadow shapes → soft modelling on arms → flat lavender silhouettes for the background → props → **global warm yellow-pink grade** → shirt print and arm hair last.
Measured tutorial palette: skin lit `#C07A77`/salmon, skin shadow `#7F404E`→magenta, shirt `#386076` / `#1F3D51`, tee `#C7D3CD` / `#78818E`, sky `#E7E29F` / `#F4F1CB`, pennants `#C08CB7`, table `#614F7A`, rim glow `#F3F3C4`.

Pipeline:
1. Flow **Nano Banana Pro photoreal photo** of the full scene (real face and hands; ask for a hard low sun from camera-left in front, a crisp shadow line down the face; avoid backlight: a backlit face posterizes into mud).
2. NB2 edits of that photo: (a) person (+ the props they touch) on flat magenta, (b) clean plate without the person.
3. Figure: `python rockstarize.py layer.jpg out.png --mode figure --key magenta`. It keys, smooths with bilateral passes (keeps the face), cuts 3 light bands from a heavily simplified luminance with smooth vector-like borders, flattens the shading inside each band while keeping material contrast and fine detail, lifts and tints the shadows magenta-violet, turns orange skin salmon, adds cream lights, a 26 % sunset gradient map, thin Canny ink (long edges only), a 4 px silhouette line, a pale-yellow rim glow on the sun side and an inner warm edge.
4. Backgrounds: **code `--mode bg` looked like camouflage; use an NB2 repaint edit of the clean photo plate instead**: `Edit @{plate}: keep the exact composition … repaint the whole photo as a flat background of a GTA VI loading-screen illustration, exactly like the background of @{tutref} …`. It keeps the geometry, so the figure's counter/car still line up.
- Verdict so far: the code figures lose the AI look and keep real anatomy, but still read as a **filtered photo**: shadow shapes follow photo lighting rather than drawn form, clothes keep photo texture. A Flow repaint of the same photo with `@{tutref}` (hybrid) is cleaner but drifts back to generic comic and changes the face. Next tuning ideas: segment skin/cloth and posterize each with its own thresholds, replace clothing texture with a flat tone + redrawn print, take the shadow shapes from a depth/normal estimate instead of the photo luminance.

## Saturation default (user, 2026-11-13)
More saturation than the official art on everything: characters ×1.25 Lab chroma (`finish_character.py` `finish.saturation`, default 1.25), plates/backgrounds ×1.25 (`cut_layer.py --plate --sat 1.25`), layers cut from artworks ×1.25 (`cut_layer.py`).

## 16:9 tests with the official cast (private, not for publishing)
- `pieces/gta6-parallax-16x9`: loading-screen parallax, 20.5 s, redrawn new-pose characters (Jason aiming, Lucia looking back, Cal with binoculars, DreQuan with cash) over Flow clean plates of the official BGs; never put a waist-up character over a plate with a big near prop (lifeguard tower, giant sunglasses): scale breaks. (First version used cut-outs: `src/main_cutouts.html`.) Plates ("Edit @{art}: remove the man completely and paint in what was behind him … keep everything else exactly the same") or the official empty BGs. Bg swap for standing characters, push transition (new plate slides in from the left, the character follows ~6 frames later with out-back) for seated ones/props. 16:9 push-in only +5.5 % (+2 % creep): the official crops are tight.
- `pieces/gta6-boxart-16x9`: box-art comic grid, 20 s: 8 redrawn panels + title panel, thick ink border, slam/slide entries with a white impact flash and a 2-frame page shake, plate + character parallax inside each panel (`make_panels.py` crops with a 10 % margin; no Flow plate → inpainted plate, only edges show).
- Per-character proof: `pieces/gta6-16x9/compare/<pose>.jpg` = official art | new pose + SFace score (`compare_poses.py`). The Flow turnaround sheets (`sheets/`) were rejected (AI look, faces drift): don't use them.

## Official cast in new poses + identity check (2026-11-13, private tests)
Cut-outs of the official art don't count: every shot is a redrawn new pose. Per character (configs `styles/gta6/characters/poses/*.json`, all inherit `pose_base.json` with an auto palette from the photo's own colours):
1. Identity anchor = a crop of the official 4K artwork around the face (`pieces/gta6-16x9/id/<name>.jpg`), attached at EVERY Flow step.
2. Photo base (NB Pro, 16:9): "Photorealistic cinematic photograph … The exact man in @{id<name>} as a real person: same face, hair, tattoos, outfit. New pose: … one hard low sun from camera-left …". Describe the face in words too (round fleshy face, droopy moustache…), but never exaggerate the build (Cal came out heavier).
3. `make_character.py` block-in → 4. NB2 render pass, short prompt: "Edit @{bk<name>}: keep composition, pose, silhouette, hands, flat lavender background and the light/shadow shapes. Repaint it as an official loading-screen illustration of exactly the man in this reference @{id<name>}: same face (…), same outfit (…), exactly the same painting technique as the reference: smooth airbrushed shading, large clean light and shadow shapes, very few thin lines, no hatching, no sketchy strokes, dark contour only on the outer silhouette, realistic hands. No text, no logos." (long prompts with 3 refs make the Flow MCP time out: keep 2 refs, short text; start a new Flow project when uploads stop resolving).
5. `finish_character.py` (key, relight, saturation ×1.25).
- **Identity gate** `python styles/gta6/tools/face_id.py <img> --char <name> [--cx 0.4]` (YuNet + SFace ONNX, anchors in `characters/official_ids.json`): PASS = cosine ≥ 0.45 AND the character ranks 1st among all 9 official faces. Calibration on the official art: same person 0.51–0.62, different people 0.08–0.48. Photos usually land 0.36–0.48; the render pass with the official art attached raises them to 0.51–0.60. Reject and retry below the gate.
- When the photo route drifts (Cal: 0.37), a **direct pose edit of the official artwork** ("Edit @{idcal}: keep this exact man … change only the pose …") scored 0.53 and looks closest; use it as the fallback (no block-in → finish runs without the alpha prior).
- Necklaces/props: say "plain gold chains, no letters" (Flow invents names).

## Identity anchors, build and clean cutouts (rules from 2026-11-13, apply always)
- **Multi-reference anchor**: collect all official art + screenshots of a character (`fuentes/gta6-style/refs_lucia/` = 4 artworks + 13 screenshots from rockstargames.com/VI/media, git-ignored). `official_ids.json` holds painted anchors (`lucia`) and screenshot anchors (`lucia_shots`); `_gates` sets per-character thresholds (Lucia: painted ≥ 0.48 AND screenshots ≥ 0.38, rank 1). Per Flow generation attach the 2 best refs: photo step = 2 screenshots (best face likeness), render pass = 1 screenshot for identity + 1 painted artwork for technique (that mix scored 0.55 / 0.49; two painted refs gave 0.50 / 0.30).
- **Build**: describe the body exactly as the official art shows it (Cal: big round beer belly, broad soft chest, thick arms, "do not slim him"); never write a build word you have not checked. Check with `pieces/gta6-16x9/build_ratio.py` (chest width / face width: official Cal 4.55, accepted 4.40, the slim one 3.08).
- **Cutout QA** (`styles/gta6/tools/qa_cutout.py`, runs automatically at the end of `finish_character.py`, writes `<out>_final_qa.jpg`): detects flat leftover key colour (also enclosed pockets and pixels that were key in `<name>_painted.jpg`), graded-lavender leftovers touching transparency, bright magenta fringes, holes, specks; `--fix` makes residual transparent, despills edge chroma toward the inner colour, cleans the pale glow on the shadow side (`--fringe-side`), removes specks, chokes 1 px. PASS = residual < 0.05 % and fringe < 3 % of the edge. Layers that wear lilac (white car + lilac jacket) need `--no-band` / `finish.qa_no_band`. Before using any layer in a piece: `python qa_cutout.py assets/*.png --fix --sheet qa.jpg` and look at the sheet (black / white / green / marks).
- Leave head-room: if the head touches the frame top in the Flow image, scale the layer ~0.85 about the bottom before using it (Cal).

## v4: making a character (current recipe, 2026-11-13)
Method from three tutorials (`fuentes/gta6-style/proceso-rockstar-3-tutoriales.md`): the Rockstar portraits are **paint-overs of a reference photo**: clean line art, flat colour per material, **dual split lighting** (warm key on one side, cool/pink light on the other, core shadow between), two tones first and then soft value transitions inside each, AO under nose/eyes/lip, a thick silhouette line, warm grade and noise. Tools in `styles/gta6/tools/`, one JSON per character in `styles/gta6/characters/` (`barman.json`, `woman_car.json` are the worked examples). Look test: `pieces/gta6-look` (v4 assets in `assets/`, v3 kept in `assets_v3/` + `src/main_v3.html`).

1. **Reference photo** (Flow, `srz-google-flow-mcp`, Nano Banana Pro, 9:16, one image): the full scene with the person, photoreal, ONE hard low sun from the side, crisp shadow line on the face, no backlight. Write the face as a character, not a model: asymmetric brows, crooked nose, scar, mole, wrinkles, freckles; "five clearly separated relaxed fingers". Prompts: see `flow4/` file names, or copy the barman/woman prompts from this repo's history.
2. **Config** (copy `barman.json`): `photo`, `out`, `sun` (left/right = which side the photo is lit from), `upper` (one garment, or two that k-means splits), `add` = props/extra garments: `poly` (photo pixels, like the Pluma tool: glass, keys, car) with `keep` (fingers on top) or `under` (only free pixels), `box` + GrabCut, `within` (relabel part of a material, e.g. the tee inside "upper"). Per material: `colors` {shadow, key, hi, rim, deep}, `key` (lit share), `hi_frac`, `rim` (share for the second light), `deep_frac` + `ao_only`, `photo_w` (photo light vs designed normals), `shape_smooth`/`angular`/`min_area` (shape design), `model` (soft modelling inside zones), `print` (vector palm fronds), `mode` (`glass`, `posterize`). `flow` {subject, face, extra} feeds the render-pass prompt. `finish` {shadow, light, split_bias, rim, grade, noise}.
3. **Block-in**: `.venv/bin/python styles/gta6/tools/make_character.py styles/gta6/characters/<name>.json [--debug]` → `<out>.png` (code-only RGBA layer), `<out>_flat.jpg` (block-in on the flat key `#D8B4E0`), `<out>_flow_prompt.txt`, `--debug` adds the material map. First run downloads the 3 ONNX models (~550 MB, `models/`, git-ignored). ~20 s.
4. **Render pass** (Flow NB2, one image): upload `<out>_flat.jpg` as `blockin`, the photo as `photo`, an official artwork as `gtaref` (character art: Brian Heder); paste `<out>_flow_prompt.txt`, aspect 9:16, model 2. Check: same face as the photo, five fingers, props intact (a bad prop in the block-in comes back mangled: fix its `poly` first).
5. **Finish**: `.venv/bin/python styles/gta6/tools/finish_character.py styles/gta6/characters/<name>.json <painted.jpg>` → `<out>_final.png` 1072×1920 RGBA (alpha = flood-fill of the key from the border, protected by the block-in alpha; multiply magenta shadows + screen cream lights to push the split light back; silhouette heavier on the shadow side; rim; gradient map; noise). Drop it into the piece's `assets/` as a full-frame layer at offset 0.
6. **Background** (Flow NB2, no people): upload `tutorial/final.png` as `tutref` + the Vice City BG as `bgref`, "background technique only, never copy buildings/signs/text", leave the lower middle open, sun on the same side as the character.
- Time per new character: ~15–20 min (photo 1 min, config + prop polygons 10 min, block-in 20 s, Flow pass 1 min, finish 5 s, review).
- Code-only (`<out>.png`) works as a fallback without Flow for the character, but it reads as a vector trace / posterized photo; the Flow pass on top of the block-in is what makes it look painted. Flow straight on the photo (same prompt, no block-in) goes back to generic comic: always paint over the block-in.
- Known limits: the Flow pass softens the hard sun (finish pushes it back only partly); small faces (full-body shots) lose detail in the block-in, but the Flow pass restores them from `@{photo}`.

## Motion rules
- **12 fps stepped**: render at 24 fps but quantise time `T = floor(t*12)/12` for **everything, camera included** (measured on the ref: odd frames identical). Only a meta move (shrink to split screen, UI overlay) may run on 1s.
- **Depths** (zoom exponent `cam.z^(0.35 + 1.3·d)`, pan × `0.3 + d`): plate 0.1–0.15 · hero cut from the same image 0.3 (keep it at offset 0 and scale 1 so its counter/props line up with the plate) · top fronds 1.0. A layer cut from its plate (woman+car) gets the same depth and the same push as the plate.
- **Shot open:** ease-out push-in ≈ +10 % in 0.8–1.1 s while the foreground flies in (fronds drop −420 px from above, cash rises +520 px from below, hero rises 160 px), then a slow creep (+3 % over the shot) and small idle bob/sway (5–8 px sine) on characters and overlays.
- **Background swap (ref 4.0–4.8 s):** foreground overlays leave first (in-cubic, up / down), old plate exits up (0.5 s), new plate rises from below (out-cubic, 0.6 s, starts 0.25 s after), character stays with a tiny −18 px lift.
- **Character swap (ref 6.0–6.8 s):** new element enters from the left with out-back overshoot (0.5 s) and shoves the old one off to the right (in-cubic); the second new element follows 4–8 frames later.
- Shot length 2–3.5 s; a new push-in after every swap.
- Text: our title pops in with out-back (0.3 s) and leaves before the swap; subtitles small, white, bottom-centre, one or two words.

## Sound (not in the look test yet)
- Ref: voice-over + ad-style music, whooshes on swaps, -14 LUFS. For us: "sonido pro" (Freesound/Commons → real-sfx → earshot) with whooshes on each swap, a cash flutter on the bills, a soft riser into the title; music = 80s synth/trap-ish groove, no copyrighted GTA tracks.

## `styles/ifverse/STYLE.md`

# ifverse — "What If…?" stickman stories

Long-form (≥ 8 min) 16:9 YouTube stories in the manner of @IfverseTales, all in code. Analysis of the source and the full spec: `ANALISIS.md`. First piece (the proof): `pieces/ten-seconds`.

## The look
- **Flat cards at real depth, filmed by a camera** (`ivStage(layers)`): each layer is drawn flat and placed at a depth d (1 = the actors' plane, 2–6 far, 0.5–0.7 foreground). Far layers pan 1/d as much, zoom 1+(z−1)/d and go soft with depth of field (`IV.dof`); blurred layers render at half resolution.
- **Film:** mood tint, vignette, black cinema bars (62 px at 1080). **No grain** (`IV.grain = 0`; the user saw it and the reference is clean). `ivPost()` is `STYLE.post`.
- **Stick people** (`ivMan`): black round head (R = 0.125 h), black limbs (0.034 h), one-colour clothes (hoodie, jacket, suit, uniform, cardigan, coat, vest, tee), cream eyes and mouth, a **warm rim light** from the mood's key (a silhouette pass nudged toward the light). Hair/hats: puffs, bun, pony, tuft, buscap, cap; glasses.
- **Faces:** eyes open / happy / wide (pupil) / squint / angry / sad / tired / dots / closed; brows angry / sad / up; mouths smile / grin / flat / o / frown / open / smirk; the speaker's mouth follows its VOICE words (`talk: id`); the narrator has no mouth. **Blink every 3.5–4 s, 3 frames.**
- **Hands change with shot size:** nub (wide) → mitten (medium) → five-finger glove (close-up); grips open / fist / point / hold / flat; `hold: { R|L|front|back: (x, y, ang, h) => prop }`.
- **Moods (`IV_MOOD`):** sunset, lunch, day, night, rain, lamp, office (+ arcade, party, hall, school from the sets). One mood per scene.
- **The ghost** (`ivGhost(fn, a)`): anything drawn in fn becomes a cyan hologram (luminance recoloured cyan, glow, 1-px jitter). Cyan = the device (the future) and the running counter only.
- **Type:** rounded bold caps (`IV.font`), cream with a warm glow (`ivTitle`, `ivTag`, `ivText`); `ivCounter` bottom-centre.

## Motion (measured from the source + the guide)
- **Motion on 1s** (`STYLE.ones = true`), no motion blur. Gestures 4–6 frames with a hard stop (`ivPoseMix` + `EZ.o3`). Walks: `ivWalk` (5 frames a step, planted feet).
- **Camera almost still:** close-ups never move; ~⅓ of wides get `ivPush(t0, 0.03, 1.8)` and stop. No shake (one 6-frame jolt allowed on the biggest hit).
- **Cuts:** hard cuts only, 3 frames before the word (`CUT(id, word)`); ~25–29 shots a minute; a shot under 0.45 s is dropped (main.js).

## Story and voice
- Title "What If You…?" + a number. 2nd-person present narration, short sentences; ~860 words, ~¼ dialogue, 10ish voices. 12 beats: the wish in minute one, plus/minus, the big hit at the halfway point, the twist before the end, a callback, a cliffhanger, a CTA.
- `script.md` with `[Name] line` and `[beat Ns]` → `tools/md2json.py` → `tools/vs_cast_gen.py` (VoiceStudio: narrator `mathomaly` at 0.9; characters = profiles cloned from voice-designed samples). Pauses SENT 0.85 / PARA 1.25 / CHAR 0.7 s, beats +1 s → ~1.7 words/s → 8:00+ from ~860 words.

## Sound (user-tuned on ten-seconds)
- **Music:** a light groove like the reference (measured 100–125 BPM, the tempo changes per section): `groove(t0, t1, chords, { bpm, lv })` in score.js — lv 0 pad · 1 + arpeggio · 2 + bass + hi-hat · 3 + kick + clap. Fast for montages (118–120, lv 3), slow for emotion (80–96, lv 0–1), heartbeat build into the big hit, silence for the twist.
- **SFX:** every action gets one (`SFX(t, kind, …)` per shot), but balanced: per-kind minimum gaps and one sound per 0.35 s (big ones exempt) → ~70 a minute. No bright "ting/ding" chimes (ding/coin are low marimba taps, max one per 12 s). In the mix SFX sit **under** the voice (≈ −6 dB), music −10 dB, both ducked by the voice.

## Production pattern (worked on ten-seconds)
head.html SHOT engine → sets.js (15 sets) + props.js (~35 props) → 8 section files built in parallel in `dev/<sec>` → full storyboard → fixes → code score (bed + 15–25 sfx/min, silence before the loudest hit) → export in chunks (frames are ~2.5 MB each; 12k frames will fill a disk).

## Frame checklist (on top of grammar/FRAME.md)
1. ≥ 3 depth layers; the far ones soft; background life (3+ details).
2. The face of whoever the shot is about is readable; nothing cut by the bars.
3. Feet on the floor line (GROUND 900 at d = 1); no sliding, no passing through furniture.
4. The picture shows the noun on its word; every spoken number on screen, landing at the end of its word.
5. Any grab or hold gets a hand close-up with an exact grip.
6. The ghost (cyan) on every use of the power, nowhere else.
7. Not the same picture three times in a row.

## Next (user notes after ten-seconds)
- **More 2D→3D, like the reference:** heads that sometimes read half-3D (sphere shading, a turn), sets with real perspective (floors, walls, objects with sides), camera moves that reveal depth.
- **Arms:** the rig bent every elbow with one sign (one arm looked flipped). Fixed: `armIK` in ivMan picks the natural bend (down first, then out facing camera / back in profile); rest poses hang straight. Check arms on every board (`pieces/ten-seconds/dev/armtest`).

## Not matched yet
- Back views (only a workaround in s08); fingertips in some hand inserts are simple capsules.
- Ghosts on far blurred layers read soft; draw important ghosts on the actors' layer.

## Proven on
`pieces/ten-seconds` — "What If You Could See 10 Seconds Into the Future?" (8:22, 239 shots, 11 voices).
`pieces/cats` — "What If You Could Understand Every Cat?" (8:31, 273 shots, 2.5D upgrade, cat rig).

## Thumbnails (from the channel's 14 thumbs, sheet in `thumbs/sheet.jpg`)
- 1280×720. Caption top-left, 2 short lines, Montserrat Black (`fonts/Montserrat-Black.ttf`), line 1 white, line 2 yellow `#ffc93c`, ends with a period ("TOO SLOW.", "CATCH ME.") — never repeats the title, it is what the hero would say.
- The hero's head BIG on the right half (≈ 55% of the height), cropped by the bottom, smug face: flat-lidded eyes, a four-point star in one eye, one-sided smirk. Warm glow behind the head, rim light.
- One glowing prop/opponent on the other side (bullet, IQ meter, the cat), an accent in red (tags "PART 2", a red word). Dark navy night, blurred bokeh background.
- Template: `pieces/cats-thumb` (scene + `ivPost` override that draws face, bubble and caption on top of the grade, `IV.bar = 0`). Copy it, change the scene.

## `styles/onebit/STYLE.md`

# Onebit

![sample](sample.png)

1-bit manga-horror pixel. Stark black and white with one flat mid grey (and a near-black for night), hard pixels, heavy black hair masses with fine strands, flat grey shadow planes with a hatched terminator, half-tone (50% Bayer) for wall tiles and ceilings, and white rims around dark silhouettes. Anatomical faces (cheekbones, nose planes, nostrils, lids and lashes, irises with a catchlight, eye bags, neck tendons, ears). Bathroom-type sets drawn flat but in one-point perspective. Hard cuts, nearly still shots, and typed subtitles in a bold white pixel font with a black outline over a dithered dark plate.

## Measured (from the references: edge-periodicity on stills + zoom crops)

- **Palette (4 steps):** ink `#000000`, night `#2b2b2b`, wall grey `#8e8e8e`, paper `#fdfdfd`. Indexes `K, DK, GR, WH`.
- **Pixel size:** the main character close-ups measure 8.05 px at 1080 (≈134x238); a wide shot of the same set measures 5.75 px (≈188x334); the bathroom reference is 2.25 px at 1280x720 (a 320-line picture). **Internal resolution: 180x320 (6 px pixels)** — it matches the finer reference shots and the 320-line bathroom reference and gives faces enough pixels for anatomy in mirror shots (face 40 px wide) while staying chunky. `obScene({ w: 135, h: 240 })` still gives the coarser 8 px look.
- **Subtitles:** cap 7 cells on a 5 px grid (35 px), vertical strokes 2 cells (10 px), 1-cell black outline plus a 1-cell drop shadow down-right, a 80%/40% dithered black plate; 2 lines max, typed at 0.045 s per glyph, no cursor.
- **Cuts:** hard cuts, one per 1.5–3.5 s; inside a shot only tiny motion on 2s (a blink, a turn, lips, a hand).

## Kit API (`kit.js`)

- `obScene(draw, { w, h, bg, cam, shake, map, light })`: low-res index buffer → upscale nearest-neighbour. `light: { amb, lights: [{ x, y, r0, r1, p }] }` darkens every non-emissive pixel by distance with Bayer dither (`v → floor(v·L + bayer)`); `amb: 0.12, lights: []` = lights out (only emissive rims/glints stay).
- `obMask(fill, fn, { thr, rim, rim8, rimDir, emit, rimEmit, noCam, noPre })`: the threshold pass; `rimDir` rims only the lit side; `emit` marks pixels the light pass must keep. Shorthands `obFill`, `obInk`, `obRect`, `obLine`, `obSpl` (smooth line), `obHatch`, `obGlow` (dithered emissive halo). Geometry: `obCR` (Catmull-Rom densify), `obAlong`, `obPoly`, `obPolyAdd`.
- Figures: `obPerson(x, y, s, { blink, stare, smile, look, shade, roll, shirt, glow, rimDir, shadowInk, noBody, key })` (y = eye line, s = half face width; `smile` → `obGrin`: uneven corners, gums, two rows of irregular teeth, lip edges, nasolabial folds and their shadow, bunched cheeks pushing tense lower lids, crow's feet), `obHand(x, y, s, { side: 'palm'|'back', mirror, flat, arm, armDx, glow })`, `obBackOfHead(x, y, s, { glow, rimDir })`, `obProfile(x, y, s, { blink })` (rim-lit foreground silhouette).
- Set: `obTiles(quad, nx, ny, { base, grout, stain, bevel })` (perspective tiles with stains, drips, cracks), `obRoomBox(frame, backWall)` (ceiling + side walls), `obLamp`, `obSink` (rim, bowl, drain, mixer tap, trap pipe), `obShelf(x, y, w, [[kind, x, h]])` (pump, round, jar, tall, cup with toothbrushes), `obTowel`, `obDoor(x, y, w, h, { open })`, `obMirror(x, y, w, h, inside, { frame, glints, wear, spots, glow })` (desilvering at the edges, water spots, a drip run).
- Text: `OB_FONT` (bold by 1-cell right dilation; advances trim empty body columns), `obSubtitle`, `obSub(lines, t0, { cx, y, plate })`, `obTypeCount`, `obTypeTimes`.

## Motion habits

- On 2s. Held shots; life is a blink (one boil), a slow push-in (<= 5%), a small head roll, a hand rising over 0.5–1 s.
- Things switch rather than fade: a lamp flickers (every 3rd boil off) and dies → the lights-out palette (silhouettes rimmed in white, eye glints, teeth).
- A shock is a hard cut plus 3 frames of whole-pixel shake.

## Frame checklist (on top of grammar/FRAME.md)

1. Only the 4 ramp colours; every edge a staircase of 6 px squares (subtitles on 5 px).
2. Big flat areas: white skin and shirts, black hair, flat grey shadow planes. Dither only for tiles, ceilings, glow and falloff; never over a whole face.
3. One light direction per shot: the shadow plane, nose plane, cast shadow under the nose and jaw all on the same side.
4. A dark mass (hair) against a lighter ground, with a white rim where it meets grey.
5. The set has 4+ props (tiles with grout and stains, sink and tap, shelf bottles, towel, door, lamp, mirror wear) but they stay line art on white so the face reads first.
6. Subtitle on its plate, 2 lines max, inside x 60-940 and above y 1500.
7. Dark scenes: near-black, dithered night forms, only emissive rims, glints and teeth bright.

## Do / don't

- Do draw with smooth canvas paths and let `obMask` snap them; give dark shapes a rim.
- Do keep faces mostly white: shading is one flat grey plane, a 1-px hatched terminator, and grey contour lines.
- Don't stack lines around the eyes (crease + bag + crow's feet + cheek contour reads as old or as goggles); with a grin drop the cheekbone line.
- Don't run the light pass with a small r0 on lit scenes: it turns everything into mid-grey mush. Use r0 ≥ 200 so only corners fall off.
- Don't name the source artists or games in output.

## Not matched yet

- The references' line weight varies more (tapered contours); ours is a constant 1 px except lids and brows.
- The bathroom reference's shading is screen-tone dots on clothes and skin too; ours keeps skin flat.
- Hands are still simple (capsule fingers); the references' hands are better.
- Reference video carries mild compression blur; ours is pixel-crisp (deliberate).

**Proven on:** `pieces/reflejo` (15 s, 6 shots, hard cuts, Spanish subtitles) — look and storyboard; export pending approval.

## `styles/pixdoc/STYLE.md`

# pixdoc — documentary pixel art

![sample](sample.png)

Short documentary explainers in fine pixel art: a full-bleed, richly detailed world drawn at 270×480 (4 px pixels on 1080×1920), ordered dithering instead of gradients, a navy subtitle bar that types itself on, small amber labels, gilded circular loupes that open on details, old-paper maps whose routes draw on, and a continuous 8-bit documentary score. Made from the user's "Ref posit pixel" references (kept local, never published). Built on the skill's `pixel` kit plus a doc layer at the end of `kit.js`.

**The bar:** *El primer hackeo* (`pieces/hackeo-1834`, approved 2026-10-12 after three rounds) is the **minimum** level of detail, motion and sound for every piece in this style. Each new piece should match it everywhere and beat it somewhere.

## Measured
- **Resolution:** world 270×480 (4 px), text 180×320 (6 px) so captions stay ≥ 42 px tall on a phone. The references measure ~2 px at 576 wide (≈3.75 px at 1080).
- **Palette (`DOC`):** bar `#050716` / ink `#010208`, caption `#eef0ea`, amber labels `#f0b23c`, sky `#4f78ab → #5f88b8 → #7ea2c8 → #aac2d8 → #e2dcc4`, paper `#f2e4c2 / #e3d1a8`, sea `#8fb0c4 / #7598b0`, grass `#678239 / #98a758 / #3f5a26`, field `#c9b16a`, stone `#d9cba6`, slate `#4a5468`, wood `#6a4426`, gold rim `#c8902e / #f2cc6a / #5a3812`. **One colour carries the story's meaning** (red = the fake symbol in hackeo-1834); don't spend it on decoration.
- **Captions:** a full-width navy bar at y ≈ 250, uppercase bitmap font with Spanish marks (Á É Í Ó Ú Ñ Ç Ü ¿ ¡ via NFD), ≤ 26 glyphs per line, typed at 30 glyphs/s (×k of the shot) with a tick sound, centred. Outlined text without a bar only for a lone line on black.
- **Labels:** amber with a 1-cell dark outline, pop in with two flickering boils and a blip. Stamps: a double red box slammed in at 2× for one boil.
- **Loupes:** circular insets (`docIris`) on a spring with a 3-ring gilded rim and a drop shadow; the world behind dims 35 %.
- **Cuts:** hard cuts on the 8th grid between beats; loupes, map zooms and route draw-ons carry the change inside a beat.

## Frame checklist (minimum, on top of grammar/FRAME.md)
1. **Depth:** landscapes have ≥ 4 layers (far ridge, ridge, middle, near) with haze getting lighter with distance, field strips in perspective (rows grow toward the camera), objects scaled by distance (towers 0.2 → 1.6). Every layer moves with the camera at its own depth (`pshift`, parallax 0.2 … 1).
2. **Camera life in every shot:** an idle float (`docFloat`) and/or a slow push-in or zoom; the opening is a steady zoom into the subject, as in the references. Maps push or zoom on springs (`viewAt`).
3. **Shadows everywhere:** cast shadows from buildings, towers, people, props, coins (`docShadow`, dithered parallelograms); ledge and cornice shadows under every overhang; interiors with a shaft of light (dither) and dust in it.
4. **Detail per set:** windows with frames, mullions and reflections; roofs with seams and dormers; wood with planks; stone and paper with static grain (`ptex`, keyed to position, never boiling); old maps with stains, darkened edges, a graticule.
5. **Maps are complete** edge to edge: every coast and neighbour that the view could show (land polygons run past the frame), light sea bands hugging each coast, paper grain on land only. Routes **draw on** (`routeDraw`: line + railway ticks + a pulsing head) and the stations light up as the head passes.
6. **3+ details of life per shot:** clouds, birds, smoke, river ripples and a barge, sheep, a clerk walking, pigeons hopping, tufts swaying on the beat, a ticking clock, candle flicker, blinking faces.
7. **People:** `docMan` for full figures (with a shadow), `docBust` for close-ups (eyes that blink and glance, brows, sideburns, hats or judges' caps, jabots). Identical twins stay identical.
8. **Action, not stills:** each beat has a visible process: arms that swing with a spring overshoot, a finger running down a page, a parcel travelling, coins piling, a counter ticking (DÍA 1…5, 1834…1836), a gavel that shakes the frame.
9. **Nothing rushes:** captions ≤ 3.5 words/s and each fully readable ≥ 1.5 s; short beats get stretched (shot speed k in `SHOT_LIST`) rather than cut. A 60–70 s piece is ~17 shots of 3–6 s.
10. **Safe area:** every caption, label and stamp inside x 60–940, y 250–1500. `textcheck` cannot read the bitmap font: check labels by eye on `review/phone.jpg`.

## Sound (minimum)
0. **All sound is code** (`src/score.js`): music and effects synthesized in the chiptune voice. No recorded SFX and no sound-layer mix/QA for this style (that toolkit in `sound-layer/` is for other styles).
1. **Music from the first frame.** Never open in silence.
2. **A continuous BED under the melody** (`bed()`): per bar a held 50 % pulse bass + a sine sub an octave down + three held 25 % pulse chord voices, + a beat "pump" in fuller sections. Spectrum check against the reference: continuous energy 20–200 Hz and held chord tones 200–700 Hz.
3. **One harmonic map** (`HAR`: [section start, progression]); bars count from each section's start so chord changes land where the section and the melody begin. Bed, arps, drums (backbeat relative to the section) and theme all read it.
4. **Everything musical on the grid:** the theme at rate 1 starting on a section's bar, harmonised so strong beats are chord tones; runs and shimmers on the 16th grid. No stretched melodies.
4b. **Every piece has its own music:** a new key, progressions, theme and groove pattern (hackeo-1834: D minor, held pulse bass; polvo-estrellas: E minor, bouncing octave bass, echoing 12.5 % lead). Reuse the machinery (`bed`/`HAR`/`groove`/`theme`), never the notes.
5. **Chiptune voice:** NES-like pulse waves 12.5 / 25 / 50 % (PeriodicWave), a triangle/pulse bass, noise hats/snare, a triangle kick; the theme on 50 % pulse with delayed vibrato. D minor documentary progression Dm–Bb–F–C was approved.
6. **Present sound effects for every visual event:** caption typing ticks, label pops (two-note square + click), big numbers (fast triad + thump), counters (ticks), stamps (sub + noise + low pulse), ERROR (a sour minor-second buzz), coins, hooves, wooden clacks with body, gavel, page turns and loupe sweeps, data chirps.
7. **Arc:** a 1 s hard silence before the turn, the loudest hit on the turn (a short stab + sub, then a flat chord), the busiest section quieter than the payoff, the ending ≥ 6 dB under the payoff. `review.mjs` story arc must pass 6/6.
8. **Deliver at about -15 LUFS, peak ≤ -1.5 dBFS** (ffmpeg loudnorm + limiter from `renders/audio.wav`).

## Timing machinery (copy from hackeo-1834's head)
`SHOT_LIST` rows `[t0, scene, title, o0, oDur, k]`: scenes, CAPS and cues are written in story time; `warp()` plays shot i from t0 at speed k (overlays included); `NT()` maps story time to video time for the score; `docCaptions()` shows only the CAPS of the current shot.

## Kit API (doc layer, `kit.js`)
`DOC`, `DOC_RES`, `DOC_TXT` · `docText(str, x, y, c, { count, align, outline, shadow, scale })`, `docTextW`, `docWrap`, `docChars` · `docCaption(str, t0, { y, max, cps, bar, pre, until })` · `docLabel(str, sx, sy, { at, until, fg, outline, align, scale })` · `docStamp(str, sx, sy, { at, fg, scale })` · `docIris(cx, cy, r, inner, { rim })`, `irisR(t0, r, t1)`, `pdiscPath` · `ptex`, `dhash`, `pbeam`, `pcloud` · `docMan(x, y, { flip, arm, walk, coat, coat2, hair, beard })`, `docBust(x, y, { coat, cap, jabot, hat, look, glasses, beard, talk, key })`, `docShadow(x, y, rx, ry, amt)` · `docFloat(seed, amp)`, `pshift(dx, dy, fn)`. Plus everything from the pixel kit (`lowres`, `pgrad`, `pdither`, `pglow`, `ppoly`, `pcircle`, `sprite`, `FONT5`…). Piece-side helpers worth copying: `sky`, `chappe`/`poseAt` (spring poses), `fields` (perspective strips), `mapWorld`/`routeDraw`/`viewAt`/`alongPts`, the score's `pul`/`hold`/`bed`/`groove`/`HAR`.

## Do / don't
- **Do** read each reference again before a piece: its opening move, its loupes, its sound bed.
- **Do** web-check every claim and say "illustrative" for invented numbers (prices, codebook words).
- **Don't** let text from the font run past 26 glyphs a line; don't use system fonts on screen.
- **Don't** animate with fades: things pop, flicker, step or spring.
- **Don't** publish or commit anything with reference pixels; don't name the reference's author.

## Not matched yet
The references' 3/4 roof framing in the opening; their slightly smaller caption type (ours is bigger on purpose for phones).

**Proven on:** `pieces/hackeo-1834` (70 s, approved).

## `styles/pov3d/STYLE.md`

# pov3d — "what if" POV in real 3D (three.js)

One fixed, high camera on a busy real-world place (a beach in the first piece); the world changes around it while a serif HUD counter on the left changes what it measures each act, and an italic serif caption sits in the lower third. Rendered with three.js r149 (inlined in `three.js`, global `THREE`) into an offscreen WebGL canvas, then drawn onto the 2D canvas under the 2D text overlay from `kit.js`. Motion on 1s.

**Proven on:** `pieces/sol-explota` (60s, "¿Qué pasaría si el Sol explotara?", approved by the user for quality). Start every new piece in this style from `template/` — it is that piece's full source.

**Current quality bar (2026-10-13): `pieces/oxigeno` (ES) + `pieces/oxygen-en` (EN), one shared `src/oxy.js` with an `OX_EN` flag.** Start new pieces from it; the full list of the user's standing rules is in the auto-memory note pov3d-style. Earlier bar: `template-ola/` (pieces/ola-700, the 65s tsunami). Its visuals and its sound design are the minimum for every new pov3d piece. Start from it, not from `template/`.

**Sound rule (2026-10-11): REAL RECORDINGS, NO MUSIC, NO SYNTH.** The user approved "option B": every ambience bed and every hit is a CC0 recording, never synthesized. Workflow and scripts: `pieces/luna/sound/` (gen.py → layers.json → bed.py → audio/bed.wav in the "voice" slot of `sound-layer/scripts/mix.py`, hits as cues from `sound-layer/kit`, then `qa.py`, `levels.py`). Find recordings with `sound-layer/scripts/sfx.py search` (Openverse, slow: run queries in parallel) and look at their spectrograms (`look.py`) before choosing. Trim hit tails so they die before planned silences; put a loud bed (water burst) under the hero hit so the mixer sizes it as the loudest moment. Write CREDITS.md and LISTEN.md per piece. The score.js synth score is no longer the sound. Still:
- ambience beds
- discrete events
- Doppler on moving sources
- wind and rumble
- reverb sends and ducking
- silence before the loudest hit, which lands on the impact
- −14 to −16 LUFS, true peak ≤ −1 dB

## How to start a new piece
1. Copy `template/piece.json` and `template/src/` into `pieces/<name>/`. Keep the `"build"` list in piece.json (it inserts `styles/pov3d/three.js` before the kit).
2. `src/scenes.js`: `g3()` builds the 3D world once (cached in `G`); `update3D(p)` poses everything from `TT` each frame and draws it with `ctx.drawImage`. Replace the world (beach → city, forest, ocean…) but keep the techniques below.
3. `src/head.html`: TIMELINE (acts, cues, board). `src/score.js`: the score.

## The quality bar (what the user approved)
- **Camera:** high and steep (fov ~50°, ~13 m up), horizon at ~48% of frame height; the subject fills the lower half; big foreground framing elements in the top corners (palm fronds).
- **Light:** low warm backlight (sun in frame, ~43% height), `VSMShadowMap` 4096 with `radius 5`, long soft shadows toward the camera; ACES tone mapping on meshes; **the sky shader skips tone mapping** so the cream/lavender gradient stays warm (top `#c3bfe6`, horizon `#fde2bd`).
- **Colour management:** `THREE.ColorManagement.legacyMode = false` — hex colours are sRGB. Without it everything washes out.
- **Water:** custom shader — turquoise shallows → blue → hazy far, five rolling foam bands, shoreline foam, sun glitter, sky reflection.
- **Land:** displaced geometry with code-drawn rock textures (vertical streaks, crevices), vertex-colour vegetation, instanced trees; sand with grain texture and colour variation; haze with distance.
- **People:** ~300 instanced smooth bodies (capsules) in swimwear: skin, trunks/bikini, arms, hair, varied heights/widths/kids; poses: lying, sitting, standing groups, walking, swimmers waist-deep; all from seeded RNG.
- **Props galore:** lifeguard tower, pier on piles, boats, buoys, umbrellas (2-colour panels), towels, chairs, coolers, boards, sandcastle, volleyball net, kites with bow tails, gulls, a small plane.
- **Effects:** additive flame sprites, smoke/steam sprites with `depthTest = false` + `renderOrder = 10` (otherwise transparent water cuts them into hard-edged smudges), plasma sphere with code texture, fog shifting colour per act.
- **Text:** `pvTitle` (two lines, top third), `pvHud(label, value, sub)` (left, y≈800–914), `pvCaption` (y≈1390) — each sits on a **feathered dark ellipse** (`pvFeather`). Keep captions short (≤ ~32 chars) to stay out of the phone UI's right edge.

## Frame checklist
- Opening frame reads like a postcard: busy, warm, foreground framing, horizon ~48%.
- Title / counter / caption never overlap a bright kite or the sun; feather under every text.
- No hard-edged dark shapes (sprite cut by water) — check stills across every act.
- Loudest sound on the turn (the flash), ≥0.5s silence before it.

## Performance
~1.3–2 s per frame in headless Chromium (software WebGL); a 60s piece exports in ~45 min. Build stills often with `--scale 0.4`.

## Not matched yet
Palm fronds are thinner than the reference's broad leaves.
