  # The Ship of Theseus — brief
  
  - **Format:** 9:16, 1080×1920, 24fps, ~66s, voice-led (English). F2 fixed stage (the sea), no hard cuts.
  - **Style:** `bitpix` (new, from `Ref bit y pixels/`): navy ground #0b1014, faint grid, crisp vector shapes with dark seams; yellow #e2bd1c = original matter, mint #00e992 = new matter, magenta #e50673 = the question. Serif (Georgia) for captions, mono for data labels. Motion on 1s with springs.
  - **Device:** the planks turn mint one by one; both ships burst into the dots of a person whose cells turn over; the word "same" splits into matter and story; the ship returns with the person as its reflection. Signature "Bitstory" at the end.
  - **Voice:** script in `voice/script.json` (rewritten in English from reference 5, reworded). Scratch OS voice for timing; final voice = Algrow "Mad 3" (blocked: account on the Starter plan, TTS needs Professional).
  - **Sound:** documentary score composed in code (`src/score.js`: D minor piano arpeggios, pads, a pulse in the Hobbes act, 1.9s silence, chord stab + sub on the hit, D major after). Effects = real CC0 recordings from `sound-layer/kit`, placed from `window.SFX_CUES` by `sound-layer/scripts/mix.py` (cue sheet `sound/cues.json`).
  
  ## Beats
  | # | t | beat | bridge |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | 0–11.6 | one plank rots and is swapped, then all 38 (counter) | old planks fly off top-right |
  | 2 | 11.6–19.5 | Athens, 30-oared galley, repairs over the centuries, Plutarch: same / not the same | — |
  | 3 | 19.5–33.4 | 1655 Hobbes: the old planks fly back in and build a second ship; two labels | — |
  | 4 | 33.4–36.65 | "Which one…?" then silence | the hit: flash + ring |
  | 5 | 36.65–44.5 | planks burst into a dot person; cells turn mint, day 0→90 | push-in on the head |
  | 6 | 44.5–51.3 | almost: the cortex stays yellow, circled | dots rise into the word |
  | 7 | 51.3–59.4 | "same" → same matter (yellow ship) / same story (mint ship); pulled apart | the two merge |
  | 8 | 59.4–66.1 | the ship again; its reflection is the person; "You were never the planks." + Bitstory | — |
  
  ## Claims and sources
  - Athenians kept Theseus's thirty-oared galley, replacing rotten timbers; philosophers argued over it — Plutarch, *Life of Theseus* 23: https://lexundria.com/plut_thes/23/prr
  - Hobbes's version (old planks reassembled), *De Corpore*, 1655 — https://www.britannica.com/print/article/2195856
  - ~330 billion cells replaced per day; the body's total in ~80–100 days — Sender & Milo, Nature Medicine 2021: https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/our-bodies-replace-billions-of-cells-every-day/ , https://wis-wander.weizmann.ac.il/node/11205
  - Neocortical neurons are as old as the person (no detectable adult neurogenesis) — Bhardwaj et al., PNAS 2006: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16901981/
  - "c. 300 BC" = the ship kept until Demetrius of Phalerum (regent 317–307 BC); "Plutarch · c. 100 AD" = date of writing (approximate).

  # cartoon3d — guiones: cómo escriben las 11 refs
  
  Transcripciones: `Ref 3D cartoon animations/_analisis/guiones/<n>.txt` (faster-whisper large-v3).
  
  ## Medidas
  - 112–243 palabras (mediana ~165), 31–65 s, ~215–225 palabras/min, voz casi sin pausas.
  - 9 de 11 usan **"You see,"** para abrir la explicación final (las otras: "Well, picture…", "That's because…").
  
  ## Estructura (siempre la misma)
  1. **Gancho = una contradicción o una acción absurda en la primera frase**, sin contexto previo.
     "Gambling is illegal in Japan, yet there's a gambling hall on almost every street." / "A man snuck into a family's house every night and moved every single thing one inch to the left." / "If you fall asleep holding two steel balls, you might wake up a genius."
  2. **Historia contada como escena**, en presente o pasado narrativo, con un protagonista concreto: "you" (te mete adentro: casino, Japón, pachinko) o "he / a man / a scientist" (cuento con giro).
  3. **Escalada en pasos cortos**: "Then, one night, a ball dropped. Then another. Then all eight at once." / "Five minutes go by, then ten…".
  4. **Un personaje secundario con una línea de diálogo burlona**: "Bro, it's just warming up." / "Hey, it's the toy guy. Did your frogs get hungry again?" / "So, someone broke in to move your furniture an inch?"
  5. **Giro / revelación** (la escena cambia de sentido): el comprador es él; el cliente era un agente; la ventana no es parte del local.
  6. **"You see," + el mecanismo real explicado simple**, con una analogía física y cotidiana (el ascensor de 19 pisos, la lista de paradas del rodillo).
  7. **Remate corto que cierra el gancho** (callback): "And that's how he ended the war." / "so you wake up holding the idea instead of the balls." / "Because nobody can do nothing forever." / "and on paper, nobody gambled."
  
  ## Voz y lenguaje
  - Inglés oral, frases cortas, conectores "So," "But," "Then," "Now," al inicio de casi cada frase.
  - Coloquial: "way more", "pretty sure", "literal garbage", "a fancy word for", "at least in his head", "statistically a little suspicious".
  - Humor seco por contraste (la reacción del mundo vs. lo que de verdad pasa).
  - Pocos números, redondos y dichos como se hablan; cada número es visual (un objeto en pantalla).
  - Nada de introducciones ("Today we'll learn…"), nada de cierre tipo "like and subscribe".
  
  ## Tipo de historia (usuario, 2026-10-23)
  La mayoría de las refs (2, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11) NO son "en 1902…": son escenas atemporales en presente — te pone a ti en una situación cotidiana (casino, ascensor, hotel) o cuenta "un tipo hizo X" como cuento — y el giro es un truco, sistema o mecanismo oculto. Solo 1, 3 y 4 son historia con época, y aun así sin fechas. Mezcla: la MAYORÍA escenas creativas sin años; las historias de época con fechas siguen valiendo, pero en minoría (no se descartan).
  
  ## Duración (usuario, 2026-10-23)
  Cada video dura **61 s** → guion de ~215–225 palabras (ritmo de las refs ~215 wpm). Alargar con más escena, escalada y diálogo, nunca con relleno: misma intensidad o más.

  # cartoon3d — "3D cartoon shorts"
  
  Flat-drawn cartoon people (white ball head, bean body, ink-brown stick limbs, thick brown outline, Flow-drawn face decals that swap on a blink) inside dense, glossy, warmly lit 3D sets. Second-person true stories, one clause = one shot, a camera that never stops. 9:16, 30 fps, motion on 1s.
  
  **Goal (user, 2026-10-22):** replicate the 7 references in `Ref 3D cartoon animations/` as closely as possible. When the tutorial (fuentes/3d-cartoon-animations/) and the references disagree, the references win (e.g. subtitles are ONE word at a time). No Creatorize.
  
  ## Pipeline (as the tutorial does it, minus Creatorize)
  1. **Refs measured** — `tools/analyze_refs.py` (frames at 30 fps, contact sheets, words, cuts/dissolves, camera) → `Ref 3D cartoon animations/_analisis/`.
  2. **People = 2D cut-outs from Google Flow, living in the 3D set** (refs, user 2026-10-22). Every layer is generated in Flow with crops of the refs uploaded as references (`_analisis/flowref/`, Flow assets `ref_head_*`, `ref_body_teal`, `ref_char_full`, `faces_master`): the bare glowing head, 43 faces + blink frames (sheets copied from the ref faces), hairstyles with the lilac gloss, bean torsos with clothes, mustache/beard/glasses, emotion symbols. `sprites/sheets.json` + `tools/slice_sprites.py` key the green out → `sprites/png/` (`face_*` cell-centred, others trimmed). Copy into a piece as `assets/face_*.png` and `assets/spr_<name>.png`. Use Nano Banana 2 when Pro hits its usage limit; the srz Flow MCP needed a patch (tile names are in aria-label now).
  3. **Sets in code** (three.js r149): props and sets (`c3Prop` PBR + `c3RBox` rounded boxes + ink hulls + room env reflections + VSM soft shadows, `c3Chrome` platinum metal), effects. Characters: `c3Person` billboards (face the camera, 2D IK limbs as ink strokes, contact shadow, subtle idle breathing/sway seen in the refs).
  4. **Voice** — `tools/trim_voice.py voz.mp3 pieces/<name>/voice`: sentence pauses → 0.20 s (max ~0.3), inner pauses ≤ 0.12 s, breaths removed, cuts only in silence; words.json for sync. Refs: ~219 wpm, voice 93–99 % of the runtime.

  DOCUMENT (ifverse/ANALISIS.md):
  # Ifverse (@IfverseTales) — análisis de estilo
  
  Material en `Ref ifverse/` (mp4 720p de los 3 más vistos, thumbnails, info.json, subtítulos de los 9 videos en `subs/` y texto plano en `txt/`, contact sheets en `frames/`).
  
  ## Datos del canal (23-oct-2026)
  Canal nuevo, 9 videos, todos subidos en octubre 2026, todos con título **"What If …?"**
  
  | Vistas | Video | Dur |
  |---|---|---|
  | **4.4M** | What If Your Reaction Time Was 10x Faster? (7-oct) | 7:13 |
  | **1.2M** | What If You Had 500 IQ? (14-oct) | 8:56 |
  | 631K | What If One Second Felt Like Ten? (parte 2 de reflejos) | 6:47 |
  | 446K | What If You Used 500 IQ to Disappear? (parte 2 IQ) | 8:36 |
  | 359K | What If One Second Felt Like Forever? (parte 3) | 9:05 |
  | 319K | What If You Woke Up in Kindergarten With All Your Memories? | 5:48 |
  | 208K | What If You Used 500 IQ to Save Your Sister? (parte 3 IQ) | 11:40 |
  | 116K | What If You Were Trapped in a Time Loop? | 8:15 |
  | 15K | What If You Were a Mentalist? | 8:21 |
  
  Lo que funcionó: **un superpoder cuantificable con número** (10x, 500 IQ). Los éxitos se convierten en trilogía; las secuelas caen ~50% cada parte.
  
  ## Visual
  - **Personajes**: stickman negro puro, cabeza = círculo grande, extremidades = trazos gruesos redondeados. **Rim light naranja/dorado** (contorno de luz cálida) que los separa del fondo. Ojos = dos óvalos blancos/crema + boca de una línea; expresiones por forma de ceja/ojo (ojos en "U" feliz, círculos con pupila = sorpresa, cejas en V = concentración).
  - **Identidad por ropa de un color**: protagonista con **hoodie rojo** (reflejos) o **hoodie azul** (500 IQ); amigo con gorra amarilla; científico con bata blanca y lentes; árbitro a rayas. El resto son siluetas grises/negras.
  - **Fondos**: vector plano con profundidad — ventanas iluminadas, skyline, estadio con multitud de stickmen, cuartos con detalles (posters, lámpara). Paleta de **atardecer violeta-naranja** (reflejos) o **gris-azulado frío de oficina/noche** (IQ). Desenfoque de profundidad (fondo blur), viñeta, grano suave, bokeh.
  - **Encuadre cine**: letterbox negro arriba/abajo (~2.35:1 dentro de 16:9). Mucha variedad de planos: cenital (mesa del café), contrapicado, primerísimo primer plano de la cara llenando pantalla, gran plano general del estadio, POV de cámara TV con REC/timecode.

  # ifverse — "What If…?" stickman stories
  
  Long-form (≥ 8 min) 16:9 YouTube stories in the manner of @IfverseTales, all in code. Analysis of the source and the full spec: `ANALISIS.md`. First piece (the proof): `pieces/ten-seconds`.
  
  ## The look
  - **Flat cards at real depth, filmed by a camera** (`ivStage(layers)`): each layer is drawn flat and placed at a depth d (1 = the actors' plane, 2–6 far, 0.5–0.7 foreground). Far layers pan 1/d as much, zoom 1+(z−1)/d and go soft with depth of field (`IV.dof`); blurred layers render at half resolution.
  - **Film:** mood tint, vignette, black cinema bars (62 px at 1080). **No grain** (`IV.grain = 0`; the user saw it and the reference is clean). `ivPost()` is `STYLE.post`.
  - **Stick people** (`ivMan`): black round head (R = 0.125 h), black limbs (0.034 h), one-colour clothes (hoodie, jacket, suit, uniform, cardigan, coat, vest, tee), cream eyes and mouth, a **warm rim light** from the mood's key (a silhouette pass nudged toward the light). Hair/hats: puffs, bun, pony, tuft, buscap, cap; glasses.
  - **Faces:** eyes open / happy / wide (pupil) / squint / angry / sad / tired / dots / closed; brows angry / sad / up; mouths smile / grin / flat / o / frown / open / smirk; the speaker's mouth follows its VOICE words (`talk: id`); the narrator has no mouth. **Blink every 3.5–4 s, 3 frames.**
  - **Hands change with shot size:** nub (wide) → mitten (medium) → five-finger glove (close-up); grips open / fist / point / hold / flat; `hold: { R|L|front|back: (x, y, ang, h) => prop }`.
  - **Moods (`IV_MOOD`):** sunset, lunch, day, night, rain, lamp, office (+ arcade, party, hall, school from the sets). One mood per scene.
  - **The ghost** (`ivGhost(fn, a)`): anything drawn in fn becomes a cyan hologram (luminance recoloured cyan, glow, 1-px jitter). Cyan = the device (the future) and the running counter only.
  - **Type:** rounded bold caps (`IV.font`), cream with a warm glow (`ivTitle`, `ivTag`, `ivText`); `ivCounter` bottom-centre.
  
  ## Motion (measured from the source + the guide)
  - **Motion on 1s** (`STYLE.ones = true`), no motion blur. Gestures 4–6 frames with a hard stop (`ivPoseMix` + `EZ.o3`). Walks: `ivWalk` (5 frames a step, planted feet).
  - **Camera almost still:** close-ups never move; ~⅓ of wides get `ivPush(t0, 0.03, 1.8)` and stop. No shake (one 6-frame jolt allowed on the biggest hit).
  - **Cuts:** hard cuts only, 3 frames before the word (`CUT(id, word)`); ~25–29 shots a minute; a shot under 0.45 s is dropped (main.js).
  
  ## Story and voice
  - Title "What If You…?" + a number. 2nd-person present narration, short sentences; ~860 words, ~¼ dialogue, 10ish voices. 12 beats: the wish in minute one, plus/minus, the big hit at the halfway point, the twist before the end, a callback, a cliffhanger, a CTA.

  # Onebit
  
  ![sample](sample.png)
  
  1-bit manga-horror pixel. Stark black and white with one flat mid grey (and a near-black for night), hard pixels, heavy black hair masses with fine strands, flat grey shadow planes with a hatched terminator, half-tone (50% Bayer) for wall tiles and ceilings, and white rims around dark silhouettes. Anatomical faces (cheekbones, nose planes, nostrils, lids and lashes, irises with a catchlight, eye bags, neck tendons, ears). Bathroom-type sets drawn flat but in one-point perspective. Hard cuts, nearly still shots, and typed subtitles in a bold white pixel font with a black outline over a dithered dark plate.
  
  ## Measured (from the references: edge-periodicity on stills + zoom crops)
  
  - **Palette (4 steps):** ink `#000000`, night `#2b2b2b`, wall grey `#8e8e8e`, paper `#fdfdfd`. Indexes `K, DK, GR, WH`.
  - **Pixel size:** the main character close-ups measure 8.05 px at 1080 (≈134x238); a wide shot of the same set measures 5.75 px (≈188x334); the bathroom reference is 2.25 px at 1280x720 (a 320-line picture). **Internal resolution: 180x320 (6 px pixels)** — it matches the finer reference shots and the 320-line bathroom reference and gives faces enough pixels for anatomy in mirror shots (face 40 px wide) while staying chunky. `obScene({ w: 135, h: 240 })` still gives the coarser 8 px look.
  - **Subtitles:** cap 7 cells on a 5 px grid (35 px), vertical strokes 2 cells (10 px), 1-cell black outline plus a 1-cell drop shadow down-right, a 80%/40% dithered black plate; 2 lines max, typed at 0.045 s per glyph, no cursor.
  - **Cuts:** hard cuts, one per 1.5–3.5 s; inside a shot only tiny motion on 2s (a blink, a turn, lips, a hand).
  
  ## Kit API (`kit.js`)
  
  - `obScene(draw, { w, h, bg, cam, shake, map, light })`: low-res index buffer → upscale nearest-neighbour. `light: { amb, lights: [{ x, y, r0, r1, p }] }` darkens every non-emissive pixel by distance with Bayer dither (`v → floor(v·L + bayer)`); `amb: 0.12, lights: []` = lights out (only emissive rims/glints stay).
  - `obMask(fill, fn, { thr, rim, rim8, rimDir, emit, rimEmit, noCam, noPre })`: the threshold pass; `rimDir` rims only the lit side; `emit` marks pixels the light pass must keep. Shorthands `obFill`, `obInk`, `obRect`, `obLine`, `obSpl` (smooth line), `obHatch`, `obGlow` (dithered emissive halo). Geometry: `obCR` (Catmull-Rom densify), `obAlong`, `obPoly`, `obPolyAdd`.
  - Figures: `obPerson(x, y, s, { blink, stare, smile, look, shade, roll, shirt, glow, rimDir, shadowInk, noBody, key })` (y = eye line, s = half face width; `smile` → `obGrin`: uneven corners, gums, two rows of irregular teeth, lip edges, nasolabial folds and their shadow, bunched cheeks pushing tense lower lids, crow's feet), `obHand(x, y, s, { side: 'palm'|'back', mirror, flat, arm, armDx, glow })`, `obBackOfHead(x, y, s, { glow, rimDir })`, `obProfile(x, y, s, { blink })` (rim-lit foreground silhouette).
  - Set: `obTiles(quad, nx, ny, { base, grout, stain, bevel })` (perspective tiles with stains, drips, cracks), `obRoomBox(frame, backWall)` (ceiling + side walls), `obLamp`, `obSink` (rim, bowl, drain, mixer tap, trap pipe), `obShelf(x, y, w, [[ki […recortado]

  # pov3d — "what if" POV in real 3D (three.js)
  
  One fixed, high camera on a busy real-world place (a beach in the first piece); the world changes around it while a serif HUD counter on the left changes what it measures each act, and an italic serif caption sits in the lower third.   **Proven on:** `pieces/sol-explota` (60s, "¿Qué pasaría si el Sol explotara?", approved by the user for quality). Start every new piece in this style from `template/` — it is that piece's full source.

  # luna — ¿Qué pasaría si la Luna chocara contra la Tierra?
  
  ## Spec
  - 9:16, 1080×1920, 24 fps, 70.0 s (1680 frames). Spanish on-screen text. Style **pov3d** (three.js r149), started from `styles/pov3d/template-ola` (ola-700), new world.
  - Format **F5, fixed place**: a handheld camera floating ~40 m up over the rooftops of a coastal town at night. A main street runs down to a promenade and quay; a harbour with moored boats; a jetty with a red/white lighthouse and a sweeping beam; a wooded headland with house lights on the left; a far headland on the right; the open sea. At the end the camera drifts back 18 m and tilts up 26° at the wave (58.5–62.95 s).
  - Reference: `Ref Lunar Animation/What if the moon crashed into earth.mp4` (80 s). Stills, spectrogram and the comparison sheet are in `references/lunar/` (moon_*.png). Same kind of scene, own layout.
  
  ## Beats
  | # | time | picture | HUD | caption |

  # scroll3d — "how it works" 3D explainer, remade from a reference
  
  A voice-led explainer in a simple clay-like 3D world on a near-black warm background: dioramas, mannequins, toy props, and the data drawn *inside* the scene (ghost frames, block lattices, arcs, cube columns, voxel fields), with karaoke captions and bold sans labels. Rendered with three.js r149 (`styles/pov3d/three.js`, global `THREE`) into an offscreen WebGL canvas, drawn onto the 2D canvas under the 2D overlay from `kit.js`. Motion on 1s, 30 fps.
  
  **Proven on:** `pieces/compresion` (98.7 s, a Spanish remake of `Ref Scroll aniamtions/4.mp4`, video compression). Start the next piece from its `src/` (head.html with the `ANCH` time map, world.js, shots.js).
  
  ## What a scroll3d piece is (the user's rule, 2026-10-16)
  - Each piece remakes ONE reference from `Ref Scroll aniamtions/` (1 Shazam, 2 AirTag, 3 Maps traffic, 4 video compression, 5 Face ID).
  - **Same shots and camera moves**, same duration rhythm; the text paraphrased into Spanish; some elements changed (character, props, colours, wall, decor) so it is not a copy.
  - I write the Spanish script (one line per English line, fitted to its time slot, "…" for pauses); the user generates the voice and drops it in `Ref Scroll aniamtions/voces/`.
  
  ## How to build one
  1. Transcribe the reference with word times (faster-whisper on CPU: `WhisperModel(..., device="cpu")`; feed PCM from ffmpeg, not the file). Contact sheets at 1 and 2 fps; `ffmpeg select='gt(scene,0.25)'` for the cuts.
  2. Write the script; after the take arrives, transcribe it (language "es", model "medium"), align words to the script lines (`voice/align.py`) → `voice.json`; pad the take with a 1.2 s tail → `voice/voice.wav`.
  3. `ANCH` in the head: [reference time, Spanish time] pairs at line starts/ends and at the words both voices share (the words a cut or a move lands on). `refT(TT)` maps the Spanish clock to reference time; author every shot in reference time R with `camKeys(R, [[R, pos, target, fov], ...])`. Then camera moves land on the same words as in the reference.
  4. Keep everything above the caption (y 1438 ± 44): frames and props sit between ~0.08 H and ~0.70 H.
  
  ## The look (what the user approved)
  - Background `#0c0a08`, a dark floor with a warm radial pool under the subject. No tone mapping (`NoToneMapping`), `ColorManagement.legacyMode = false`, hemisphere 0.95 + one warm key with PCF soft shadows + a faint cool rim.
  - Clay materials (MeshStandard, roughness ~0.85), code-drawn textures with relief: plaster mottling, wood planks, knit chevrons, painting, rug.
  - One yellow (`#f2b632`) = "what changed", one cyan (`#3fd0d6`) = "motion / instruction"; white tags with black text for names ("Fotograma clave").
  - Text: **Helvetica FreeSans Bold** for everything (`assets/FreeSans.ttf`, copied from `fonts/Helvetica FreeSansBold.ttf`; the build embeds it as a FontFace). Captions 54 px in a dark rounded box at y 1438; spoken words white, the rest grey; chunks ≤ 21 characters.
  - Small grey notes for honesty ("esquemático: …", the arithmetic under a number).

  # tapestry
  
  An embroidered linen tapestry in the Bayeux manner, like the Game of Thrones / House of the Dragon tapestries (refs: `Ref amphora mitologia/house of the dragon*`). **The style for every House of the Dragon and Game of Thrones video** (user, 2026-10-20). Start new pieces by copying `pieces/rhaenyra`.
  Proven on: `pieces/rhaenyra` (60.5s, 12 panels, approved 2026-10-20).
  
  ## The look
  - **Linen:** `#d7cab6`, a tabby weave with visible threads, slubs and soft folds (`tpLinen`, tiled; it scrolls with the strip).
  - **Embroidery:** every shape is laid work (`tpFill`): parallel threads in three shades, a sheen, couching ties, and a dark stem-stitch outline (`#291817`). Lines are stem stitch (`tpStem`).
  - **Borders:** top band y 58–268 and bottom band y 1652–1862 (the user asked for them close to the edges, but not touching). Each has two stitched rules, diagonal striped bars, and an emblem per compartment (`tpBand`).
  - **Lettering:** stitched capitals in Herculanum. Words alternate red and navy, and keywords take their side's colour (`tpCaption`, `tpText`). Captions sit at the top of each panel and slide with the cloth.
  - **Figures** (`tpFigure`): a long gown, a surcoat with dotted borders, a belt with a buckle, a cloak with a clasp, sleeves with cuffs, hands with fingers. The 3/4 face has eye whites, irises, lids, heavy brows, a nose, rosy cheeks and stitched hair.
    - **Red lips only on women; men take `male: true`** (the user's rule).
  - **Props:** a dragon along an S spine (`tpDragon`: scales, belly plates, spines, finger-boned wings, horns, a jaw, rider, fire). The Iron Throne is a chair of swords (`tpThrone`/`tpSword`). Also castles, banners, clouds as scallops, rain, lightning, waves, flames, and Bayeux trees as panel dividers.
  - **Wiggle:** the same turbulence displacement as amphora, every 3 frames.
  
  ## Motion and structure
  - One long strip: panel i sits at world x = i·W, and **each scene change is a 0.8s slide to the right**, never a cut (`stripPos`).
  - Panels are drawn in local units and scaled by `PZ` 1.12 into the band, with feet at y 1600.
  - Figures sway and nod, dragons flap and undulate, and the words stitch in as they are spoken.
  
  ## Sound
  - An English take cut at word gaps.
  - Music is the theme the user supplies per piece (Rhaenyra: "House Of The Dragon - Rhaenyra Targaryen Theme.mp3" always from 0:30), loudnorm'd to −14, with music gain +10 and voice.music −1 (the user wants the bgm with strong presence), and a 0.5s dip before the payoff.
  - SFX in code: cloth slides, bells, roars, wings, thunder, fire.
  
  ## Checklist
  1. The borders are intact, and the caption is inside the band.
  2. Every figure has face detail and clothing layers, and men have no red lips.
  3. Dragons read as dragons (neck, wings with fingers, tail), and the throne reads as swords.
  4. Transitions are slides to the right only.
  
  ## Approved details (keep)
  - Captions at y 470 (top of the band, close to the drawings).
  - The end card: the apple at y 720, AMPHORUS just below at y 1040, 80px gold capitals with a shine (`tpLogo`), no stitch dots.
  - Pose changes (kneel → stand) are blended over ~0.9s, never jumpe […recortado]

  # yokai — dithered folk horror (three.js)
  
  A first-person folk tale told in on-screen paragraphs over a low-res 3D world, cold and foggy, pushed through a fixed palette with ordered dither. Made from `Ref earlobe horror/` (reel 5 the main reference).
  
  **Quality bar (2026-10-25, approved by the user): `pieces/behemoth`** (before it, pieces/jorogumo). Its full source is in `template/` (src, piece.json, brief, the card print, sound/mix.py). Start every new yokai piece from `template/` and go further from there — this level is the minimum.
  
  ## The look (measured, then pushed by the user's notes)
  - **Pixels:** three.js renders at `YK.LW × YK.LH` = 216×384 (5 px pixel at 1080), no antialias, blown up with no smoothing.
  - **Palette:** `YK.PAL.main` — blue-blacks, teals, cold greys, a few warm browns and rusts, no mid greens or oranges. Keep the warm browns: going full cyan was rejected.
  - **Grade before quantising** (`ykBlit`): saturation 0.6, cold grade `[0.9, 0.97, 1.0]` + lift `[1, 5, 7]`, gain 0.9, Bayer 4×4 spread 34 — gradients and fog read as dot screens.
  - **Cel shading:** every MeshStandardMaterial becomes MeshToon with a 3-band gradient (45 / 135 / 255).
  - **Fog:** dense in every light preset (night / day / dusk / dawn, all cool teal; dusk is teal, not orange).
  - **Detail:** code textures on everything (gravel, basalt, bark, needles, kasuri, robe, creature stripes), tens of thousands of wind-swayed grass blades, layered trees, props that tell the place (shrine, rope, lanterns, firewood, hat), mist sprites, spray, motes, falling leaves, birds.
  - **Text:** the code pixel font (`ykPara`): centred paragraph at y≈1300, u = 6 px, outlined; decodes glyph by glyph from noise and scrambles out. No badge in the top left.
  - **Card** (`ykCard`): stars on black, a striped beige frame, a legend-style print (generated with Flow / Nano Banana Pro as an Edo woodblock print, `assets/print.jpg`) drawn ~132 px wide through `YK.PAL.print` so it reads very pixelated, the name and a red seal.
  - **Transitions:** dithered fades (`vis`) and hard cuts; a planned black + exact silence before the reveal.
  
  ## The opening shot is the hook (user, 2026-10-22)
  The first 0–4 s decide whether people stay, so the creature must read clearly in the opening shot, as it does in every reference. Keep it dark and keep the same mood, but:
  - frame the creature as the subject: big in frame (≥ 35% of the height), in the upper half above the paragraph, from a good angle (a low angle or a silhouette against a lighter sky or fog);
  - separate it from the ground: rim or back light, a lighter fog layer behind it, and a tonal gap between the creature and the background;
  - show its defining wrong feature in that shot (legs, neck, face), not just a vague shape.
  Jorōgumo's opening (her shape lost in the mist behind the falls) is too hard to read. Do better than it.
  
  How the reference account does it (7 hooks studied, 2026-10-24, `references/tiktok/earlobehuman/`):
  - The creature is in frame from frame 0, centred in the upper half, filling 30–60% of the width, and the paragraph sits below it.
  - It is the brightest or the most saturated thing in t […recortado]

  # jorogumo — brief
  
  ## Spec
  - 9:16, 1080×1920, 24 fps, 75 s, English on-screen text (no voice). Style **yokai** (new, from `Ref earlobe horror/`): three.js at 216×384, toon shading in 3 bands, a sparse teal palette with 4×4 Bayer dither, cold grade, heavy fog; pixel font decoding glyph by glyph.
  - First-person folk tale: the grandson tells of his grandfather, the Jōren falls (Izu) and the jorōgumo. Card: a generated Edo-style print, heavily pixelated, "Jorōgumo" + red seal.
  
  ## Beats
  | # | time | picture | paragraph |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | 0–4.5 | night; her shape on the brink, a thread glints | the oath |
  | 2 | 4.5–9 | card (print, name, seal) | (same) |
  | 3 | 9–18 | the pool; he sleeps on the bank, axe and firewood by him | he dozed off |
  | 4 | 18–27 | threads round his legs up into the mist; he sits up | he woke |
  | 5 | 27–36 | he chops them free, ties them to a stump, backs away | the stump |
  | 6 | 36–45 | the stump tears out, dragged into the pool; black, 0.6 s silence | dragged down |
  | 7 | 45.6–56 | the reveal: the woman on the falls, eight legs | the woman |
  | 8 | 56–66 | the mask smiles, splits into eight eyes and fangs; he runs | "clever boy" |
  | 9 | 66–75 | dawn, tourists photograph the falls, one thread glints | today |
  
  ## Claims + sources
  - Jōren Falls (Izu, Shizuoka) is tied to the jorōgumo; the thread-tied-to-a-stump tale — Wikipedia "Jorōgumo"; yokai.jp (densho).
  - "Clever" (kashikoi) comes from the Kashikobuchi (Sendai) variant — yokai.jp.
  - The first-person frame and the merged versions are fiction, as in the reference.

## Texto completo de las skills propias más usadas

### `.claude/skills/ver-youtube/SKILL.md`

---
name: ver-youtube
description: Mira uno o más videos de YouTube con Claude por API (créditos mensuales del plan Max, no tokens del plan) bajándolos con yt-dlp, transcribiendo con Whisper local y analizando fotogramas, y guarda notas de aprendizaje en español en fuentes/[tema]/[titulo-del-video].md, con pasos y minutos, lo que se ve en pantalla, consejos y dudas. # ver-youtube

Convierte videos de YouTube en notas de aprendizaje. El script baja el video, lo transcribe en local y le manda a Claude (API, con los créditos de $200/mes del plan Max) los fotogramas con timestamp + la transcripción. Así no se gastan tokens del plan de Claude Code: yo solo leo el `.md` final.

## Entrada
- Uno o más links de YouTube (públicos o no listados; yt-dlp no baja privados).
- Un tema. Si el usuario no lo dice, deducilo de su pedido o preguntá en una línea; define la carpeta `fuentes/<tema>/` y orienta las notas.

## Antes de correr
1. Requisitos: `yt-dlp`, `ffmpeg`, `node` en PATH; Python con `anthropic`, `faster-whisper` y `numpy`. Si falta algo, explicale al usuario qué se instala y para qué antes de instalarlo.
2. La clave sale de `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` en el `.env` del proyecto (el script la busca desde la carpeta actual hacia arriba). Nunca la muestres ni la copies a otros archivos, y nunca la pongas como variable de entorno de Windows. Si da error de autenticación, la clave venció (dura 30 días): pedile al usuario una nueva de platform.claude.com → Claves y acceso.

## Ejecutar
Desde la raíz del proyecto (las notas quedan en `./fuentes/`):

```
python .claude/skills/ver-youtube/scripts/ver_youtube.py --tema "<tema>" <url1> <url2> ...
```

Opciones: `--force` rehace notas ya existentes (por defecto las saltea), `--model` cambia el modelo (default `claude-sonnet-5-5`; `claude-haiku-5-5` es más barato para videos largos).

Por cada video: lee título y canal (oEmbed), baja el video ≤720p, transcribe con Whisper `small` en CPU, saca hasta 60 fotogramas repartidos en el video y pide las notas a Claude. Imprime los tokens usados (un short de ~2 min ≈ 29k de entrada, unos $0.13 con Sonnet). Un video que falla no frena a los demás.

## Formato de las notas
Secciones: **De qué trata**, **Pasos / método** (con [MM:SS] cada uno), **Lo que se ve en pantalla** (herramientas, configuraciones, ejemplos), **Consejos y advertencias**, **Lo que no queda claro**. Son notas para aprender, no transcripción.

## Después
Revisá cada `.md` sin leerlo entero (por ejemplo `grep "^## "` para ver que estén las cinco secciones y los timestamps). Si una nota sale floja, rehacela con `--force`. Al usuario respondele con la lista de archivos creados (rutas) y una línea por video; no pegues las notas enteras.

---
name: real-sfx
